CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulliWeightdefinition

def bernoulliWeight (p : ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The probability of the assignment a when each unit is independently treated with probability p: ∏_i (p if a i else 1 - p).

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulliDesigndefinition

def bernoulliDesign (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) : Design ι

The Bernoulli design with treatment probability p, 0 ≤ p ≤ 1: every assignment is in the support and has probability bernoulliWeight p.

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulliDesign_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem bernoulliDesign_inclusionProb (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (i : ι) :
  (bernoulliDesign p hp0 hp1).inclusionProb i = p

Under the Bernoulli design every unit is treated with probability p.

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulliDesign_prob_patterntheorem

theorem bernoulliDesign_prob_pattern (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (s : Finset ι)
  (b : ι → Bool) :
  (bernoulliDesign p hp0 hp1).prob (fun a => ∀ i ∈ s, a i = b i) =
    ∏ i ∈ s, if b i then p else 1 - p

The finite-pattern product law. Under the Bernoulli design, for any finite set s of units and any target pattern b, the probability that every unit of s receives its target treatment is ∏_{i ∈ s} (p if b i else 1 - p): the coin flips are independent.

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulliDesign_pairInclusionProbtheorem

theorem bernoulliDesign_pairInclusionProb (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) {i j : ι}
  (hij : i ≠ j) : (bernoulliDesign p hp0 hp1).pairInclusionProb i j = p * p

Under the Bernoulli design two distinct units are both treated with probability p * p.

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulli_htEstimator_unbiasedtheorem

theorem bernoulli_htEstimator_unbiased [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (p : ℝ)
  (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) :
  (bernoulliDesign p hp0.le hp1.le).expect (po.htEstimator p) = po.ate

Unbiasedness under the Bernoulli design. In a nonempty population, if each unit is treated independently with probability p, 0 < p < 1, then the Horvitz-Thompson estimator (1/N) Σ_i (A_i Y_i / p - (1 - A_i) Y_i / (1 - p)) is unbiased for the average treatment effect.

CausalInference.Randomized.bernoulli_htEstimator_variancetheorem

theorem bernoulli_htEstimator_variance [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p)
  (hp1 : p < 1) :
  (bernoulliDesign p hp0.le hp1.le).variance (po.htEstimator p) =
    ((Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹) ^ 2 *
      ∑ i, p * (1 - p) * (po.y1 i / p + po.y0 i / (1 - p)) ^ 2

Variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator under the Bernoulli design. In a nonempty population, if each unit is treated independently with probability p, 0 < p < 1, the variance of the estimator over the design is N⁻² Σ_i p (1 - p) (y1 i / p + y0 i / (1 - p))^2.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Complete

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Complete.lean · 302 lines · 15 public theorems · 5 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.FinitePopulation

Complete randomization. Exactly n1 of the N units are treated, and the treated set is drawn uniformly among the N choose n1 possibilities. We compute the first and second order inclusion probabilities by a symmetry argument and show that the difference in means is unbiased for the finite-population average treatment effect. Source: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences.

Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015)

Public declarations (20)

CausalInference.Randomized.numTreateddefinition

def numTreated (a : ι → Bool) : ℕ

The number of units treated by the assignment a.

CausalInference.Randomized.numTreated_eq_sumtheorem

theorem numTreated_eq_sum (a : ι → Bool) : (numTreated a : ℝ) = ∑ i, treatInd a i

The number of treated units, as a real number, is the sum of the treatment indicators.

CausalInference.Randomized.numTreated_comp_permtheorem

theorem numTreated_comp_perm (a : ι → Bool) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) :
  numTreated (a ∘ σ) = numTreated a

Permuting the units does not change the number of treated units.

CausalInference.Randomized.completeSupportdefinition

def completeSupport (n1 : ℕ) : Finset (ι → Bool)

The support of complete randomization: the assignments treating exactly n1 units.

CausalInference.Randomized.mem_completeSupporttheorem

theorem mem_completeSupport {n1 : ℕ} {a : ι → Bool} :
  a ∈ completeSupport n1 ↔ numTreated a = n1

CausalInference.Randomized.card_completeSupporttheorem

theorem card_completeSupport (n1 : ℕ) :
  #(completeSupport (ι := ι) n1) = (Fintype.card ι).choose n1

The assignments treating exactly n1 units correspond to the n1-element subsets of the population, so there are N choose n1 of them.

CausalInference.Randomized.completeSupport_nonemptytheorem

theorem completeSupport_nonempty {n1 : ℕ} (h : n1 ≤ Fintype.card ι) :
  (completeSupport (ι := ι) n1).Nonempty

CausalInference.Randomized.completeDesigndefinition

def completeDesign (n1 : ℕ) (h : n1 ≤ Fintype.card ι) : Design ι

Complete randomization: the uniform design on the assignments treating exactly n1 of the N units, for n1 ≤ N.

CausalInference.Randomized.completeDesign_expect_comp_permtheorem

theorem completeDesign_expect_comp_perm (n1 : ℕ) (h : n1 ≤ Fintype.card ι)
  (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (completeDesign n1 h).expect (fun a => f (a ∘ σ)) = (completeDesign n1 h).expect f

Complete randomization is invariant under relabeling the units: the expectation of a ↦ f (a ∘ σ) equals that of f for every permutation σ.

CausalInference.Randomized.completeDesign_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem completeDesign_inclusionProb (n1 : ℕ) (h : n1 ≤ Fintype.card ι)
  (hN : 0 < Fintype.card ι) (i : ι) :
  (completeDesign n1 h).inclusionProb i = n1 / Fintype.card ι

Under complete randomization every unit is treated with probability n1 / N.

CausalInference.Randomized.completeDesign_pairInclusionProbtheorem

theorem completeDesign_pairInclusionProb (n1 : ℕ) (h : n1 ≤ Fintype.card ι)
  (hN : 1 < Fintype.card ι) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :
  (completeDesign n1 h).pairInclusionProb i j =
    n1 * (n1 - 1) / (Fintype.card ι * (Fintype.card ι - 1))

Under complete randomization two distinct units are both treated with probability n1 (n1 - 1) / (N (N - 1)).

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansdefinition

def PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeans (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (n1 n0 : ℕ)
  (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The fixed-denominator difference in means (1/n1) Σ_i A_i Y_i - (1/n0) Σ_i (1 - A_i) Y_i, with the counts n1 and n0 supplied from outside. It is the difference between the average observed outcomes of the treated and the control units only for assignments that treat exactly n1 units, with n1 + n0 = N (see diffInMeansObs_eq_diffInMeans); for other assignments it is a different statistic. The observed statistic computed from the realized arm counts is PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansObs.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeans_eq_htEstimatortheorem

theorem PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeans_eq_htEstimator (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) {n1 n0 : ℕ}
  (hn : n1 + n0 = Fintype.card ι) (hn1 : 0 < n1) (hn0 : 0 < n0) (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.diffInMeans n1 n0 a = po.htEstimator (n1 / Fintype.card ι) a

A fixed-denominator identity: with n1 + n0 = N and both positive, the fixed-denominator expression diffInMeans n1 n0 coincides, for every assignment, with the Horvitz-Thompson estimator using the treatment probability n1 / N. For an assignment that does not treat exactly n1 units neither side is the observed difference in means.

CausalInference.Randomized.complete_diffInMeans_unbiasedtheorem

theorem complete_diffInMeans_unbiased (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) {n1 n0 : ℕ}
  (hn : n1 + n0 = Fintype.card ι) (hn1 : 0 < n1) (hn0 : 0 < n0) :
  (completeDesign n1 (by omega)).expect (po.diffInMeans n1 n0) = po.ate

Unbiasedness of the difference in means under complete randomization. If exactly n1 of the N = n1 + n0 units are treated, uniformly at random, with n1, n0 > 0, then the difference in means is unbiased for the finite-population average treatment effect.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansObsdefinition

def PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansObs (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (a : ι → Bool) :
  ℝ

The observed difference in means: the average observed outcome among the units actually treated by a minus that among the units actually left as controls, with the realized arm counts numTreated a and N - numTreated a as denominators. It is a difference of arm means when both arms are nonempty, which holds on the support of complete randomization with 0 < n1 < N.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansObs_eq_diffInMeanstheorem

theorem PotentialOutcomes.diffInMeansObs_eq_diffInMeans (po : PotentialOutcomes ι)
  {n1 n0 : ℕ} (hn : n1 + n0 = Fintype.card ι) {a : ι → Bool}
  (ha : a ∈ completeSupport n1) : po.diffInMeansObs a = po.diffInMeans n1 n0 a

On the support of complete randomization with n1 treated, n1 + n0 = N, the observed difference in means equals the fixed-denominator expression diffInMeans n1 n0.

CausalInference.Randomized.complete_diffInMeansObs_unbiasedtheorem

theorem complete_diffInMeansObs_unbiased (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) {n1 n0 : ℕ}
  (hn : n1 + n0 = Fintype.card ι) (hn1 : 0 < n1) (hn0 : 0 < n0) :
  (completeDesign n1 (by omega)).expect po.diffInMeansObs = po.ate

Unbiasedness of the observed difference in means under complete randomization. If exactly n1 of the N = n1 + n0 units are treated, uniformly at random, with n1, n0 > 0, then the observed difference in means is unbiased for the finite-population average treatment effect.

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.inclusionProb_permtheorem

theorem Design.inclusionProb_perm (d : Design ι) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι)
  (hσ : ∀ f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ, d.expect (fun a => f (a ∘ σ)) = d.expect f) (i : ι) :
  d.inclusionProb (σ i) = d.inclusionProb i

For a design invariant under the relabeling σ of the units, the unit σ i is treated with the same probability as i.

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.pairInclusionProb_permtheorem

theorem Design.pairInclusionProb_perm (d : Design ι) (σ : Equiv.Perm ι)
  (hσ : ∀ f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ, d.expect (fun a => f (a ∘ σ)) = d.expect f) (i j : ι) :
  d.pairInclusionProb (σ i) (σ j) = d.pairInclusionProb i j

For a design invariant under the relabeling σ of the units, the pair (σ i, σ j) is treated jointly with the same probability as (i, j).

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.inclusionProb_of_perm_invarianttheorem

theorem Design.inclusionProb_of_perm_invariant (d : Design ι) (m : ℕ)
  (hσ : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ),
    d.expect (fun a => f (a ∘ σ)) = d.expect f)
  (hsupp : ∀ a ∈ d.support, numTreated a = m) (i : ι) :
  d.inclusionProb i = m / Fintype.card ι

Inclusion probabilities of an exchangeable design. If a design is invariant under every relabeling of the units and every assignment in its support treats exactly m units, then every unit is treated with probability m / N.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.FinitePopulation

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/FinitePopulation.lean · 458 lines · 36 public theorems · 20 definitions

Finite populations, assignments, and randomized designs. The design-based (randomization) framework of Neyman (1923) and Fisher (1935), as presented in Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences. A finite population ι carries fixed potential outcomes y1 y0 : ι → ℝ; the only randomness is in the treatment assignment a : ι → Bool.

Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Fisher (1935); Imbens and Rubin (2015)

Public declarations (56)

CausalInference.Randomized.popMeandefinition

def popMean (f : ι → ℝ) : ℝ

The finite-population mean (1/N) Σ_i f i of a vector f over the units. It is a mean only for a nonempty population, 0 < N; for N = 0 Lean's convention 0⁻¹ = 0 returns 0, and every result interpreting popMean as a mean assumes 0 < N (or Nonempty ι).

CausalInference.Randomized.popVardefinition

def popVar (f : ι → ℝ) : ℝ

The finite-population variance (1/(N - 1)) Σ_i (f i - f̄)^2, with Neyman's N - 1 denominator. It is meaningful only for 1 < N; for N = 1 Lean's convention 0⁻¹ = 0 returns 0, and every result interpreting popVar as a variance assumes 1 < N.

CausalInference.Randomized.popVar_nonnegtheorem

theorem popVar_nonneg (f : ι → ℝ) (hN : 1 < Fintype.card ι) : 0 ≤ popVar f

The finite-population variance is nonnegative when the population has at least two units.

  popVar f = 0

A constant vector has zero finite-population variance (in a population of at least two units, where the variance is defined).

The population mean is additive.

CausalInference.Randomized.popMean_subtheorem

The population mean commutes with subtraction.

CausalInference.Randomized.popMean_consttheorem

theorem popMean_const [Nonempty ι] (c : ℝ) : popMean (fun _ : ι => c) = c

The population mean of a constant vector is that constant (in a nonempty population).

CausalInference.Randomized.popMean_smultheorem

CausalInference.Randomized.Designstructure

structure Design (ι : Type*)

A randomized design: a finite set of assignments with nonnegative weights summing to one. The set support is the summation set of every expectation; an assignment outside it is never drawn. The weight of an assignment in support is its probability of being drawn; the value of weight outside support carries no meaning (use Design.mass for the probability of an arbitrary assignment). Assignments in support may have weight zero.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimatorGendefinition

def htEstimatorGen (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (π : ι → ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The Horvitz-Thompson estimator of the average treatment effect with unit-specific inclusion probabilities π i: (1/N) Σ_i (A_i Y_i / π_i - (1 - A_i) Y_i / (1 - π_i)), where A_i is the treatment indicator and Y_i the observed outcome.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimatordefinition

def htEstimator (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (p : ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The Horvitz-Thompson estimator of the average treatment effect for a design that treats every unit with probability p: (1/N) Σ_i (A_i Y_i / p - (1 - A_i) Y_i / (1 - p)), where A_i is the treatment indicator and Y_i the observed outcome.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimator_eq_htEstimatorGentheorem

theorem htEstimator_eq_htEstimatorGen (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (p : ℝ) :
  po.htEstimator p = po.htEstimatorGen (fun _ => p)

The constant-probability estimator is the general one with π i = p for every unit.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimatorGen_eqtheorem

theorem htEstimatorGen_eq (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (π : ι → ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.htEstimatorGen π a = (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    ∑ i, (treatInd a i * po.y1 i / π i - (1 - treatInd a i) * po.y0 i / (1 - π i))

The general Horvitz-Thompson estimator rewritten with potential outcomes.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimator_eqtheorem

theorem htEstimator_eq (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (p : ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.htEstimator p a = (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ *
    ∑ i, (treatInd a i * po.y1 i / p - (1 - treatInd a i) * po.y0 i / (1 - p))

The Horvitz-Thompson estimator rewritten with potential outcomes: the treatment indicator selects y1 and its complement selects y0.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimatorGen_unbiasedtheorem

theorem htEstimatorGen_unbiased [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (d : Design ι)
  (π : ι → ℝ) (hπ0 : ∀ i, 0 < π i) (hπ1 : ∀ i, π i < 1)
  (hπ : ∀ i, d.inclusionProb i = π i) :
  d.expect (po.htEstimatorGen π) = po.ate

Unbiasedness of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator, unit-specific probabilities. In a nonempty population, if a design treats unit i with probability π i, 0 < π i < 1, then the expectation of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator with weights π equals the finite-population average treatment effect.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimator_unbiasedtheorem

theorem htEstimator_unbiased [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (d : Design ι) (p : ℝ)
  (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hπ : ∀ i, d.inclusionProb i = p) :
  d.expect (po.htEstimator p) = po.ate

Unbiasedness of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator. In a nonempty population, if a design treats every unit with the same probability p, 0 < p < 1, then the expectation of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator over the design equals the finite-population average treatment effect. This is the constant case of htEstimatorGen_unbiased.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Fisher

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Fisher.lean · 236 lines · 11 public theorems · 7 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.FinitePopulation

Fisher randomization tests under the sharp null. Fisher's sharp null hypothesis states that treatment has no effect on any unit: y1 i = y0 i for all i. Under it the observed outcome vector is the same for every assignment, so the value a test statistic would take under any other assignment can be computed from the observed data, and the randomization distribution of the statistic is known exactly. The randomization p-value p(a) = P_{a'}(T(a') ≥ T(a)) is then valid: P(p ≤ α) ≤ α for every α ≥ 0. The same holds for the general sharp null y1 i = y0 i + τ i after imputing the missing outcomes, and inverting the tests of constant additive effects gives a confidence set with coverage at least 1 - α. Sources: Fisher (1935), The Design of Experiments; Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences.

Sources: Fisher (1935); Imbens and Rubin (2015)

  (T : (ι → Bool) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (a a' : ι → Bool) :
  T a' (po.observed a') = T a' (po.observed a)

Under the sharp null the value of a test statistic T under any assignment a', which depends on the outcomes observed under a', equals the value imputed from the outcomes observed under the realized assignment a. Hence the randomization distribution of T is known from the observed data.

Validity of the Fisher randomization test. Under Fisher's sharp null, for any design and any test statistic T, the randomization p-value computed from the observed data, p(a) = P_{a'}(T a' Y(a) ≥ T a Y(a)) with Y(a) the outcomes observed under a, satisfies P(p ≤ α) ≤ α for every α ≥ 0.

Validity of the Fisher randomization test, uniform design. Under Fisher's sharp null, for the uniform design on a finite nonempty set S of assignments and any test statistic T, the p-value p(a) = #{a' ∈ S | T a' Y(a) ≥ T a Y(a)} / #S satisfies #{a ∈ S | p(a) ≤ α} / #S ≤ α for every α ≥ 0.

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.constEffectConfSetdefinition

def Design.constEffectConfSet (d : Design ι) (T : (ι → Bool) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ)
  (α : ℝ) (y : ι → ℝ) (a : ι → Bool) : Set ℝ

The confidence set for a constant additive effect obtained by inverting Fisher tests: the values c for which the sharp null y1 = y0 + c is not rejected at level α, that is, whose randomization p-value exceeds α.

CausalInference.Randomized.constEffectConfSet_coveragetheorem

theorem constEffectConfSet_coverage (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) {c : ℝ}
  (hc : po.SharpNullAt fun _ => c) (d : Design ι) (T : (ι → Bool) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) {α : ℝ}
  (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
  1 - α ≤ d.prob (fun a => c ∈ d.constEffectConfSet T α (po.observed a) a)

Coverage of the test-inversion confidence set. If the treatment effect is constant, y1 i = y0 i + c for every unit, then for any design, any test statistic, and any α ≥ 0, the confidence set obtained by inverting Fisher tests contains c with probability at least 1 - α. Membership in the set is decided classically.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Neyman

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Neyman.lean · 521 lines · 25 public theorems · 5 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.Complete

Neyman's variance formula for complete randomization. For the difference in means τ̂ under complete randomization with n1 treated and n0 control units out of N = n1 + n0, Neyman (1923) showed Var(τ̂) = S1²/n1 + S0²/n0 - S_τ²/N, where S1², S0², S_τ² are the finite-population variances (with denominator N - 1) of the treated potential outcomes, the control potential outcomes, and the unit-level effects. Consequently the conservative variance S1²/n1 + S0²/n0 is an upper bound, attained exactly when the unit-level effects are constant. The within-arm sample variances s1², s0² are unbiased for S1², S0², so the observable estimator V̂ = s1²/n1 + s0²/n0 is conservative with bias exactly S_τ²/N. All variances with denominator N - 1 are used only where 1 < N, which follows from n1, n0 > 0. Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences.

Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015)

CausalInference.Randomized.sum_sum_ite_eqtheorem

theorem sum_sum_ite_eq [DecidableEq ι] (A B : ℝ) (w : ι → ℝ) :
  ∑ i, ∑ j, (if i = j then A else B) * w i * w j =
    (A - B) * ∑ i, w i ^ 2 + B * (∑ i, w i) ^ 2

A double sum whose coefficient depends only on whether the indices agree: Σ_i Σ_j (A if i = j else B) w_i w_j = (A - B) Σ_i w_i^2 + B (Σ_i w_i)^2.

  ∑ i, B i * (y i - m⁻¹ * ∑ j, B j * y j) ^ 2 =

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.expect_armSampleVartheorem

theorem Design.expect_armSampleVar (d : Design ι) (B : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (m : ℕ) (y : ι → ℝ) (hB : ∀ a i, B a i * B a i = B a i)
  (hsum : ∀ a ∈ d.support, ∑ i, B a i = m)
  (h1 : ∀ i, d.expect (fun a => B a i) = m / Fintype.card ι)
  (h2 : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → d.expect (fun a => B a i * B a j) =
    m * (m - 1) / (Fintype.card ι * (Fintype.card ι - 1)))
  (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmN : m ≤ Fintype.card ι) :
  d.expect (fun a => armSampleVar (B a) m y) = popVar y

Unbiasedness of a within-arm sample variance. Let B a be an arm indicator vector (entries 0 or 1) that has exactly m ones for every assignment of the support, with first moments E[B_i] = m / N and, for i ≠ j, second moments E[B_i B_j] = m (m - 1) / (N (N - 1)). If 2 ≤ m ≤ N, the arm sample variance of a fixed vector y is unbiased for its finite-population variance.

Expectation of Neyman's variance estimator. Under complete randomization with n1 treated and n0 control units, n1 + n0 = N, 2 ≤ n1, 2 ≤ n0, the observable estimator V̂ = s1²/n1 + s0²/n0 has expectation S1²/n1 + S0²/n0.

CausalInference.Randomized.complete_neymanVarEst_biastheorem

theorem complete_neymanVarEst_bias [DecidableEq ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) {n1 n0 : ℕ}
  (hn : n1 + n0 = Fintype.card ι) (hn1 : 2 ≤ n1) (hn0 : 2 ≤ n0) :
  (completeDesign n1 (by omega)).expect po.neymanVarEst -
    (completeDesign n1 (by omega)).variance po.diffInMeansObs =
    po.varEffect / Fintype.card ι

Conservativeness of Neyman's variance estimator. Under complete randomization with n1 treated and n0 control units, n1 + n0 = N, 2 ≤ n1, 2 ≤ n0, the bias of the observable estimator V̂ = s1²/n1 + s0²/n0 for the variance of the observed difference in means is exactly S_τ²/N: E[V̂] - Var(τ̂) = S_τ²/N ≥ 0.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Cluster

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Cluster.lean · 313 lines · 19 public theorems · 7 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.Neyman, Designs.Randomized.Fisher

Cluster randomization. The units are partitioned into clusters by a map g : ι → κ, and m1 of the M clusters are drawn by complete randomization; every unit of a drawn cluster is treated. Treating clusters as units whose outcomes are the cluster totals reduces the analysis to complete randomization: the Horvitz-Thompson estimator built from the cluster totals is unbiased for the unit-level average treatment effect. A concrete example with clusters of unequal sizes shows that the plain difference in means of individual outcomes is biased. Sources: Middleton and Aronow (2015), Unbiased estimation of the average treatment effect in cluster-randomized experiments; Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences.

Sources: Imbens and Rubin (2015); Middleton and Aronow (2015)

Public declarations (26)

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterSupportdefinition

def clusterSupport (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) : Finset (ι → Bool)

The support of cluster randomization: the unit-level assignments b ∘ g obtained from an assignment b treating exactly m1 clusters, where g maps each unit to its cluster.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterDesigndefinition

def clusterDesign (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ) : Design ι

Cluster randomization: m1 of the M clusters are drawn by complete randomization and all units of the drawn clusters are treated. It is the push forward of complete randomization of the cluster labels under b ↦ b ∘ g: a unit-level assignment a has probability #{b | numTreated b = m1, b ∘ g = a} / (M choose m1), the number of cluster assignments that induce it over the number of cluster assignments. When some cluster label has no units, several cluster assignments induce the same unit-level assignment, and these multiplicities are kept.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterDesign_expecttheorem

theorem clusterDesign_expect (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ)
  (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 h).expect f = (completeDesign m1 h).expect fun b => f (b ∘ g)

An expectation under cluster randomization is the expectation under complete randomization of the clusters of the induced unit-level statistic. No assumption on the cluster map is needed: cluster labels without units are allowed.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterDesign_variancetheorem

theorem clusterDesign_variance (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ)
  (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 h).variance f = (completeDesign m1 h).variance fun b => f (b ∘ g)

The variance under cluster randomization is the variance under complete randomization of the clusters of the induced unit-level statistic.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterDesign_expect_eq_uniformtheorem

theorem clusterDesign_expect_eq_uniform {g : ι → κ} (hg : Function.Surjective g) (m1 : ℕ)
  (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ) (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 h).expect f =
    (Design.uniform (clusterSupport g m1) ((completeSupport_nonempty h).image _)).expect f

The uniform form under nonempty clusters. If every cluster is nonempty (g surjective), distinct cluster assignments induce distinct unit-level assignments, and cluster randomization is the uniform design on clusterSupport g m1. Without surjectivity the two laws differ (see emptyCluster_laws_differ).

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterDesign_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem clusterDesign_inclusionProb (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ) (i : ι) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 h).inclusionProb i = m1 / Fintype.card κ

Under cluster randomization every unit is treated with probability m1 / M.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.clusterTotalsdefinition

def PotentialOutcomes.clusterTotals (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (g : ι → κ) :
  PotentialOutcomes κ

The cluster-level potential outcomes: the totals T1 c = Σ_{i ∈ c} y1 i and T0 c = Σ_{i ∈ c} y0 i of the potential outcomes over each cluster c.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.htEstimator_comp_eqtheorem

theorem PotentialOutcomes.htEstimator_comp_eq [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (g : ι → κ)
  {m1 m0 : ℕ} (hm : m1 + m0 = Fintype.card κ) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hm0 : 0 < m0) (b : κ → Bool) :
  po.htEstimator (m1 / Fintype.card κ) (b ∘ g) =
    (Fintype.card κ : ℝ) / Fintype.card ι * (po.clusterTotals g).diffInMeans m1 m0 b

The cluster Horvitz-Thompson estimator as a cluster-level difference in means. For a cluster assignment b treating m1 of the M = m1 + m0 clusters, the unit-level Horvitz-Thompson estimator with treatment probability m1 / M evaluated at the induced unit assignment b ∘ g equals (M / N) times the difference in means of the cluster totals: (1/N) ((M/m1) Σ_c B_c T_c - (M/m0) Σ_c (1 - B_c) T_c), with T_c the observed cluster total. The population of units is assumed nonempty, so that N > 0.

CausalInference.Randomized.cluster_htEstimator_unbiasedtheorem

theorem cluster_htEstimator_unbiased [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (g : ι → κ)
  {m1 m0 : ℕ} (hm : m1 + m0 = Fintype.card κ) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hm0 : 0 < m0) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 (by omega)).expect (po.htEstimator (m1 / Fintype.card κ)) = po.ate

Unbiasedness under cluster randomization. In a nonempty population of units, if m1 of the M = m1 + m0 clusters are treated by complete randomization, m1, m0 > 0, then the Horvitz-Thompson estimator built from the cluster totals is unbiased for the unit-level average treatment effect. Cluster labels without units are allowed: such a cluster has totals zero. The proof treats clusters as units with outcome totals and applies the unbiasedness of the difference in means under complete randomization.

CausalInference.Randomized.Design.variance_const_multheorem

theorem Design.variance_const_mul (d : Design ι) (c : ℝ) (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  d.variance (fun a => c * f a) = c ^ 2 * d.variance f

Scaling a statistic by a constant c scales its variance by c².

CausalInference.Randomized.cluster_htEstimator_variancetheorem

theorem cluster_htEstimator_variance [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (g : ι → κ)
  {m1 m0 : ℕ} (hm : m1 + m0 = Fintype.card κ) (hm1 : 0 < m1) (hm0 : 0 < m0) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 (by omega)).variance (po.htEstimator (m1 / Fintype.card κ)) =
    ((Fintype.card κ : ℝ) / Fintype.card ι) ^ 2 *
      ((po.clusterTotals g).varTreated / m1 + (po.clusterTotals g).varControl / m0 -
        (po.clusterTotals g).varEffect / Fintype.card κ)

Exact variance under cluster randomization. In a nonempty population of units, if m1 of the M = m1 + m0 clusters are treated by complete randomization, m1, m0 > 0, then the variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator built from the cluster totals is (M / N)² (S_{T1}²/m1 + S_{T0}²/m0 - S_{T1 - T0}²/M), Neyman's formula applied to the cluster totals, with all three finite-population variances taken across the M clusters.

CausalInference.Randomized.cluster_fisher_pValue_validtheorem

theorem cluster_fisher_pValue_valid (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (hnull : po.SharpNull)
  (g : ι → κ) (m1 : ℕ) (h : m1 ≤ Fintype.card κ) (T : (ι → Bool) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ)
  {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
  (clusterDesign g m1 h).prob
    (fun a => (clusterDesign g m1 h).fisherPValue T (po.observed a) a ≤ α) ≤ α

Fisher's test under cluster randomization. Under the sharp null the Fisher randomization p-value computed with the cluster design is valid. No assumption on the cluster map is needed: the design carries the multiplicities of cluster assignments.

The plain difference in means of individual outcomes, with the realized (random) group sizes: (1/n1(a)) Σ_i A_i Y_i - (1/(N - n1(a))) Σ_i (1 - A_i) Y_i, where n1(a) is the number of treated units under a.

def clusterExampleMap : Fin 3 → Fin 2

Three units in two clusters of unequal sizes: unit 0 forms cluster 0, and units 1 and 2 form cluster 1.

def clusterExamplePO : PotentialOutcomes (Fin 3)

Potential outcomes of the example: y1 = (1, 0, 0) and y0 = (0, 0, 0), so only the unit of the small cluster responds to treatment.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExampleMap_surjectivetheorem

theorem clusterExampleMap_surjective : Function.Surjective clusterExampleMap

Every cluster of the example is nonempty.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExample_clusterSupporttheorem

theorem clusterExample_clusterSupport :
  clusterSupport clusterExampleMap 1 = {![true, false, false], ![false, true, true]}

Treating one of the two clusters yields exactly two unit-level assignments: treat unit 0 alone, or treat units 1 and 2.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExample_groups_nonemptytheorem

theorem clusterExample_groups_nonempty :
  ∀ a ∈ clusterSupport clusterExampleMap 1, 0 < numTreated a ∧ numTreated a < 3

In every assignment of the example both the treated and the control group are nonempty, so the bias below is not an artifact of dividing by zero.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExample_atetheorem

theorem clusterExample_ate : clusterExamplePO.ate = 1 / 3

The average treatment effect of the example is 1/3.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExample_expect_naiveDiffInMeanstheorem

theorem clusterExample_expect_naiveDiffInMeans :
  (clusterDesign clusterExampleMap 1 (by decide)).expect clusterExamplePO.naiveDiffInMeans =
    1 / 2

Under cluster randomization of the example (one of two clusters treated), the plain difference in means has expectation 1/2.

CausalInference.Randomized.clusterExample_naiveDiffInMeans_biasedtheorem

theorem clusterExample_naiveDiffInMeans_biased :
  (clusterDesign clusterExampleMap 1 (by decide)).expect clusterExamplePO.naiveDiffInMeans ≠
    clusterExamplePO.ate

Counterexample. With clusters of unequal sizes, the plain difference in means of individual outcomes is biased under cluster randomization: in the example its expectation is 1/2, while the average treatment effect is 1/3.

def emptyClusterMap : Fin 1 → Fin 3

One unit and three cluster labels, of which only the label 0 has a unit.

Drawing one of the three labels induces two unit-level assignments: treat the unit, or not.

CausalInference.Randomized.emptyCluster_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem emptyCluster_inclusionProb :
  (clusterDesign emptyClusterMap 1 (by decide)).inclusionProb 0 = 1 / 3

Under cluster randomization (one of three labels drawn) the unit is treated with probability 1/3.

CausalInference.Randomized.emptyCluster_uniform_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem emptyCluster_uniform_inclusionProb :
  (Design.uniform (clusterSupport emptyClusterMap 1)
    ((completeSupport_nonempty (by decide)).image _)).inclusionProb 0 = 1 / 2

CausalInference.Randomized.emptyCluster_laws_differtheorem

theorem emptyCluster_laws_differ :
  (clusterDesign emptyClusterMap 1 (by decide)).inclusionProb 0 ≠
    (Design.uniform (clusterSupport emptyClusterMap 1)
      ((completeSupport_nonempty (by decide)).image _)).inclusionProb 0

The two laws differ when a cluster label has no units. With one unit and three labels, one of which is drawn, cluster randomization and the uniform design on the induced unit-level assignments give the unit different treatment probabilities (1/3 and 1/2).

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Paired

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Paired.lean · 375 lines · 20 public theorems · 6 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.Stratified

Paired randomization. The units are grouped into J pairs by a stratum map s : ι → σ whose strata all have two units, and within every pair exactly one unit is treated, each with probability 1/2, independently across pairs: stratified randomization with one treated unit per stratum. The paired estimator is the mean of the within-pair differences D_k (treated minus control). We show that it is unbiased, compute its exact variance, and show that the usual variance estimator (the sample variance of the D_k divided by J) is conservative in expectation, with equality under a constant pair-level effect. Sources: Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences, chapter 10.

Sources: Imbens and Rubin (2015)

CausalInference.Randomized.pairedDesigndefinition

def pairedDesign (s : ι → σ) (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) : Design ι

Paired randomization: the strata are pairs (every stratum has exactly two units), and within every pair exactly one unit is treated, each with probability 1/2, independently across pairs. It is stratified randomization with one treated unit per stratum.

CausalInference.Randomized.pairedDesign_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem pairedDesign_inclusionProb (s : ι → σ) (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) (i : ι) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).inclusionProb i = 1 / 2

Under paired randomization every unit is treated with probability 1/2.

theorem pairedDesign_pairInclusionProb_of_ne (s : ι → σ) (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2)
  {i j : ι} (hij : s i ≠ s j) : (pairedDesign s hs).pairInclusionProb i j = 1 / 4

Under paired randomization two units of different pairs are both treated with probability 1/4.

CausalInference.Randomized.pairedDesign_expect_prodtheorem

theorem pairedDesign_expect_prod (s : ι → σ) (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2)
  (f : ∀ k, ({i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).expect (fun a => ∏ k, f k (stratumAssign s a k)) =
    ∏ k, (completeDesign 1 (by rw [card_stratum_subtype, hs k]; norm_num)).expect (f k)

Joint independence of the pair assignments. Under paired randomization, the expectation of a product ∏_k f_k (A|_k) of statistics each depending only on the assignment of one pair is the product of the expectations E_k[f_k], each computed under the design that treats one of the two units of the pair k uniformly at random.

CausalInference.Randomized.pairedDesign_expect_prod_eq_prod_expecttheorem

theorem pairedDesign_expect_prod_eq_prod_expect (s : ι → σ) (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2)
  (f : ∀ k, ({i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).expect (fun a => ∏ k, f k (stratumAssign s a k)) =
    ∏ k, (pairedDesign s hs).expect (fun a => f k (stratumAssign s a k))

Joint independence of the pair assignments, within the design. Under paired randomization, the expectation of a product of statistics each depending only on the assignment of one pair is the product of their expectations.

CausalInference.Randomized.card_eq_two_mul_of_pairstheorem

With J pairs of two units, the population has N = 2 J units.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairDiffdefinition

The within-pair difference of the pair k: the observed outcome of its treated unit minus that of its control unit, Σ_{i ∈ k} (A_i Y_i - (1 - A_i) Y_i).

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairedEstimatordefinition

The paired estimator: the mean (1/J) Σ_k D_k of the within-pair differences over the J pairs.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairEffectdefinition

def pairEffect (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) : ℝ

The average treatment effect τ_k = (1/2) Σ_{i ∈ k} (y1 i - y0 i) within the pair k.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairVardefinition

def pairVar (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) : ℝ

The randomization variance of the within-pair difference of the pair k, written with c i = y1 i + y0 i: (1/2) Σ_{i ∈ k} (c i - c̄_k)², with c̄_k the mean of c over the pair. For a pair {u, v} it equals (c u - c v)² / 4.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairedVarEstimatordefinition

def pairedVarEstimator (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (a : ι → Bool) :
  ℝ

The usual variance estimator for the paired estimator: the sample variance of the J within-pair differences divided by J, that is (1/(J (J - 1))) Σ_k (D_k - D̄)².

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairDiff_eqtheorem

theorem pairDiff_eq (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.pairDiff s k a = ∑ i ∈ stratum s k, (treatInd a i * (po.y1 i + po.y0 i) - po.y0 i)

The within-pair difference is affine in the treatment indicators: D_k = Σ_{i ∈ k} (A_i (y1 i + y0 i) - y0 i).

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.pairEffect_eqtheorem

theorem pairEffect_eq (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) :
  po.pairEffect s k = ∑ i ∈ stratum s k, (1 / 2 * (po.y1 i + po.y0 i) - po.y0 i)

The pair effect as a sum: τ_k = Σ_{i ∈ k} ((y1 i + y0 i) / 2 - y0 i).

  (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) (k : σ) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).expect (po.pairDiff s k) = po.pairEffect s k

Under paired randomization the within-pair difference of the pair k has mean τ_k.

CausalInference.Randomized.paired_variance_pairDifftheorem

  (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) (k : σ) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).variance (po.pairDiff s k) = po.pairVar s k

Under paired randomization the variance of the within-pair difference of the pair k is pairVar k; for the pair {u, v} this is ((y1 u + y0 u) - (y1 v + y0 v))² / 4.

CausalInference.Randomized.paired_expect_pairDiff_mul_of_netheorem

theorem paired_expect_pairDiff_mul_of_ne (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) {k l : σ} (hkl : k ≠ l) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).expect (fun a => po.pairDiff s k a * po.pairDiff s l a) =
    po.pairEffect s k * po.pairEffect s l

Under paired randomization the within-pair differences of distinct pairs are uncorrelated: E[D_k D_l] = τ_k τ_l for k ≠ l.

CausalInference.Randomized.paired_expect_pairDiff_multheorem

theorem paired_expect_pairDiff_mul (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  (hs : ∀ k, stratumSize s k = 2) (k l : σ) :
  (pairedDesign s hs).expect (fun a => po.pairDiff s k a * po.pairDiff s l a) =
    (if k = l then po.pairVar s k else 0) + po.pairEffect s k * po.pairEffect s l

The second moments of the within-pair differences under paired randomization: E[D_k D_l] = (pairVar k if k = l, else 0) + τ_k τ_l.

With J pairs the average treatment effect is the mean of the pair effects: τ = (1/J) Σ_k τ_k.

CausalInference.Designs.Randomized.Stratified

CausalInference/Designs/Randomized/Stratified.lean · 607 lines · 26 public theorems · 11 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.Neyman, Designs.Randomized.Fisher

Stratified (block) randomization. The units are partitioned into strata by a map s : ι → σ. Within every stratum k exactly n1 k of its N_k units are treated by complete randomization, independently across strata. We construct this design as the uniform design on the assignments with the prescribed number of treated units in every stratum, compute its inclusion probabilities by symmetry, and show that the stratified estimator Σ_k (N_k / N) τ̂_k is unbiased with variance Σ_k (N_k / N)² V_k, where V_k is Neyman's variance within the stratum k. Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences, chapter 9.

Sources: Neyman (1923, translated 1990); Imbens and Rubin (2015)

If no stratum is asked to treat more units than it has, some assignment treats exactly n1 k units of every stratum k.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesigndefinition

def stratifiedDesign (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ) (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) :
  Design ι

Stratified randomization: within every stratum k, exactly n1 k of its N_k units are treated, independently across strata. It is the uniform design on the assignments with the prescribed number of treated units in every stratum; independence across strata is proved in stratifiedDesign_expect_prod.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_expect_comp_permtheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_expect_comp_perm (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (e : Equiv.Perm ι) (he : ∀ i, s (e i) = s i)
  (f : (ι → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect (fun a => f (a ∘ e)) = (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect f

Stratified randomization is invariant under every permutation of the units that preserves the strata.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratum_swaptheorem

theorem stratum_swap {s : ι → σ} {i j : ι} (hij : s i = s j) (x : ι) :
  s (Equiv.swap i j x) = s x

Swapping two units of the same stratum preserves every unit's stratum.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_inclusionProbtheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_inclusionProb (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (i : ι) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).inclusionProb i = n1 (s i) / stratumSize s (s i)

Under stratified randomization a unit i is treated with probability n1 k / N_k, where k is its stratum.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_pairInclusionProb_of_eqtheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_pairInclusionProb_of_eq (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) (hs : s i = s j) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).pairInclusionProb i j =
    n1 (s i) * (n1 (s i) - 1) / (stratumSize s (s i) * (stratumSize s (s i) - 1))

Under stratified randomization two distinct units of the same stratum k are both treated with probability n1 k (n1 k - 1) / (N_k (N_k - 1)).

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_pairInclusionProb_of_netheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_pairInclusionProb_of_ne (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) {i j : ι} (hs : s i ≠ s j) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).pairInclusionProb i j =
    (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).inclusionProb i * (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).inclusionProb j

Under stratified randomization two units of different strata are treated independently: the probability that both are treated is the product of their inclusion probabilities.

CausalInference.Randomized.card_stratum_subtypetheorem

theorem card_stratum_subtype (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) :
  Fintype.card {i // s i = k} = stratumSize s k

The stratum k, viewed as a type, has N_k elements.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratumAssigndefinition

def stratumAssign (s : ι → σ) (a : ι → Bool) (k : σ) : {i // s i = k} → Bool

The assignment of the units of the stratum k induced by an assignment a of the whole population.

CausalInference.Randomized.numTreated_stratumAssigntheorem

theorem numTreated_stratumAssign (s : ι → σ) (a : ι → Bool) (k : σ) :
  numTreated (stratumAssign s a k) = numTreatedIn s k a

The number of treated units of the induced stratum assignment is the number of treated units of the stratum.

CausalInference.Randomized.sum_stratifiedSupporttheorem

theorem sum_stratifiedSupport (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (F : (∀ k, {i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  ∑ a ∈ stratifiedSupport s n1, F (stratumAssign s a) =
    ∑ x ∈ Fintype.piFinset fun k => completeSupport (ι := {i // s i = k}) (n1 k), F x

Sums over the stratified support are sums over the product of the complete-randomization supports of the strata: a ↦ (stratumAssign s a k)_k is a bijection between the two.

CausalInference.Randomized.card_stratifiedSupport_eq_prodtheorem

theorem card_stratifiedSupport_eq_prod (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ) :
  (#(stratifiedSupport s n1) : ℝ) =
    ∏ k, (#(completeSupport (ι := {i // s i = k}) (n1 k)) : ℝ)

The number of assignments of stratified randomization is the product over the strata of the numbers of assignments of complete randomization within each stratum, as a real number.

CausalInference.Randomized.card_stratifiedSupporttheorem

theorem card_stratifiedSupport (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ) :
  #(stratifiedSupport s n1) = ∏ k, (stratumSize s k).choose (n1 k)

The size of the stratified support. The number of assignments treating exactly n1 k units of every stratum k is ∏_k (N_k choose n1 k).

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_expect_prodtheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_expect_prod (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (f : ∀ k, ({i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect (fun a => ∏ k, f k (stratumAssign s a k)) =
    ∏ k, (completeDesign (n1 k) (by rw [card_stratum_subtype]; exact h k)).expect (f k)

Independence across strata. Under stratified randomization, the expectation of a product ∏_k f_k (A|_k) of statistics each depending only on the assignment of one stratum is the product of the expectations E_k[f_k], each computed under complete randomization of n1 k units within the stratum k.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_expect_stratumtheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_expect_stratum (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (k : σ) (g : ({i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect (fun a => g (stratumAssign s a k)) =
    (completeDesign (n1 k) (by rw [card_stratum_subtype]; exact h k)).expect g

The marginal law of one stratum. Under stratified randomization, a statistic depending only on the assignment of the stratum k has the expectation it has under complete randomization of n1 k units within that stratum.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_expect_prod_eq_prod_expecttheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_expect_prod_eq_prod_expect (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (f : ∀ k, ({i // s i = k} → Bool) → ℝ) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect (fun a => ∏ k, f k (stratumAssign s a k)) =
    ∏ k, (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).expect (fun a => f k (stratumAssign s a k))

Independence across strata, within the design. Under stratified randomization, the expectation of a product of statistics each depending only on the assignment of one stratum is the product of their expectations.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.stratumDiffInMeansdefinition

def stratumDiffInMeans (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) (n1 n0 : ℕ)
  (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The difference in means within the stratum k, with n1 treated and n0 control units there: (1/n1) Σ_{i ∈ k} A_i Y_i - (1/n0) Σ_{i ∈ k} (1 - A_i) Y_i.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.stratifiedEstimatordefinition

def stratifiedEstimator (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (n1 n0 : σ → ℕ)
  (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The stratified estimator Σ_k (N_k / N) τ̂_k, where τ̂_k is the difference in means within the stratum k, with n1 k treated and n0 k control units there.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.stratifiedWeightdefinition

def stratifiedWeight (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (n1 n0 : σ → ℕ)
  (i : ι) : ℝ

The coefficient of the treatment indicator of unit i in the stratified estimator: (N_k / N) (y1 i / n1 k + y0 i / n0 k), where k is the stratum of i.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.stratifiedEstimator_eq_lineartheorem

theorem stratifiedEstimator_eq_linear (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (n1 n0 : σ → ℕ)
  (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.stratifiedEstimator s n1 n0 a =
    -∑ i, (stratumSize s (s i) : ℝ) / Fintype.card ι * (po.y0 i / n0 (s i)) +
      ∑ i, treatInd a i * po.stratifiedWeight s n1 n0 i

The stratified estimator is affine in the treatment indicators: τ̂ = -Σ_i (N_k / N) y0 i / n0 k + Σ_i A_i w_i, with w the stratified weights.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratified_estimator_unbiasedtheorem

theorem stratified_estimator_unbiased [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  {n1 n0 : σ → ℕ} (hn : ∀ k, n1 k + n0 k = stratumSize s k)
  (hn1 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 0 < n1 k) (hn0 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 0 < n0 k) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 (fun k => by have := hn k; omega)).expect
    (po.stratifiedEstimator s n1 n0) = po.ate

Unbiasedness of the stratified estimator. In a nonempty population, under stratified randomization with n1 k treated and n0 k control units in every stratum k, n1 k + n0 k = N_k, and n1 k, n0 k > 0 for every nonempty stratum, the stratified estimator Σ_k (N_k / N) τ̂_k is unbiased for the population average treatment effect. Empty strata are allowed: they have weight N_k / N = 0.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.restrictdefinition

def PotentialOutcomes.restrict (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) :
  PotentialOutcomes {i // s i = k}

The potential outcomes of the units of the stratum k, as a population of its own.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratified_estimator_variancetheorem

theorem stratified_estimator_variance [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  {n1 n0 : σ → ℕ} (hn : ∀ k, n1 k + n0 k = stratumSize s k)
  (hn1 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 0 < n1 k) (hn0 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 0 < n0 k) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 (fun k => by have := hn k; omega)).variance
    (po.stratifiedEstimator s n1 n0) =
    ∑ k, ((stratumSize s k : ℝ) / Fintype.card ι) ^ 2 *
      ((po.restrict s k).varTreated / n1 k + (po.restrict s k).varControl / n0 k -
        (po.restrict s k).varEffect / stratumSize s k)

Variance of the stratified estimator. In a nonempty population, under stratified randomization with n1 k treated and n0 k control units in every stratum k, n1 k + n0 k = N_k, and n1 k, n0 k > 0 for every nonempty stratum, the variance of the stratified estimator is Σ_k (N_k / N)² V_k, where V_k = S1k²/n1 k + S0k²/n0 k - Sτk²/N_k is Neyman's variance of the difference in means within the stratum k, computed from the potential outcomes of that stratum alone. An empty stratum contributes 0.

CausalInference.Randomized.PotentialOutcomes.stratifiedVarEstdefinition

def PotentialOutcomes.stratifiedVarEst (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The observable variance estimator for the stratified estimator: Σ_k (N_k / N)² (s1k²/n1k + s0k²/n0k), where s1k², s0k² are the within-arm sample variances of the stratum k and n1k, n0k its realized arm counts (Neyman's estimator neymanVarEst computed within each stratum from the observed outcomes of that stratum). It is meaningful only when both arms of every nonempty stratum have at least two units.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratified_varEst_expecttheorem

theorem stratified_varEst_expect [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (s : ι → σ)
  {n1 n0 : σ → ℕ} (hn : ∀ k, n1 k + n0 k = stratumSize s k)
  (hn1 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 2 ≤ n1 k) (hn0 : ∀ k, stratumSize s k ≠ 0 → 2 ≤ n0 k) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 (fun k => by have := hn k; omega)).expect (po.stratifiedVarEst s) =
    (stratifiedDesign s n1 (fun k => by have := hn k; omega)).variance
      (po.stratifiedEstimator s n1 n0) +
      ∑ k, ((stratumSize s k : ℝ) / Fintype.card ι) ^ 2 *
        ((po.restrict s k).varEffect / stratumSize s k)

Expectation of the stratified variance estimator. In a nonempty population, under stratified randomization with n1 k treated and n0 k control units in every stratum k, n1 k + n0 k = N_k, and 2 ≤ n1 k, 2 ≤ n0 k for every nonempty stratum, the observable estimator Σ_k (N_k / N)² (s1k²/n1k + s0k²/n0k) has expectation equal to the exact variance of the stratified estimator plus Σ_k (N_k / N)² Sτk²/N_k, where Sτk² is the variance of the unit effects within the stratum k. In particular it is conservative.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratum_uniquetheorem

theorem stratum_unique [Unique σ] (s : ι → σ) (k : σ) : stratum s k = univ

With a single stratum, the stratum is the whole population.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedDesign_uniquetheorem

theorem stratifiedDesign_unique [Unique σ] (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ)
  (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) :
  stratifiedDesign s n1 h =
    completeDesign (n1 default) (by simpa [stratumSize, stratum_unique] using h default)

One stratum is complete randomization. With a single stratum, stratified randomization treating n1 units is the complete randomization treating n1 units.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratifiedEstimator_uniquetheorem

theorem stratifiedEstimator_unique [Unique σ] [Nonempty ι] (po : PotentialOutcomes ι)
  (s : ι → σ) (n1 n0 : σ → ℕ) (a : ι → Bool) :
  po.stratifiedEstimator s n1 n0 a = po.diffInMeans (n1 default) (n0 default) a

With a single stratum, the stratified estimator is the difference in means.

CausalInference.Randomized.stratified_fisher_pValue_validtheorem

theorem stratified_fisher_pValue_valid (po : PotentialOutcomes ι) (hnull : po.SharpNull)
  (s : ι → σ) (n1 : σ → ℕ) (h : ∀ k, n1 k ≤ stratumSize s k) (T : (ι → Bool) → (ι → ℝ) → ℝ)
  {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
  (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).prob
    (fun a => (stratifiedDesign s n1 h).fisherPValue T (po.observed a) a ≤ α) ≤ α

Fisher's test under stratified randomization. Under the sharp null the Fisher randomization p-value computed with the stratified design is valid.

Difference in differences

Two-period identification and its exact bias, staggered adoption with group-time effects, and a two-way fixed effects counterexample.

CausalInference.Designs.DifferenceInDifferences.EventStudy

CausalInference/Designs/DifferenceInDifferences/EventStudy.lean · 481 lines · 25 public theorems · 21 definitions · imports Designs.DifferenceInDifferences.Staggered

Two-way fixed effects under staggered adoption: a negative result. A concrete balanced panel with two equally sized cohorts and three periods (0, 1, 2): the early cohort is first treated in period 1, the late cohort in period 2, and nobody is never treated. Untreated outcomes are 0, so parallel trends and no anticipation hold exactly, but treatment effects are heterogeneous over time.

Sources: Goodman-Bacon (2021); Sun and Abraham (2021)

Public declarations (46)

CausalInference.EventStudy.adoptiondefinition

def adoption : Fin 2 → ℕ

Adoption period of each cohort, with periods 0, 1, 2: cohort 0 (early) is first treated in period 1, cohort 1 (late) in period 2. There is no never-treated cohort.

CausalInference.EventStudy.treatdefinition

def treat (i : Fin 2) (t : Fin 3) : ℝ

The treatment indicator of cohort i in period t: 1 from the adoption period on.

CausalInference.EventStudy.effectdefinition

def effect (a b c : ℝ) : Fin 2 → Fin 3 → ℝ

Cohort-time treatment effects, parameterized by a = ATT(early, 1), b = ATT(early, 2), c = ATT(late, 2); effects are 0 before adoption.

CausalInference.EventStudy.outcomedefinition

def outcome (a b c : ℝ) (i : Fin 2) (t : Fin 3) : ℝ

The cohort-time mean outcome. Untreated potential outcomes are 0 in every cell (so parallel trends holds exactly), and the observed outcome is the treatment effect when treated.

CausalInference.EventStudy.residdefinition

def resid (y : Fin 2 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (α : Fin 2 → ℝ) (δ : Fin 3 → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (i : Fin 2) (t : Fin 3) : ℝ

The residual of the two-way fixed effects fit with cohort effects α, period effects δ, and treatment coefficient β.

CausalInference.EventStudy.NormalEquationsdefinition

def NormalEquations (y : Fin 2 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (α : Fin 2 → ℝ) (δ : Fin 3 → ℝ) (β : ℝ) : Prop

The normal equations of the least squares regression of the outcome on cohort dummies, period dummies, and the treatment indicator, for a balanced panel with equally sized cohorts: the residual is orthogonal to every cohort dummy, every period dummy, and the treatment indicator.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeCoefdefinition

def twfeCoef (a b c : ℝ) : ℝ

The closed form of the static two-way fixed effects coefficient in this design: β = a - b / 2 + c / 2.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeCohortEffectdefinition

def twfeCohortEffect (a b c : ℝ) : Fin 2 → ℝ

Cohort effects solving the normal equations together with twfeCoef: the cohort means of outcome - β * treat, with β = twfeCoef a b c.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfePeriodEffectdefinition

def twfePeriodEffect (a b c : ℝ) : Fin 3 → ℝ

Period effects solving the normal equations together with twfeCoef: the period means of outcome - β * treat minus the grand mean, with β = twfeCoef a b c.

CausalInference.EventStudy.normalEquations_twfeCoeftheorem

theorem normalEquations_twfeCoef (a b c : ℝ) :
  NormalEquations (outcome a b c) (twfeCohortEffect a b c) (twfePeriodEffect a b c)
    (twfeCoef a b c)

The closed form solves the two-way fixed effects normal equations. For all effects a, b, c, the coefficient twfeCoef a b c, with the explicit cohort and period effects, makes the residual orthogonal to all regressors.

CausalInference.EventStudy.eq_twfeCoef_of_normalEquationstheorem

theorem eq_twfeCoef_of_normalEquations {a b c : ℝ} {α : Fin 2 → ℝ} {δ : Fin 3 → ℝ} {β : ℝ}
  (h : NormalEquations (outcome a b c) α δ β) : β = twfeCoef a b c

Uniqueness of the treatment coefficient. Any solution of the normal equations has treatment coefficient twfeCoef a b c; so twfeCoef is the population two-way fixed effects coefficient, whatever cohort and period effects accompany it.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeWeightdefinition

def twfeWeight : Fin 3 → ℝ

The implicit weights of the two-way fixed effects coefficient on the group-time effects (ATT(early, 1), ATT(early, 2), ATT(late, 2)).

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeCoef_eq_sum_twfeWeighttheorem

theorem twfeCoef_eq_sum_twfeWeight (a b c : ℝ) :
  twfeCoef a b c = ∑ k, twfeWeight k * ![a, b, c] k

Weight decomposition. The two-way fixed effects coefficient is the linear combination 1 * ATT(early, 1) - 1/2 * ATT(early, 2) + 1/2 * ATT(late, 2) of the group-time effects.

CausalInference.EventStudy.sum_twfeWeighttheorem

theorem sum_twfeWeight : ∑ k, twfeWeight k = 1

The weights sum to one.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeWeight_one_negtheorem

theorem twfeWeight_one_neg : twfeWeight 1 < 0

A negative weight. The coefficient decomposes as β = a / 2 + (c - (b - a)) / 2: half the early cohort's effect a measured against the not-yet-treated late cohort in period 1, plus half the late cohort's change c in period 2 measured against the already-treated early cohort, whose change b - a serves as the comparison. Through that comparison the weight on ATT(early, 2) = b is -1/2 < 0, so the two-way fixed effects coefficient is not a convex combination of the group-time effects.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeCoef_wrong_signtheorem

theorem twfeCoef_wrong_sign : twfeCoef 1 4 1 = -1 / 2

Wrong sign. With ATT(early, 1) = 1, ATT(early, 2) = 4, and ATT(late, 2) = 1, every group-time effect is positive while the two-way fixed effects coefficient is -1/2.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfeCoef_not_mem_convexHulltheorem

theorem twfeCoef_not_mem_convexHull :
  NormalEquations (outcome 1 4 1) (twfeCohortEffect 1 4 1) (twfePeriodEffect 1 4 1)
      (twfeCoef 1 4 1) ∧
    twfeCoef 1 4 1 ∉ convexHull ℝ (Set.range ![(1 : ℝ), 4, 1])

Not a convex combination. In the example with effects 1, 4, 1, the two-way fixed effects coefficient, which is the unique treatment coefficient solving the normal equations, lies outside the convex hull of the group-time effects.

CausalInference.EventStudy.exMeasuredefinition

def exMeasure : Measure (Fin 2)

The uniform probability measure on the two units.

CausalInference.EventStudy.exCohortdefinition

def exCohort (i : Fin 2) : WithTop ℕ

The cohort (first treated period) of each unit.

CausalInference.EventStudy.effectNatdefinition

def effectNat (a b c : ℝ) (i : Fin 2) (t : ℕ) : ℝ

The treatment effect of unit i in period t, extended by 0 beyond period 2.

CausalInference.EventStudy.exYdefinition

Potential outcomes: under its own adoption date a unit's outcome is its treatment effect from adoption on, and every other potential outcome, in particular the never-treated one, is 0.

CausalInference.EventStudy.exYobsdefinition

def exYobs (a b c : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin 2) : ℝ

Observed outcomes, defined by consistency.

theorem ex_noAnticipation (a b c : ℝ) :

CausalInference.EventStudy.ex_untreatedtheorem

theorem ex_untreated (a b c : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (i : Fin 2) : exY a b c t ⊤ i = 0

Never-treated potential outcomes are identically 0.

CausalInference.EventStudy.ex_parallel_trendstheorem

theorem ex_parallel_trends (a b c : ℝ) (s c' : Set (Fin 2)) (r : ℕ) :
  ∫ ω, (exY a b c (r + 1) ⊤ ω - exY a b c r ⊤ ω) ∂exMeasure[|s]
    = ∫ ω, (exY a b c (r + 1) ⊤ ω - exY a b c r ⊤ ω) ∂exMeasure[|c']

Hence parallel trends against the never-treated potential outcomes holds for every cohort, comparison event, and period.

CausalInference.EventStudy.ex_cohort_twotheorem

  Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY a b c) 1 1 = a ∧
    Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY a b c) 1 2 = b ∧
    Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY a b c) 2 2 = c

The group-time effects of the model, in the sense of Staggered.att, are ATT(1, 1) = a, ATT(1, 2) = b, and ATT(2, 2) = c.

theorem twfe_not_convex_combination :
  Staggered.Consistency exCohort (exY 1 4 1) (exYobs 1 4 1) ∧

  0 < Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY 1 4 1) 1 2 ∧
  0 < Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY 1 4 1) 2 2 ∧
  (-1 / 2 : ℝ) ∉ convexHull ℝ {Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY 1 4 1) 1 1,
    Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY 1 4 1) 1 2,
    Staggered.att exMeasure exCohort (exY 1 4 1) 2 2}

Two-way fixed effects is not a convex combination of group-time effects. In the staggered adoption model with ATT(1, 1) = 1, ATT(1, 2) = 4, ATT(2, 2) = 1, consistency and no anticipation hold, the never-treated group is empty (so the design is the not-yet-treated one), and parallel trends against the not-yet-treated group holds for every cohort, period, and step, because untreated outcomes are 0. The observed cohort-time means are the cells of the regression, and every solution of the normal equations has treatment coefficient -1/2 (the cohort and period effects are determined only up to a constant shift between them, so only the treatment coefficient is unique). That coefficient solves the normal equations, has the wrong sign, and lies outside the convex hull of the group-time effects.

CausalInference.EventStudy.dynDummydefinition

def dynDummy : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ

The event-time dummies, indexed by k : Fin 3 for the event times -2, 0, 1, as cohort-by-period indicator matrices. Event time -2 occurs only for the late cohort in period 0; event time 0 for the early cohort in period 1 and the late cohort in period 2; event time 1 for the early cohort in period 2. The never-treated cohort has no dummy.

CausalInference.EventStudy.dynOutcomedefinition

def dynOutcome : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ

The cohort-time mean outcomes: early cohort (0, 1, 4), late cohort (0, 0, 2), never-treated cohort (0, 0, 0).

CausalInference.EventStudy.dynResiddefinition

def dynResid (y : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (α δ β : Fin 3 → ℝ) (i t : Fin 3) : ℝ

The residual of the dynamic fit with cohort effects α, period effects δ, and event-time coefficients β.

CausalInference.EventStudy.DynNormalEquationsdefinition

def DynNormalEquations (y : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ) (α δ β : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Prop

The normal equations of the dynamic event-study regression: the residual is orthogonal to every cohort dummy, every period dummy, and every event-time dummy.

CausalInference.EventStudy.dynNormalEquations_solutiontheorem

theorem dynNormalEquations_solution :
  DynNormalEquations dynOutcome ![-1 / 10, 2 / 5, 1 / 10] ![0, -3 / 10, 0]
    ![-2 / 5, 3 / 2, 41 / 10]

An explicit solution of the dynamic normal equations, with lead coefficient -2/5.

CausalInference.EventStudy.dyn_lead_contaminationtheorem

theorem dyn_lead_contamination :
  (dynOutcome 0 0 = 0 ∧ dynOutcome 1 0 = 0 ∧ dynOutcome 1 1 = 0) ∧
  (∃ α δ β : Fin 3 → ℝ, DynNormalEquations dynOutcome α δ β) ∧
  ∀ α δ β : Fin 3 → ℝ, DynNormalEquations dynOutcome α δ β → β 0 = -2 / 5

Lead contamination. In the panel above, all pre-treatment cells equal the untreated outcome 0, yet every solution of the dynamic normal equations has lead coefficient β₋₂ = -2/5 ≠ 0, and such a solution exists.

CausalInference.EventStudy.doubleDemeandefinition

def doubleDemean (D : ι → τ → ℝ) (i : ι) (t : τ) : ℝ

The double-demeaned regressor D̃ i t = D i t - D̄ i· - D̄ ·t + D̄ ··, with row, column, and grand means over a balanced panel.

CausalInference.EventStudy.PanelNormalEquationsdefinition

def PanelNormalEquations (D y : ι → τ → ℝ) (α : ι → ℝ) (δ : τ → ℝ) (β : ℝ) : Prop

The normal equations of the least squares regression of y on unit dummies, period dummies, and the regressor D in a balanced panel: the residual is orthogonal to every unit dummy, every period dummy, and D.

CausalInference.EventStudy.sum_sum_mul_add_eq_zerotheorem

theorem sum_sum_mul_add_eq_zero {M : ι → τ → ℝ} (hrow : ∀ i, ∑ t, M i t = 0)
  (hcol : ∀ t, ∑ i, M i t = 0) (u : ι → ℝ) (v : τ → ℝ) :
  ∑ i, ∑ t, M i t * (u i + v t) = 0

A panel array with zero row sums and zero column sums is orthogonal to every additive array u i + v t.

CausalInference.EventStudy.doubleDemean_eqtheorem

theorem doubleDemean_eq (D : ι → τ → ℝ) (i : ι) (t : τ) :
  doubleDemean D i t = D i t + (-((Fintype.card τ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ s, D i s)
    + (((Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * Fintype.card τ)⁻¹ * ∑ j, ∑ s, D j s
      - (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j, D j t))

The double-demeaned regressor differs from the regressor by an additive array.

CausalInference.EventStudy.sum_doubleDemean_rowtheorem

theorem sum_doubleDemean_row [Nonempty τ] (D : ι → τ → ℝ) (i : ι) :
  ∑ t, doubleDemean D i t = 0

The double-demeaned regressor has zero row sums.

CausalInference.EventStudy.sum_doubleDemean_coltheorem

theorem sum_doubleDemean_col [Nonempty ι] (D : ι → τ → ℝ) (t : τ) :
  ∑ i, doubleDemean D i t = 0

The double-demeaned regressor has zero column sums.

CausalInference.EventStudy.twfe_coef_mul_sum_sqtheorem

theorem twfe_coef_mul_sum_sq [Nonempty ι] [Nonempty τ] {D y : ι → τ → ℝ} {α : ι → ℝ}
  {δ : τ → ℝ} {β : ℝ} (h : PanelNormalEquations D y α δ β) :
  β * ∑ i, ∑ t, doubleDemean D i t ^ 2 = ∑ i, ∑ t, doubleDemean D i t * y i t

The two-way fixed effects coefficient by double demeaning. In a balanced panel with finitely many units and periods (both nonempty), every solution (α, δ, β) of the normal equations of the regression of y on unit dummies, period dummies, and D satisfies β ∑ᵢ ∑ₜ D̃ᵢₜ² = ∑ᵢ ∑ₜ D̃ᵢₜ yᵢₜ, where D̃ is the double-demeaned regressor. When ∑ D̃² ≠ 0 this determines β.

CausalInference.Designs.DifferenceInDifferences.Staggered

CausalInference/Designs/DifferenceInDifferences/Staggered.lean · 497 lines · 23 public theorems · 16 definitions · imports Designs.DifferenceInDifferences.TwoPeriod

Staggered adoption difference in differences. Group-time average treatment effects with staggered, absorbing treatment adoption, following Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), Difference-in-differences with multiple time periods.

Sources: Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021)

Public declarations (39)

CausalInference.Staggered.cohortdefinition

def cohort (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (g : WithTop ℕ) : Set Ω

The cohort first treated in period g (g = ⊤: the never-treated group).

CausalInference.Staggered.notYetTreateddefinition

def notYetTreated (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (t : ℕ) : Set Ω

The units not yet treated in period t, {Gc > t}; it contains the never-treated.

CausalInference.Staggered.Consistencydefinition

def Consistency (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) :
  Prop

Consistency. The observed outcome in period t is the potential outcome under the unit's own adoption date.

CausalInference.Staggered.NoAnticipationdefinition

def NoAnticipation (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ) : Prop

No anticipation (almost surely). In every period strictly before a unit's adoption date, its potential outcome under that adoption date equals its never-treated potential outcome.

CausalInference.Staggered.ParallelTrendsNeverTreateddefinition

def ParallelTrendsNeverTreated (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ)
  (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (g s : ℕ) : Prop

Parallel trends against the never-treated group, for cohort g between periods s and s + 1: E[Y (s+1) ⊤ - Y s ⊤ | Gc = g] = E[Y (s+1) ⊤ - Y s ⊤ | Gc = ⊤].

CausalInference.Staggered.ParallelTrendsNotYetTreateddefinition

def ParallelTrendsNotYetTreated (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ)
  (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (g t s : ℕ) : Prop

Parallel trends against the not-yet-treated group {Gc > t}, for cohort g between periods s and s + 1: E[Y (s+1) ⊤ - Y s ⊤ | Gc = g] = E[Y (s+1) ⊤ - Y s ⊤ | Gc > t].

CausalInference.Staggered.attdefinition

def att (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
  (g t : ℕ) : ℝ

The group-time average treatment effect ATT(g, t) = E[Y t g - Y t ⊤ | Gc = g].

CausalInference.Staggered.diddefinition

def did (μ : Measure Ω) (Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (s c : Set Ω) (b t : ℕ) : ℝ

The observed long difference in differences between the events s and c, from base period b to period t.

CausalInference.Staggered.MeanNoAnticipationdefinition

def MeanNoAnticipation (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ) (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
  (g b : ℕ) : Prop

No anticipation in means for cohort g at base period b: E[Y b g | Gc = g] = E[Y b ⊤ | Gc = g]. This is the only no-anticipation restriction on the treated cohort that the identification theorems use; it follows from the almost sure NoAnticipation when b < g (meanNoAnticipation_of_noAnticipation).

CausalInference.Staggered.MeanNoAnticipationNotYetTreateddefinition

def MeanNoAnticipationNotYetTreated (μ : Measure Ω) (Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ)
  (Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (b t : ℕ) : Prop

No anticipation in means for the not-yet-treated group {Gc > t} at periods b and t: the observed mean equals the never-treated mean, E[Yobs b | Gc > t] = E[Y b ⊤ | Gc > t] and E[Yobs t | Gc > t] = E[Y t ⊤ | Gc > t]. Under consistency it follows from the almost sure NoAnticipation when b ≤ t (meanNoAnticipationNotYetTreated_of_noAnticipation).

  notYetTreated Gc t = (⋃ k ∈ Finset.range (t + 1), cohort Gc k)ᶜ

The not-yet-treated group in period t is the complement of the cohorts 0, …, t.

CausalInference.Staggered.long_parallel_trendstheorem

theorem long_parallel_trends {μ : Measure Ω} {m : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {s c : Set Ω} {b t : ℕ}
  (hbt : b ≤ t) (hm : ∀ r, b ≤ r → r ≤ t → Integrable (m r) μ)

    ∫ ω, (m (r + 1) ω - m r ω) ∂μ[|s] = ∫ ω, (m (r + 1) ω - m r ω) ∂μ[|c]) :
  ∫ ω, (m t ω - m b ω) ∂μ[|s] = ∫ ω, (m t ω - m b ω) ∂μ[|c]

One-period parallel trends between two events, for every period from b to t, imply parallel long differences from b to t, when m r is integrable for b ≤ r ≤ t.

CausalInference.Staggered.att_eq_did_neverTreatedtheorem

theorem att_eq_did_neverTreated {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ}
  {Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {g b t : ℕ}
  (hg : MeasurableSet (cohort Gc g)) (hnev : MeasurableSet (cohort Gc ⊤))
  (hgpos : μ (cohort Gc g) ≠ 0) (hnevpos : μ (cohort Gc ⊤) ≠ 0)
  (hcons : Consistency Gc Y Yobs) (hNA : MeanNoAnticipation μ Gc Y g b) (hbt : b ≤ t)
  (hPT : ∀ r, b ≤ r → r < t → ParallelTrendsNeverTreated μ Gc Y g r)
  (hYgb : Integrable (Y b g) μ) (hYgt : Integrable (Y t g) μ)
  (hY0 : ∀ r, b ≤ r → r ≤ t → Integrable (Y r ⊤) μ) :
  att μ Gc Y g t = did μ Yobs (cohort Gc g) (cohort Gc ⊤) b t

**Identification of ATT(g, t) with never-treated controls** (Callaway and Sant'Anna). Let μ be a finite measure under which cohort g and the never-treated group have positive mass, and b ≤ t (the usual choice is the base period b = g - 1 for g ≥ 1). Under consistency, no anticipation in means for cohort g at the base period b, one-period parallel trends between cohort g and the never-treated group in every period from b to t, and integrability of Y b g, Y t g, and of the never-treated outcomes Y r ⊤ for b ≤ r ≤ t, ATT(g, t) = (E[Yobs t | Gc = g] - E[Yobs b | Gc = g]) - (E[Yobs t | Gc = ⊤] - E[Yobs b | Gc = ⊤]).

CausalInference.Staggered.att_eq_did_notYetTreatedtheorem

theorem att_eq_did_notYetTreated {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ}
  {Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {g b t : ℕ}
  (hg : MeasurableSet (cohort Gc g))
  (hgpos : μ (cohort Gc g) ≠ 0) (hnytpos : μ (notYetTreated Gc t) ≠ 0)
  (hcons : Consistency Gc Y Yobs) (hNA : MeanNoAnticipation μ Gc Y g b)
  (hNAc : MeanNoAnticipationNotYetTreated μ Gc Y Yobs b t) (hbt : b ≤ t) (_hgt : g ≤ t)
  (hPT : ∀ r, b ≤ r → r < t → ParallelTrendsNotYetTreated μ Gc Y g t r)
  (hYgb : Integrable (Y b g) μ) (hYgt : Integrable (Y t g) μ)
  (hYobsb : Integrable (Yobs b) μ[|notYetTreated Gc t])
  (hYobst : Integrable (Yobs t) μ[|notYetTreated Gc t])
  (hY0 : ∀ r, b ≤ r → r ≤ t → Integrable (Y r ⊤) μ) :
  att μ Gc Y g t = did μ Yobs (cohort Gc g) (notYetTreated Gc t) b t

**Identification of ATT(g, t) with not-yet-treated controls** (Callaway and Sant'Anna). Let μ be a finite measure under which cohort g and the not-yet-treated group {Gc > t} (which contains the never-treated) have positive mass, and b ≤ t. Under consistency, no anticipation in means for cohort g at b and for {Gc > t} at b and t, one-period parallel trends between cohort g and {Gc > t} in every period from b to t, and integrability of Y b g, Y t g, and of Y r ⊤ for b ≤ r ≤ t, and of Yobs b, Yobs t given {Gc > t}, ATT(g, t) equals (E[Yobs t | Gc = g] - E[Yobs b | Gc = g]) - (E[Yobs t | Gc > t] - E[Yobs b | Gc > t]). The hypothesis g ≤ t (post-adoption periods) keeps cohort g out of the comparison group; the linear argument does not use it.

theorem eventTimeAggregate_mem_convexHull {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ} {Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {S : Finset ℕ} (e : ℕ)
  (hne : S.Nonempty) (hS : ∀ g ∈ S, μ (cohort Gc g) ≠ 0)
  (_hint : ∀ g ∈ S, Integrable (fun ω => Y (g + e) g ω - Y (g + e) ⊤ ω) μ[|cohort Gc g]) :
  eventTimeAggregate μ Gc Y S e
    ∈ convexHull ℝ ((fun g => att μ Gc Y g (g + e)) '' (S : Set ℕ))

The event-time aggregate is a convex combination of group-time effects. Let μ be a finite measure and S a nonempty finite set of cohorts, each of positive mass, whose effects Y (g + e) g - Y (g + e) ⊤ are integrable given Gc = g (so that each ATT(g, g + e) is a genuine mean; the convexity argument itself does not use this). Then the aggregate lies in the convex hull of {ATT(g, g + e) : g ∈ S}.

CausalInference.Staggered.eventTimeAggregate_eq_sum_didtheorem

theorem eventTimeAggregate_eq_sum_did {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  {Gc : Ω → WithTop ℕ} {Y : ℕ → WithTop ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {Yobs : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {S : Finset ℕ}
  {e : ℕ} {base : ℕ → ℕ} (hnev : MeasurableSet (cohort Gc ⊤))
  (hnevpos : μ (cohort Gc ⊤) ≠ 0) (hcons : Consistency Gc Y Yobs)
  (hS : ∀ g ∈ S, MeasurableSet (cohort Gc g) ∧ μ (cohort Gc g) ≠ 0)
  (hNA : ∀ g ∈ S, MeanNoAnticipation μ Gc Y g (base g)) (hbt : ∀ g ∈ S, base g ≤ g + e)
  (hPT : ∀ g ∈ S, ∀ r, base g ≤ r → r < g + e → ParallelTrendsNeverTreated μ Gc Y g r)
  (hY : ∀ t d, Integrable (Y t d) μ) :
  eventTimeAggregate μ Gc Y S e
    = ∑ g ∈ S, cohortWeight μ Gc S g * did μ Yobs (cohort Gc g) (cohort Gc ⊤) (base g) (g + e)

Identification of the event-time aggregate. If, for every cohort g ∈ S with base period base g ≤ g + e, the hypotheses of att_eq_did_neverTreated hold (finite measure, positive mass of cohort g and of the never-treated group, consistency, no anticipation in means at base g, parallel trends from base g to g + e, integrable potential outcomes), then the event-time aggregate equals the cohort-size-weighted sum of the observed differences in differences ∑_{g ∈ S} w_g DiD(g, ⊤; base g, g + e).

theorem att_eq_did_of_twoPeriod {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]

CausalInference.Designs.DifferenceInDifferences.TwoPeriod

CausalInference/Designs/DifferenceInDifferences/TwoPeriod.lean · 623 lines · 31 public theorems · 22 definitions

Two by two difference in differences. Identification of the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) in the canonical design with two groups and two periods, on a probability space (Ω, μ) with conditional means taken against ProbabilityTheory.cond (μ[|s]).

Sources: Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021)

Public declarations (53)

  Integrable f μ[|s]

A function integrable for μ is integrable for every conditional measure μ[|s].

  (h : ∀ ω ∈ s, f ω = g ω) : ∫ ω, f ω ∂μ[|s] = ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ[|s]

Conditional means given a measurable event s only depend on the values on s.

theorem integral_cond_eq_of_eqOn {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {s : Set Ω}
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hμs : μ s ≠ 0) {f : Ω → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (h : ∀ ω ∈ s, f ω = k) :
