  (hz : μ (M.instrumentEq z') ≠ 0) :
  obsMean μ M.observed treatedInd z' = μ.real {ω | M.D z' ω = true}

Under instrument independence, P(D = 1 | Z = z') = P(D z' = 1).

CausalInference.IVModel.obsMean_untreatedIndtheorem

theorem obsMean_untreatedInd [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) {z' : Bool}
  (hz : μ (M.instrumentEq z') ≠ 0) :
  obsMean μ M.observed untreatedInd z' = μ.real {ω | M.D z' ω = true}ᶜ

Under instrument independence, P(D = 0 | Z = z') = P(D z' = 0).

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_mem_Icc_armstheorem

theorem ate_mem_Icc_arms [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ} (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) {z₁ z₀ : Bool} (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq z₁) ≠ 0)
  (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq z₀) ≠ 0) (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  M.ate μ z ∈ Icc
    (obsMean μ M.observed yTreated z₁ - obsMean μ M.observed yUntreated z₀ +
      lo * obsMean μ M.observed untreatedInd z₁ - hi * obsMean μ M.observed treatedInd z₀)
    (obsMean μ M.observed yTreated z₁ - obsMean μ M.observed yUntreated z₀ +
      hi * obsMean μ M.observed untreatedInd z₁ - lo * obsMean μ M.observed treatedInd z₀)

The IV bound inclusion for an arbitrary choice of arms: under the exclusion restriction, instrument independence, P(Z = z₁) ≠ 0, P(Z = z₀) ≠ 0 and potential outcomes in [lo, hi], E[Y z 1 - Y z 0] lies between E[Y 1{D=1} | Z=z₁] - E[Y 1{D=0} | Z=z₀] + lo P(D=0 | Z=z₁) - hi P(D=1 | Z=z₀) and the same with lo and hi exchanged. The arm z₁ is used for the treated mean E[Y 1] and the arm z₀ for the untreated mean E[Y 0].

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_mem_Icc_boundstheorem

theorem ate_mem_Icc_bounds [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ} (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0)
  (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  M.ate μ z ∈ Icc (lowerBound μ lo hi M.observed) (upperBound μ lo hi M.observed)

IV bounds on the average treatment effect (Robins 1989; Manski 1990). Assume the exclusion restriction, instrument independence, P(Z = z) ≠ 0 for both instrument values, and potential outcomes with values in [lo, hi]. Then for either instrument value z indexing the outcomes, E[Y z 1 - Y z 0] lies between lowerBound and upperBound: E[Y 1{D=1} | Z=1] - E[Y 1{D=0} | Z=0] + lo P(D=0 | Z=1) - hi P(D=1 | Z=0) and the same with lo and hi exchanged. Both endpoints are functionals of the observed data. The argument splits E[Y 1] over {D 1 = 1}, where it is identified from the arm Z = 1, and its complement, where it is bounded by lo and hi, and splits E[Y 0] likewise using the arm Z = 0. Monotonicity is not needed for the inclusion, and without it the interval is valid but not claimed to be sharp; monotonicity enters the stratum interpretation (meanY1_eq, meanY0_eq), the complier form of the width (upperBound_sub_lowerBound) and sharpness within monotone models (identifiedSet_ate). The hypotheses are stronger than the population-level conditions under which Hernan and Robins (Causal Inference: What If) state the natural bounds: the exclusion restriction is imposed unit by unit (almost surely), not only on the means E[Y^{z,d}], and instrument independence is joint independence of Z and all potential variables, not marginal exchangeability for each (z, d).

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_mem_Icc_boundsSwaptheorem

theorem ate_mem_Icc_boundsSwap [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ} (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0)
  (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  M.ate μ z ∈ Icc (lowerBoundSwap μ lo hi M.observed) (upperBoundSwap μ lo hi M.observed)

IV bounds with the instrument arms swapped. Under the same assumptions as ate_mem_Icc_bounds, E[Y z 1 - Y z 0] lies between lowerBoundSwap and upperBoundSwap, which use the arm Z = 0 for the treated mean and the arm Z = 1 for the untreated mean.

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_mem_Icc_bounds_intertheorem

theorem ate_mem_Icc_bounds_inter [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ} (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0)
  (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  M.ate μ z ∈ Icc (max (lowerBound μ lo hi M.observed) (lowerBoundSwap μ lo hi M.observed))
    (min (upperBound μ lo hi M.observed) (upperBoundSwap μ lo hi M.observed))

Intersection of the two arm orderings. Under the assumptions of ate_mem_Icc_bounds, the average treatment effect lies in the intersection of the two intervals, [max lowerBound lowerBoundSwap, min upperBound upperBoundSwap]. No sharpness claim is made for this intersection.

CausalInference.IVModel.upperBound_sub_lowerBoundtheorem

theorem upperBound_sub_lowerBound [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ}
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) :
  upperBound μ lo hi M.observed - lowerBound μ lo hi M.observed =
    (hi - lo) * (1 - μ.real M.compliers)

Width of the IV bounds under monotonicity. Under instrument independence, monotonicity and P(Z = z) ≠ 0 for both z, the IV bounds have width (hi - lo) (1 - P(compliers)). It is the assumption-free width IVBounds.upperBound_sub_lowerBound rewritten with the identified never-taker and always-taker shares.

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_eq_sum_stratatheorem

theorem ate_eq_sum_strata (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) {z : Bool}
  (hY : ∀ d, Integrable (M.Y z d) μ) :
  M.ate μ z = ∫ ω in M.compliers, M.effect z ω ∂μ + ∫ ω in M.alwaysTakers, M.effect z ω ∂μ +
    ∫ ω in M.neverTakers, M.effect z ω ∂μ

Stratum decomposition of the average treatment effect: under monotonicity and integrable potential outcomes, E[Y z 1 - Y z 0] is the sum of the integrals of the unit-level effect over the compliers, the always-takers and the never-takers.

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_eq_strata_condtheorem

theorem ate_eq_strata_cond [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) {z : Bool}
  (hY : ∀ d, Integrable (M.Y z d) μ) :
  M.ate μ z = μ.real M.compliers * M.complierEffect μ z +
    μ.real M.alwaysTakers * ∫ ω, M.effect z ω ∂μ[|M.alwaysTakers] +
    μ.real M.neverTakers * ∫ ω, M.effect z ω ∂μ[|M.neverTakers]

The stratum decomposition in conditional form: ATE = P(C) CACE + P(AT) E[Y 1 - Y 0 | AT] + P(NT) E[Y 1 - Y 0 | NT], where each conditional mean is an integral against the conditional measure. A stratum of probability zero contributes zero, as it should; no division by its probability occurs.

CausalInference.IVModel.obsMean_treatedInd_falsetheorem

theorem obsMean_treatedInd_false [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ)
  (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) :
  obsMean μ M.observed treatedInd false = μ.real M.alwaysTakers

The always-taker share is identified: P(D = 1 | Z = 0) = P(AT).

CausalInference.IVModel.obsMean_untreatedInd_truetheorem

theorem obsMean_untreatedInd_true [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ)
  (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) :
  obsMean μ M.observed untreatedInd true = μ.real M.neverTakers

The never-taker share is identified: P(D = 0 | Z = 1) = P(NT).

CausalInference.IVModel.obsMean_yTreated_falsetheorem

theorem obsMean_yTreated_false [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {z : Bool} (hY : Integrable (M.Y z true) μ) :
  obsMean μ M.observed yTreated false = ∫ ω in M.alwaysTakers, M.Y z true ω ∂μ

The treated outcome of the always-takers is identified: E[Y 1{D=1} | Z=0] = ∫_AT Y z 1. Dividing by P(D = 1 | Z = 0) = P(AT), when positive, gives E[Y 1 | AT].

CausalInference.IVModel.obsMean_yUntreated_truetheorem

theorem obsMean_yUntreated_true [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) {z : Bool} (hY : Integrable (M.Y z false) μ) :
  obsMean μ M.observed yUntreated true = ∫ ω in M.neverTakers, M.Y z false ω ∂μ

The untreated outcome of the never-takers is identified: E[Y 1{D=0} | Z=1] = ∫_NT Y z 0.

CausalInference.IVModel.meanY1_eqtheorem

theorem meanY1_eq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ) (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ)
  (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) {z : Bool}
  (hY : Integrable (M.Y z true) μ) :
  ∫ ω, M.Y z true ω ∂μ =
    obsMean μ M.observed yTreated true + ∫ ω in M.neverTakers, M.Y z true ω ∂μ

E[Y z 1] = E[Y 1{D=1} | Z=1] + ∫_NT Y z 1: the only unidentified part of the treated mean is the treated outcome of the never-takers.

CausalInference.IVModel.meanY0_eqtheorem

theorem meanY0_eq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ) (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ)
  (hM : M.Monotonicity μ) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {z : Bool}
  (hY : Integrable (M.Y z false) μ) :
  ∫ ω, M.Y z false ω ∂μ =
    obsMean μ M.observed yUntreated false + ∫ ω in M.alwaysTakers, M.Y z false ω ∂μ

E[Y z 0] = E[Y 1{D=0} | Z=0] + ∫_AT Y z 0: the only unidentified part of the untreated mean is the untreated outcome of the always-takers.

CausalInference.IVModel.measurableSet_treatmentPairtheorem

theorem measurableSet_treatmentPair (p : Bool × Bool → Prop) :
  MeasurableSet {w : Potentials | p (w.1 false, w.1 true)}

A set of potential-variable vectors defined by a condition on the pair of potential treatments is measurable.

CausalInference.IVModel.refillPotdefinition

def refillPot (c1 c0 : ℝ) (w : Potentials) : Potentials

Refilling the unobserved potential outcomes: on the never-takers (D 0 = D 1 = 0) the treated outcome is set to c1, on the always-takers (D 0 = D 1 = 1) the untreated outcome is set to c0, for both instrument values; the potential treatments and all other potential outcomes are unchanged.

CausalInference.IVModel.measurable_refillPottheorem

theorem measurable_refillPot (c1 c0 : ℝ) : Measurable (refillPot c1 c0)

CausalInference.IVModel.refilldefinition

def refill (c1 c0 : ℝ) : IVModel Ω

The model M with its unobserved potential outcomes refilled by refillPot c1 c0: the treated outcome of the never-takers becomes c1 and the untreated outcome of the always-takers becomes c0.

CausalInference.IVModel.observed_refilltheorem

theorem observed_refill (c1 c0 : ℝ) : (M.refill c1 c0).observed = M.observed

Refilling never changes the observed data: the refilled outcomes are never observed.

CausalInference.IVModel.refill_exclusiontheorem

theorem refill_exclusion (hE : M.Exclusion μ) (c1 c0 : ℝ) : (M.refill c1 c0).Exclusion μ

CausalInference.IVModel.refill_independencetheorem

theorem refill_independence (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (c1 c0 : ℝ) :
  (M.refill c1 c0).InstrumentIndependence μ

CausalInference.IVModel.refill_relevance_ifftheorem

theorem refill_relevance_iff (c1 c0 : ℝ) : (M.refill c1 c0).Relevance μ ↔ M.Relevance μ

Refilling leaves the instrument and the potential treatments unchanged, so the first stage and hence relevance are unchanged.

CausalInference.IVModel.refill_boundedtheorem

theorem refill_bounded {lo hi : ℝ} (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) {c1 c0 : ℝ}
  (hc1 : c1 ∈ Icc lo hi) (hc0 : c0 ∈ Icc lo hi) :
  ∀ z d ω, (M.refill c1 c0).Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi

CausalInference.IVModel.ate_refilltheorem

theorem ate_refill [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {lo hi : ℝ} (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0)
  (hb : ∀ z d ω, M.Y z d ω ∈ Icc lo hi) {c1 c0 : ℝ} (hc1 : c1 ∈ Icc lo hi)
  (hc0 : c0 ∈ Icc lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  (M.refill c1 c0).ate μ z = obsMean μ M.observed yTreated true -
    obsMean μ M.observed yUntreated false + c1 * obsMean μ M.observed untreatedInd true -
    c0 * obsMean μ M.observed treatedInd false

The average treatment effect of the refilled model: E[Y 1{D=1} | Z=1] - E[Y 1{D=0} | Z=0] + c1 P(D=0 | Z=1) - c0 P(D=1 | Z=0).

CausalInference.IVBounds.modelsdefinition

def models (μ : Measure Ω) (lo hi : ℝ) : Set (IVModel Ω)

The maintained assumptions for the IV bounds, as a class of models on the fixed (Ω, μ): the exclusion restriction, instrument independence, monotonicity, P(Z = z) ≠ 0 for both instrument values, and potential outcomes with values in [lo, hi].

CausalInference.IVBounds.refill_mem_modelstheorem

theorem refill_mem_models {M : IVModel Ω} (hM : M ∈ models μ lo hi) {c1 c0 : ℝ}
  (hc1 : c1 ∈ Icc lo hi) (hc0 : c0 ∈ Icc lo hi) : M.refill c1 c0 ∈ models μ lo hi

CausalInference.IVBounds.identifiedSet_atetheorem

theorem identifiedSet_ate [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {M : IVModel Ω} (hM : M ∈ models μ lo hi)
  (z : Bool) :
  identifiedSet (models μ lo hi) IVModel.observed (fun M' ↦ M'.ate μ z) M.observed =
    Icc (lowerBound μ lo hi M.observed) (upperBound μ lo hi M.observed)

Sharpness of the IV bounds (the identified set). Under exclusion, instrument independence, monotonicity, positive instrument probabilities and outcomes in [lo, hi], the identified set of the average treatment effect at the observed data of any model M of the class is exactly [lowerBound, upperBound]. Each value is attained by refilling the treated outcome of the never-takers and the untreated outcome of the always-takers with constants (IVModel.refill). The observation is the realized observed-data map ω ↦ (Z ω, Dobs ω, Yobs ω) on the fixed probability space (Ω, μ); models differ in their potential outcomes. This observation is finer than the observed-data law, so the sharpness statement is at least as strong as sharpness for the law (models with equal observation maps have equal laws).

CausalInference.IVBounds.exists_model_ate_eq_lowerBoundtheorem

theorem exists_model_ate_eq_lowerBound [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {M : IVModel Ω}
  (hM : M ∈ models μ lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  ∃ M' ∈ models μ lo hi, M'.observed = M.observed ∧
    μ.map M'.observed = μ.map M.observed ∧ M'.ate μ z = lowerBound μ lo hi M.observed

The lower IV bound is attained: some model of the class with the same observed data (hence the same observed-data law) has average treatment effect equal to lowerBound.

CausalInference.IVBounds.exists_model_ate_eq_upperBoundtheorem

theorem exists_model_ate_eq_upperBound [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {M : IVModel Ω}
  (hM : M ∈ models μ lo hi) (z : Bool) :
  ∃ M' ∈ models μ lo hi, M'.observed = M.observed ∧
    μ.map M'.observed = μ.map M.observed ∧ M'.ate μ z = upperBound μ lo hi M.observed

The upper IV bound is attained: some model of the class with the same observed data (hence the same observed-data law) has average treatment effect equal to upperBound.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.MeanIndependentdefinition

def MeanIndependent (μ : Measure Ω) (Zi : Ω → Bool) (m : POModel Ω) : Prop

Mean independence of the potential outcomes from a binary instrument Zi: E[Y1 | Zi = z] = E[Y1] and E[Y0 | Zi = z] = E[Y0] for both instrument values, the conditional means being integrals against μ[|Zi = z]. The condition is imposed only for instrument values of positive probability, since conditioning on a null event is meaningless; the theorems below assume both values have positive probability.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.integral_eq_cond_add_condtheorem

theorem integral_eq_cond_add_cond [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
  {g : Ω → ℝ} (hg : Integrable g μ) :
  μ.real s * ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ[|s] + μ.real sᶜ * ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ[|sᶜ] = ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ

A finite mean is the weighted average of the two conditional means given s and sᶜ: ∫ g = μ(s) E[g | s] + μ(sᶜ) E[g | sᶜ].

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.boundY1_eq_integraltheorem

theorem boundY1_eq_integral {ν : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {A : Ω → Bool}
  (hA : Measurable A) (c : ℝ) (y : Ω → ℝ) : boundY1 ν A c y = ∫ ω, (treated A).indicator y ω ∂ν +
    c * ∫ ω, (treated A)ᶜ.indicator 1 ω ∂ν

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.boundY0_eq_integraltheorem

theorem boundY0_eq_integral {ν : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {A : Ω → Bool}
  (hA : Measurable A) (c : ℝ) (y : Ω → ℝ) : boundY0 ν A c y = ∫ ω, (treated A)ᶜ.indicator y ω ∂ν +
    c * ∫ ω, (treated A).indicator 1 ω ∂ν

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.boundY1_eq_weightedtheorem

theorem boundY1_eq_weighted [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {A : Ω → Bool} (hA : Measurable A) {s : Set Ω}
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℝ) {y : Ω → ℝ} (hy : Integrable y μ) :
  boundY1 μ A c y = μ.real s * boundY1 (μ[|s]) A c y + μ.real sᶜ * boundY1 (μ[|sᶜ]) A c y

The no-assumption Manski bound for E[Y1] is the P(s)-weighted average of the Manski bounds computed within s and within sᶜ.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.boundY0_eq_weightedtheorem

theorem boundY0_eq_weighted [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {A : Ω → Bool} (hA : Measurable A) {s : Set Ω}
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℝ) {y : Ω → ℝ} (hy : Integrable y μ) :
  boundY0 μ A c y = μ.real s * boundY0 (μ[|s]) A c y + μ.real sᶜ * boundY0 (μ[|sᶜ]) A c y

The no-assumption Manski bound for E[Y0] is the P(s)-weighted average of the Manski bounds computed within s and within sᶜ.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.Icc_max_min_subsettheorem

theorem Icc_max_min_subset {p q a b c d : ℝ} (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hpq : p + q = 1) :
  Icc (max a b) (min c d) ⊆ Icc (p * a + q * b) (p * c + q * d)

Convex combinations lie between the minimum and the maximum: if p, q ≥ 0 and p + q = 1, then [max a b, min c d] ⊆ [p a + q b, p c + q d].

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.preimage_false_eq_compltheorem

theorem preimage_false_eq_compl (Zi : Ω → Bool) : Zi ⁻¹' {false} = (Zi ⁻¹' {true})ᶜ

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.meanY1_mem_Icctheorem

theorem meanY1_mem_Icc [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable A) (hm : m ∈ boundedModels lo hi)
  (hMI : MeanIndependent μ Zi m) (hz : ∀ z, μ (Zi ⁻¹' {z}) ≠ 0) :
  meanY1 μ m ∈ Icc
    (max (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo (observed A m))
      (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo (observed A m)))
    (min (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi (observed A m))
      (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi (observed A m)))

**Mean-independence bounds on E[Y1]** (Manski 1990). If the potential outcomes are mean independent of the instrument Zi, both instrument values have positive probability, and the potential outcomes are bounded in [lo, hi], then E[Y1] lies in the intersection over z of the worst-case bounds computed within {Zi = z}: between max_z of the conditional lower bounds and min_z of the conditional upper bounds.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.meanY0_mem_Icctheorem

theorem meanY0_mem_Icc [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable A) (hm : m ∈ boundedModels lo hi)
  (hMI : MeanIndependent μ Zi m) (hz : ∀ z, μ (Zi ⁻¹' {z}) ≠ 0) :
  meanY0 μ m ∈ Icc
    (max (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo (observed A m))
      (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo (observed A m)))
    (min (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi (observed A m))
      (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi (observed A m)))

**Mean-independence bounds on E[Y0]** (Manski 1990): the intersection over z of the worst-case bounds for E[Y0] computed within {Zi = z}.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.ate_mem_Icctheorem

theorem ate_mem_Icc [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable A) (hm : m ∈ boundedModels lo hi)
  (hMI : MeanIndependent μ Zi m) (hz : ∀ z, μ (Zi ⁻¹' {z}) ≠ 0) :
  ate μ m ∈ Icc
    (max (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo (observed A m))
        (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo (observed A m)) -
      min (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi (observed A m))
        (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi (observed A m)))
    (min (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi (observed A m))
        (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi (observed A m)) -
      max (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo (observed A m))
        (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo (observed A m)))

Mean-independence bounds on the average treatment effect: combining the bounds on E[Y1] and E[Y0], max_z L1_z - min_z U0_z ≤ E[Y1] - E[Y0] ≤ min_z U1_z - max_z L0_z.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.Icc_meanY1_subsettheorem

theorem Icc_meanY1_subset [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable A) (hZ : Measurable Zi)
  {y : Ω → ℝ} (hy : Integrable y μ) :
  Icc (max (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo y) (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo y))
      (min (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi y) (boundY1 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi y)) ⊆
    Icc (boundY1 μ A lo y) (boundY1 μ A hi y)

The mean-independence bounds on E[Y1] are at least as tight as the no-assumption Manski bounds: for a probability measure and a measurable binary Zi, the interval [max_z L_z, min_z U_z] is contained in [L, U], because L and U are the P(Zi = z)-weighted averages of L_z and U_z.

CausalInference.MeanIndependence.Icc_meanY0_subsettheorem

theorem Icc_meanY0_subset [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable A) (hZ : Measurable Zi)
  {y : Ω → ℝ} (hy : Integrable y μ) :
  Icc (max (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A lo y) (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A lo y))
      (min (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {true}]) A hi y) (boundY0 (μ[|Zi ⁻¹' {false}]) A hi y)) ⊆
    Icc (boundY0 μ A lo y) (boundY0 μ A hi y)

The mean-independence bounds on E[Y0] are at least as tight as the no-assumption Manski bounds.

CausalInference.map_cond_applytheorem

theorem map_cond_apply {α β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β] {μ : Measure α}
  {f : α → β} (hf : Measurable f) {S T : Set β} (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hT : MeasurableSet T) :
  (μ.map f)[T | S] = μ[f ⁻¹' T | f ⁻¹' S]

Conditioning commutes with pushforward: (f_* μ)[T | S] = μ[f⁻¹ T | f⁻¹ S].

CausalInference.IVBounds.obsEventdefinition

def obsEvent (d : Bool) (B : Set ℝ) : Set (Bool × Bool × ℝ)

The observed event {D = d, Y ∈ B} in the space Bool × Bool × ℝ of observed data (Z, D, Y).

CausalInference.IVBounds.measurableSet_obsEventtheorem

theorem measurableSet_obsEvent (d : Bool) {B : Set ℝ} (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  MeasurableSet (obsEvent d B)

CausalInference.IVModel.cond_obs_eventtheorem

theorem cond_obs_event [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) {z : Bool}
  (hz : μ (M.instrumentEq z) ≠ 0) (d : Bool) {B : Set ℝ} (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  μ[{ω | M.Dobs ω = d ∧ M.Yobs ω ∈ B} | M.instrumentEq z] =
    μ {ω | M.D z ω = d ∧ M.Y z d ω ∈ B}

Under instrument independence and P(Z = z) ≠ 0, P(D = d, Y ∈ B | Z = z) = P(D z = d, Y z d ∈ B) for every measurable B.

CausalInference.IVModel.instrumentalInequality_treatedtheorem

theorem instrumentalInequality_treated [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {B : Set ℝ}
  (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  μ[{ω | M.Dobs ω = true ∧ M.Yobs ω ∈ B} | M.instrumentEq false] ≤
    μ[{ω | M.Dobs ω = true ∧ M.Yobs ω ∈ B} | M.instrumentEq true]

Instrumental inequality for the treated (Balke and Pearl 1997, in the form implied by monotonicity). Under exclusion, instrument independence, monotonicity and P(Z = z) ≠ 0 for both z, for every measurable outcome set B: P(Y ∈ B, D = 1 | Z = 0) ≤ P(Y ∈ B, D = 1 | Z = 1). The difference is the probability that a complier has treated outcome in B. For a binary outcome take B = {y}.

CausalInference.IVModel.instrumentalInequality_untreatedtheorem

theorem instrumentalInequality_untreated [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {B : Set ℝ}
  (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  μ[{ω | M.Dobs ω = false ∧ M.Yobs ω ∈ B} | M.instrumentEq true] ≤
    μ[{ω | M.Dobs ω = false ∧ M.Yobs ω ∈ B} | M.instrumentEq false]

Instrumental inequality for the untreated. Under the same assumptions, for every measurable outcome set B: P(Y ∈ B, D = 0 | Z = 1) ≤ P(Y ∈ B, D = 0 | Z = 0). The difference is the probability that a complier has untreated outcome in B.

CausalInference.IVModel.law_instrumentalInequality_treatedtheorem

theorem law_instrumentalInequality_treated [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {B : Set ℝ}
  (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  (μ.map M.observed)[obsEvent true B | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {false}] ≤
    (μ.map M.observed)[obsEvent true B | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {true}]

The instrumental inequality for the treated, stated for the observed-data law ν = μ.map (Z, Dobs, Yobs): ν(D = 1, Y ∈ B | Z = 0) ≤ ν(D = 1, Y ∈ B | Z = 1).

CausalInference.IVModel.law_instrumentalInequality_untreatedtheorem

theorem law_instrumentalInequality_untreated [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hE : M.Exclusion μ)
  (hI : M.InstrumentIndependence μ) (hM : M.Monotonicity μ)
  (h₁ : μ (M.instrumentEq true) ≠ 0) (h₀ : μ (M.instrumentEq false) ≠ 0) {B : Set ℝ}
  (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
  (μ.map M.observed)[obsEvent false B | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {true}] ≤
    (μ.map M.observed)[obsEvent false B | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {false}]

The instrumental inequality for the untreated, stated for the observed-data law: ν(D = 0, Y ∈ B | Z = 1) ≤ ν(D = 0, Y ∈ B | Z = 0).

CausalInference.IVBounds.binaryModeldefinition

def binaryModel : IVModel (Space 3)

A binary IV model on Bool × Fin 3 used to produce a violating observed-data law: a fair coin Z is drawn independently of a unit uniform on {0, 1, 2}; units 0 and 1 take the treatment exactly when Z = 1, unit 2 exactly when Z = 0; the outcome is binary, equal to 1 only for unit 2 when treated.

CausalInference.IVBounds.binaryModel_independencetheorem

theorem binaryModel_independence : binaryModel.InstrumentIndependence (P 3)

CausalInference.IVBounds.binaryModel_instrument_ne_zerotheorem

theorem binaryModel_instrument_ne_zero (z : Bool) : P 3 (binaryModel.instrumentEq z) ≠ 0

CausalInference.IVBounds.violatingLawdefinition

def violatingLaw : Measure (Bool × Bool × ℝ)

A concrete observed-data law on Bool × Bool × ℝ with a binary outcome: the law of (Z, Dobs, Yobs) in binaryModel.

CausalInference.IVBounds.violatingLaw_lttheorem

theorem violatingLaw_lt :
  violatingLaw[obsEvent true {1} | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {true}] <
    violatingLaw[obsEvent true {1} | Prod.fst ⁻¹' {false}]

The law violatingLaw violates the instrumental inequality for the treated with B = {1}: P(D = 1, Y = 1 | Z = 1) = 0 < P(D = 1, Y = 1 | Z = 0).

CausalInference.IVBounds.not_assumptions_of_law_eq_violatingLawtheorem

theorem not_assumptions_of_law_eq_violatingLaw {Ω' : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω']
  {μ' : Measure Ω'} [IsFiniteMeasure μ'] (M' : IVModel Ω')
  (hlaw : μ'.map M'.observed = violatingLaw) :
  ¬ (M'.Exclusion μ' ∧ M'.InstrumentIndependence μ' ∧ M'.Monotonicity μ')

The IV assumptions are falsifiable. No binary IV model, on any probability space, whose observed-data law is violatingLaw satisfies the exclusion restriction, instrument independence and monotonicity. (Both instrument values have probability 1 / 2 under violatingLaw, so the positivity conditions of the instrumental inequalities hold automatically.)

CausalInference.InstrumentalVariables.LinearIV

CausalInference/InstrumentalVariables/LinearIV.lean · 374 lines · 20 public theorems · 8 definitions · imports InstrumentalVariables.Bounds

Linear instrumental variables. The linear structural model Y = α + β D + U with real treatment, instrument and error, as in Wooldridge (Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data), and its relation to the Wald ratio (Wald 1940) and to the local average treatment effect of Angrist, Imbens and Rubin (1996). This model is separate from the binary potential outcomes model CausalInference.IVModel; the two meet only through the covariance ratio.

Sources: Angrist, Imbens and Rubin (1996); Wald (1940); Wooldridge

Public declarations (28)

CausalInference.LinearIVModelstructure

structure LinearIVModel (Ω : Type*)

A linear structural model Y = α + β D + U with a real treatment D, a real instrument Z and a real structural error U on a sample space Ω. The parameter of interest is the slope β, the effect of a unit change of D on Y, the same for every unit.

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.Ydefinition

def Y (ω : Ω) : ℝ

The outcome, given by the structural equation Y = α + β D + U.

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.SecondMomentsstructure

structure SecondMoments : Prop

Finite second moments of the treatment, the instrument and the error.

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.Exogeneitydefinition

def Exogeneity : Prop

Exogeneity of the instrument: Cov(Z, U) = 0.

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.Relevancedefinition

def Relevance : Prop

Relevance of the instrument: Cov(Z, D) ≠ 0.

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.covariance_Ytheorem

theorem covariance_Y [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {W : Ω → ℝ} (hW : MemLp W 2 μ)
  (hD : MemLp L.D 2 μ) (hU : MemLp L.U 2 μ) :
  cov[W, L.Y; μ] = L.β * cov[W, L.D; μ] + cov[W, L.U; μ]

Covariance of any square integrable W with the outcome: Cov(W, Y) = β Cov(W, D) + Cov(W, U).

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.covRatio_eqtheorem

theorem covRatio_eq [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : L.SecondMoments μ) (hR : L.Relevance μ) :
  cov[L.Z, L.Y; μ] / cov[L.Z, L.D; μ] = L.β + cov[L.Z, L.U; μ] / cov[L.Z, L.D; μ]

The IV estimand with its bias. With finite second moments and a relevant instrument, Cov(Z, Y) / Cov(Z, D) = β + Cov(Z, U) / Cov(Z, D).

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.beta_eq_covRatiotheorem

theorem beta_eq_covRatio [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : L.SecondMoments μ)
  (hE : L.Exogeneity μ) (hR : L.Relevance μ) :
  L.β = cov[L.Z, L.Y; μ] / cov[L.Z, L.D; μ]

Identification of the structural slope by linear IV (see Wooldridge, Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data). With finite second moments, exogeneity Cov(Z, U) = 0 and relevance Cov(Z, D) ≠ 0, β = Cov(Z, Y) / Cov(Z, D).

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.covRatio_ne_betatheorem

theorem covRatio_ne_beta [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : L.SecondMoments μ) (hR : L.Relevance μ)
  (hU : cov[L.Z, L.U; μ] ≠ 0) : cov[L.Z, L.Y; μ] / cov[L.Z, L.D; μ] ≠ L.β

If exogeneity fails (Cov(Z, U) ≠ 0) but the instrument is relevant, the IV ratio differs from β, by exactly Cov(Z, U) / Cov(Z, D).

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.olsSlope_eqtheorem

theorem olsSlope_eq [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hD : MemLp L.D 2 μ) (hU : MemLp L.U 2 μ)
  (hV : Var[L.D; μ] ≠ 0) :
  cov[L.D, L.Y; μ] / Var[L.D; μ] = L.β + cov[L.D, L.U; μ] / Var[L.D; μ]

Ordinary least squares under endogeneity. With finite second moments of D and U and Var(D) ≠ 0, the OLS slope is Cov(D, Y) / Var(D) = β + Cov(D, U) / Var(D).

CausalInference.LinearIVModel.olsSlope_ne_betatheorem

theorem olsSlope_ne_beta [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hD : MemLp L.D 2 μ) (hU : MemLp L.U 2 μ)
  (hV : Var[L.D; μ] ≠ 0) (hDU : cov[L.D, L.U; μ] ≠ 0) :
  cov[L.D, L.Y; μ] / Var[L.D; μ] ≠ L.β

OLS is biased when the treatment is correlated with the error: if Cov(D, U) ≠ 0 and Var(D) ≠ 0, the OLS slope differs from β.

CausalInference.LinearIV.covariance_boolToRealtheorem

theorem covariance_boolToReal [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Zb : Ω → Bool} (hZ : Measurable Zb)
  {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : Integrable X μ) :
  cov[fun ω ↦ IVModel.boolToReal (Zb ω), X; μ] =
    μ.real (Zb ⁻¹' {true}) * μ.real (Zb ⁻¹' {false}) *
      (∫ ω, X ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {true}] - ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {false}])

Covariance with a binary instrument: for Zb : Ω → Bool measurable, coded as 0/1, and X integrable, Cov(Z, X) = P(Z = 1) P(Z = 0) (E[X | Z = 1] - E[X | Z = 0]), with conditional means taken against μ[|Z = z]. Only integrability of X is needed, since Z is bounded.

CausalInference.LinearIV.covRatio_eq_waldRatiotheorem

theorem covRatio_eq_waldRatio [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Zb : Ω → Bool} (hZ : Measurable Zb)
  {X D : Ω → ℝ} (hX : Integrable X μ) (hD : Integrable D μ) (h₁ : μ (Zb ⁻¹' {true}) ≠ 0)
  (h₀ : μ (Zb ⁻¹' {false}) ≠ 0)
  (hR : ∫ ω, D ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {true}] - ∫ ω, D ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {false}] ≠ 0) :
  cov[fun ω ↦ IVModel.boolToReal (Zb ω), X; μ] / cov[fun ω ↦ IVModel.boolToReal (Zb ω), D; μ] =
    (∫ ω, X ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {true}] - ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {false}]) /
      (∫ ω, D ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {true}] - ∫ ω, D ω ∂μ[|Zb ⁻¹' {false}])

Covariance ratio equals the Wald ratio for a binary instrument (Wald 1940). If both instrument values have positive probability and the first stage E[D | Z = 1] - E[D | Z = 0] is nonzero, then for integrable X and D, Cov(Z, X) / Cov(Z, D) = (E[X | Z = 1] - E[X | Z = 0]) / (E[D | Z = 1] - E[D | Z = 0]).

CausalInference.IVModel.integrable_Yobstheorem

theorem integrable_Yobs (hY : ∀ z, Integrable (M.YD z) μ) : Integrable M.Yobs μ

With integrable responses Y z (D z) for both instrument values the observed outcome is integrable.

CausalInference.IVModel.integrable_Yobs_of_integrabletheorem

theorem integrable_Yobs_of_integrable (hY : ∀ z d, Integrable (M.Y z d) μ) :
  Integrable M.Yobs μ

With integrable potential outcomes the observed outcome is integrable.

CausalInference.IVModel.integrable_DobsRealtheorem

theorem integrable_DobsReal [IsFiniteMeasure μ] : Integrable M.DobsReal μ

The observed treatment, coded as a real number, is integrable for a finite measure.

CausalInference.IVModel.covRatio_eq_waldtheorem

theorem covRatio_eq_wald [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hY : ∀ z, Integrable (M.YD z) μ)
  (hR : M.Relevance μ) :
  cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.Yobs; μ] / cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.DobsReal; μ] =
    M.wald μ

The linear IV estimand of a binary IV model is the Wald ratio. With integrable responses Y z (D z) and relevance (which includes P(Z = z) ≠ 0 for both z), the covariance ratio Cov(Z, Yobs) / Cov(Z, Dobs) (with Z and Dobs coded as 0/1) equals M.wald μ.

CausalInference.IVModel.LATEAssumptions.covRatio_eq_complierEffecttheorem

theorem LATEAssumptions.covRatio_eq_complierEffect [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {M : IVModel Ω}
  (h : M.LATEAssumptions μ) (z : Bool) :
  cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.Yobs; μ] / cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.DobsReal; μ] =
    M.complierEffect μ z

The linear IV estimand under the LATE assumptions is the complier effect. Under exclusion, instrument independence, monotonicity, relevance (including positive mass of both instrument arms) and integrable responses Y z (D z), the covariance ratio Cov(Z, Yobs) / Cov(Z, Dobs) equals the complier average causal effect E[Y z 1 - Y z 0 | compliers], which in general differs from the average treatment effect (see IVCounterexample.ate_not_identified).

CausalInference.IVModel.LATEAssumptions.covRatio_eq_of_homogeneoustheorem

theorem LATEAssumptions.covRatio_eq_of_homogeneous [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {M : IVModel Ω}
  (h : M.LATEAssumptions μ) {z : Bool} {β : ℝ} (hβ : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, M.effect z ω = β) :
  cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.Yobs; μ] / cov[fun ω ↦ boolToReal (M.Z ω), M.DobsReal; μ] =
    β

Homogeneous effects. If, in addition to the LATE assumptions, the unit-level effect Y z 1 - Y z 0 equals a constant β almost surely, then the linear IV estimand Cov(Z, Yobs) / Cov(Z, Dobs) equals β. Without homogeneity it is only the complier effect (LATEAssumptions.covRatio_eq_complierEffect).

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.coinsdefinition

def coins : Measure (Bool × Bool)

Two independent fair coins: the uniform distribution on Bool × Bool.

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.integral_coinstheorem

theorem integral_coins (f : Bool × Bool → ℝ) :
  ∫ x, f x ∂coins =
    (f (true, true) + f (true, false) + f (false, true) + f (false, false)) / 4

The mean of any function of two fair coins is its average over the four outcomes.

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.memLp_coinstheorem

theorem memLp_coins {f : Bool × Bool → ℝ} (hf : ∀ x, |f x| ≤ 2) : MemLp f 2 coins

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.endogenousdefinition

def endogenous : LinearIVModel (Bool × Bool)

A valid instrument with an endogenous treatment: Z and V are independent fair coins (coded 0/1), the treatment is D = Z + V, the structural error is U = V, and Y = D + U (α = 0, β = 1). Then Cov(Z, U) = 0 but Cov(D, U) ≠ 0.

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.endogenous_secondMomentstheorem

theorem endogenous_secondMoments : endogenous.SecondMoments coins

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.endogenous_iv_olstheorem

theorem endogenous_iv_ols :
  endogenous.Exogeneity coins ∧ endogenous.Relevance coins ∧
    cov[endogenous.Z, endogenous.Y; coins] / cov[endogenous.Z, endogenous.D; coins] =
      endogenous.β ∧
    cov[endogenous.D, endogenous.Y; coins] / Var[endogenous.D; coins] = 3 / 2 ∧
    cov[endogenous.D, endogenous.Y; coins] / Var[endogenous.D; coins] ≠ endogenous.β

**IV recovers β while OLS does not.** In endogenous the instrument is exogenous and relevant, so Cov(Z, Y) / Cov(Z, D) = β = 1, while the OLS slope is Cov(D, Y) / Var(D) = 3 / 2 ≠ β.

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.invaliddefinition

def invalid : LinearIVModel (Bool × Bool)

An instrument violating exogeneity: Z is a fair coin (coded 0/1) and D = U = Z, with Y = U (α = 0, β = 0). Then Cov(Z, U) ≠ 0.

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.invalid_secondMomentstheorem

theorem invalid_secondMoments : invalid.SecondMoments coins

CausalInference.LinearIVExample.invalid_iv_biasedtheorem

theorem invalid_iv_biased :
  ¬ invalid.Exogeneity coins ∧ invalid.Relevance coins ∧
    cov[invalid.Z, invalid.Y; coins] / cov[invalid.Z, invalid.D; coins] =
      invalid.β + cov[invalid.Z, invalid.U; coins] / cov[invalid.Z, invalid.D; coins] ∧
    cov[invalid.Z, invalid.Y; coins] / cov[invalid.Z, invalid.D; coins] = 1 ∧
    cov[invalid.Z, invalid.Y; coins] / cov[invalid.Z, invalid.D; coins] ≠ invalid.β

Counterexample: exogeneity fails. In invalid the instrument is relevant but Cov(Z, U) = 1 / 4 ≠ 0; the IV ratio equals β + Cov(Z, U) / Cov(Z, D) = 1, which differs from β = 0.

Interference

Partial interference, the direct, indirect, total and overall effects of Hudgens and Halloran, and two-stage randomization.

CausalInference.Interference.Basic

CausalInference/Interference/Basic.lean · 183 lines · 10 public theorems · 9 definitions

Potential outcomes under interference. Under interference the potential outcome of a unit is indexed by the whole assignment vector: Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ, where Y a i is the outcome of unit i when the units are assigned according to a (true means treated). This file sets up the basic restrictions on Y.

Sources: Hudgens and Halloran (2008); Aronow and Samii (2017)

Public declarations (19)

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterferencedefinition

def NoInterference (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) : Prop

No interference (the no-interference component of SUTVA): the outcome of unit i depends on the assignment vector only through the unit's own assignment a i.

CausalInference.Interference.PartialInterferencedefinition

def PartialInterference (g : ι → G) (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) : Prop

Partial interference for the partition of units into groups given by g : ι → G: the outcome of unit i depends on the assignment vector only through the assignments of the units in the same group as i.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.partialInterferencetheorem

theorem NoInterference.partialInterference {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (g : ι → G) : PartialInterference g Y

No interference implies partial interference for every partition into groups.

CausalInference.Interference.unitOutcomedefinition

def unitOutcome (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (i : ι) (t : Bool) : ℝ

The classical unit level potential outcome of unit i under treatment t: the outcome when every unit receives t. Under no interference this is the outcome of i under any assignment that gives i the treatment t.

CausalInference.Interference.y1definition

def y1 (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : ℝ

The classical potential outcome under treatment, y1 i.

CausalInference.Interference.y0definition

def y0 (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : ℝ

The classical potential outcome under control, y0 i.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.eq_unitOutcometheorem

theorem NoInterference.eq_unitOutcome {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (a : ι → Bool) (i : ι) : Y a i = unitOutcome Y i (a i)

Under no interference the outcome of unit i under any assignment vector a is the classical potential outcome of i at its own treatment a i.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.eq_itetheorem

theorem NoInterference.eq_ite {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (a : ι → Bool) (i : ι) : Y a i = if a i then y1 Y i else y0 Y i

Under no interference, Y a i = y1 i if i is treated and Y a i = y0 i otherwise.

CausalInference.Interference.ExposureDependsdefinition

def ExposureDepends (f : (ι → Bool) → ι → E) (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) : Prop

The outcomes depend on the assignment vector only through the exposure mapping f : (ι → Bool) → ι → E: two assignment vectors giving unit i the same exposure give i the same outcome.

CausalInference.Interference.exposureDepends_iff_existstheorem

theorem exposureDepends_iff_exists (f : (ι → Bool) → ι → E) (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) :
  ExposureDepends f Y ↔ ∃ y : ι → E → ℝ, ∀ a i, Y a i = y i (f a i)

Dependence through an exposure mapping is equivalent to the existence of exposure level potential outcomes y i e with Y a i = y i (f a i).

CausalInference.Interference.noInterference_iff_exposureDependstheorem

theorem noInterference_iff_exposureDepends (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) :
  NoInterference Y ↔ ExposureDepends (fun a i ↦ a i) Y

No interference is exposure dependence for the exposure mapping a ↦ a i.

CausalInference.Interference.groupExposuredefinition

def groupExposure [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G) (a : ι → Bool) (i : ι) : ι → Bool

The group exposure mapping for g : ι → G: unit i is exposed to the assignments of the members of its own group, with nonmembers recorded as false.

CausalInference.Interference.groupExposure_eq_ifftheorem

theorem groupExposure_eq_iff [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G) (a b : ι → Bool) (i : ι) :
  groupExposure g a i = groupExposure g b i ↔ ∀ j, g j = g i → a j = b j

Two assignment vectors give unit i the same group exposure exactly when they agree on the group of i.

CausalInference.Interference.partialInterference_iff_exposureDependstheorem

theorem partialInterference_iff_exposureDepends [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G)
  (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) :
  PartialInterference g Y ↔ ExposureDepends (groupExposure g) Y

Partial interference is exposure dependence for the group exposure mapping.

CausalInference.Interference.ExposureDepends.of_finertheorem

theorem ExposureDepends.of_finer {E' : Type*} {f : (ι → Bool) → ι → E}
  {f' : (ι → Bool) → ι → E'} {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : ExposureDepends f' Y)
  (hff' : ∀ a b i, f a i = f b i → f' a i = f' b i) : ExposureDepends f Y

If the exposure f determines the exposure f' (equal f exposures give equal f' exposures), then dependence through f' implies dependence through f.

CausalInference.Interference.stratifiedExposuredefinition

def stratifiedExposure [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G) (a : ι → Bool) (i : ι) :
  Bool × ℕ

The stratified interference exposure for the partition g : ι → G: the pair formed by the unit's own assignment and the number of treated units in its group.

CausalInference.Interference.StratifiedInterferencedefinition

def StratifiedInterference [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G)
  (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) : Prop

Stratified interference (Hudgens and Halloran): the outcome of unit i depends on the assignment vector only through the unit's own assignment and the number of treated units in the group of i. It is exposure dependence for stratifiedExposure g.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.stratifiedInterferencetheorem

theorem NoInterference.stratifiedInterference [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq G]
  {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y) (g : ι → G) :
  StratifiedInterference g Y

No interference implies stratified interference for every partition into groups.

CausalInference.Interference.StratifiedInterference.partialInterferencetheorem

theorem StratifiedInterference.partialInterference [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq G] {g : ι → G}
  {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : StratifiedInterference g Y) : PartialInterference g Y

Stratified interference implies partial interference for the same partition: an assignment of the group of i determines both a i and the number treated in that group.

CausalInference.Interference.Counterexamples

CausalInference/Interference/Counterexamples.lean · 114 lines · 5 public theorems · 2 definitions · imports Interference.TwoStage

A two-unit counterexample under interference. Two units, each of which responds only if both units are treated: Y a i = 1 if a 0 = a 1 = true and Y a i = 0 otherwise.

Sources: Hudgens and Halloran (2008)

Public declarations (7)

CausalInference.Interference.twoUnitYdefinition

def twoUnitY (a : Fin 2 → Bool) (_i : Fin 2) : ℝ

Potential outcomes of two units that respond only when both are treated.

CausalInference.Interference.twoUnitY_not_noInterferencetheorem

theorem twoUnitY_not_noInterference : ¬ NoInterference twoUnitY

The two-unit outcomes violate no interference.

CausalInference.Interference.twoUnitY_unit_effect_ill_definedtheorem

theorem twoUnitY_unit_effect_ill_defined :
  twoUnitY ![true, false] 0 - twoUnitY ![false, false] 0 = 0 ∧
    twoUnitY ![true, true] 0 - twoUnitY ![false, true] 0 = 1

The effect on unit 0 of switching it from control to treatment depends on the treatment of unit 1: it is 0 when unit 1 is a control and 1 when unit 1 is treated.

CausalInference.Interference.diffInMeansdefinition

def diffInMeans {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The classical difference in means: mean outcome of the treated units minus mean outcome of the control units.

CausalInference.Interference.expect_diffInMeans_completeRandomizationtheorem

theorem expect_diffInMeans_completeRandomization {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk0 : 0 < k) (hk : k < Fintype.card ι) :
  expect (completeRandomization ι k hk.le) (diffInMeans Y) =
    -directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) (completeRandomization ι k hk.le)

Under complete randomization of k among n units with 0 < k < n, the expected difference in means is ȳ(1; ψ) - ȳ(0; ψ), the negative of the Hudgens and Halloran direct effect DE(ψ) = ȳ(0; ψ) - ȳ(1; ψ), for arbitrary potential outcomes Y (interference allowed).

CausalInference.Interference.twoUnitY_diffInMeans_biasedtheorem

theorem twoUnitY_diffInMeans_biased :
  expect (completeRandomization (Fin 2) 1 (by simp)) (diffInMeans twoUnitY) = 0 ∧
    (Fintype.card (Fin 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (y1 twoUnitY i - y0 twoUnitY i) = 1

Under complete randomization of one of the two units the expected difference in means is 0, while the average effect of treating both units versus treating neither is 1; the difference in means is biased for that effect.

CausalInference.Interference.twoUnitY_diffInMeans_netheorem

theorem twoUnitY_diffInMeans_ne :
  expect (completeRandomization (Fin 2) 1 (by simp)) (diffInMeans twoUnitY) ≠
    (Fintype.card (Fin 2) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (y1 twoUnitY i - y0 twoUnitY i)

The bias itself: under complete randomization of one of the two units, the expected difference in means differs from the average effect of treating both units versus neither.

CausalInference.Interference.PartialInterference

CausalInference/Interference/PartialInterference.lean · 584 lines · 34 public theorems · 16 definitions · imports Interference.Basic

Partial interference: allocation strategies and the Hudgens and Halloran estimands. A group is a finite set of individuals ι; its potential outcomes Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ are indexed by the group's assignment vector. A population is a finite family of groups κ : G → Type* with group outcomes Y g; indexing each group's outcomes by that group's own assignment vector is exactly the partial interference assumption, and PartialInterference.eq_groupOutcome makes the passage from a population wide outcome function precise.

Sources: Hudgens and Halloran (2008)

Public declarations (50)

CausalInference.Interference.extendFromGroupdefinition

def extendFromGroup [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G) (c : G) (b : {j // g j = c} → Bool) :
  ι → Bool

The assignment vector on the whole population obtained from an assignment b of the members of group c, giving every nonmember the assignment false.

CausalInference.Interference.groupOutcomedefinition

def groupOutcome [DecidableEq G] (g : ι → G) (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (c : G)
  (b : {j // g j = c} → Bool) (j : {j // g j = c}) : ℝ

The group level potential outcomes of group c induced by population wide potential outcomes Y: the outcome of member j when the group is assigned b and every other unit is assigned false.

CausalInference.Interference.PartialInterference.eq_groupOutcometheorem

theorem PartialInterference.eq_groupOutcome [DecidableEq G] {g : ι → G}
  {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : PartialInterference g Y) (a : ι → Bool) (j : ι) :
  Y a j = groupOutcome g Y (g j) (fun k ↦ a k) ⟨j, rfl⟩

Under partial interference the population wide outcome of unit j is the group level outcome of its group, evaluated at the restriction of the assignment vector to that group.

CausalInference.Interference.AllocationStrategystructure

structure AllocationStrategy (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

An allocation strategy for a finite group ι: a probability weight function on the group's assignment vectors (nonnegative weights summing to one).

CausalInference.Interference.AllocationStrategy.treatProbdefinition

def treatProb (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool) : ℝ

The probability under ψ that individual i receives treatment t.

CausalInference.Interference.AllocationStrategy.treatProb_nonnegtheorem

theorem treatProb_nonneg (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool) :
  0 ≤ ψ.treatProb i t

CausalInference.Interference.AllocationStrategy.treatProb_false_add_truetheorem

theorem treatProb_false_add_true (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) :
  ψ.treatProb i false + ψ.treatProb i true = 1

The probabilities of control and of treatment of an individual add up to one.

CausalInference.Interference.AllocationStrategy.Positivedefinition

def Positive (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) : Prop

Positivity of an allocation strategy: every individual receives each treatment with positive probability, so that every conditional average ȳ_i(t; ψ) is a genuine conditional mean.

CausalInference.Interference.indivSumdefinition

def indivSum (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool) : ℝ

The weighted sum ∑_{a : a i = t} ψ(a) Y a i, the numerator of ȳ_i(t; ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.indivAvgdefinition

def indivAvg (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι)
  (t : Bool) : ℝ

The individual average potential outcome ȳ_i(t; ψ) of Hudgens and Halloran: the average of Y a i over assignment vectors drawn from ψ, conditionally on a i = t. It is a genuine conditional average only when ψ.treatProb i t > 0; when that probability is zero the value is the meaningless 0 / 0 = 0. Every causal contrast built on it below assumes positivity (AllocationStrategy.Positive or the relevant cell); the only results stated without it are identities in which this average is multiplied by its probability, so that its value is irrelevant (treatProb_mul_indivAvg, indivMarginal_eq).

CausalInference.Interference.indivMarginaldefinition

def indivMarginal (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) : ℝ

The marginal individual average potential outcome ȳ_i(ψ) = ∑_a ψ(a) Y a i.

CausalInference.Interference.treatProb_mul_indivAvgtheorem

theorem treatProb_mul_indivAvg (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι)
  (t : Bool) : ψ.treatProb i t * indivAvg Y ψ i t = indivSum Y ψ i t

ψ.treatProb i t * ȳ_i(t; ψ) is the numerator indivSum. When the probability is zero both sides are zero, because every weight in the numerator is zero; the value assigned to ȳ_i(t; ψ) in that case plays no role.

CausalInference.Interference.indivMarginal_eqtheorem

theorem indivMarginal_eq (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) :
  indivMarginal Y ψ i = ψ.treatProb i false * indivAvg Y ψ i false +
    ψ.treatProb i true * indivAvg Y ψ i true

The marginal individual average is the mixture ȳ_i(ψ) = P(a i = 0) ȳ_i(0; ψ) + P(a i = 1) ȳ_i(1; ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.le_indivAvgtheorem

theorem le_indivAvg (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool)
  (hp : 0 < ψ.treatProb i t) {m : ℝ} (hm : ∀ a, a i = t → m ≤ Y a i) :
  m ≤ indivAvg Y ψ i t

Interpretation of ȳ_i(t; ψ) as a conditional mean, lower bound: if i receives t with positive probability and m ≤ Y a i for every assignment vector with a i = t, then m ≤ ȳ_i(t; ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.indivAvg_letheorem

theorem indivAvg_le (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool)
  (hp : 0 < ψ.treatProb i t) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ a, a i = t → Y a i ≤ M) :
  indivAvg Y ψ i t ≤ M

Interpretation of ȳ_i(t; ψ) as a conditional mean, upper bound: if i receives t with positive probability and Y a i ≤ M for every assignment vector with a i = t, then ȳ_i(t; ψ) ≤ M.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.indivAvg_eqtheorem

theorem NoInterference.indivAvg_eq {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (t : Bool) (hp : 0 < ψ.treatProb i t) :
  indivAvg Y ψ i t = unitOutcome Y i t

Under no interference the individual average potential outcome is the classical potential outcome, provided the treatment t has positive probability for i.

CausalInference.Interference.groupAvgdefinition

def groupAvg (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (t : Bool) :
  ℝ

The group average potential outcome ȳ(t; ψ) = n⁻¹ ∑_i ȳ_i(t; ψ) of a group of n individuals. It is a genuine average only for a nonempty group (n > 0); every causal statement about it below assumes [Nonempty ι].

CausalInference.Interference.groupMarginaldefinition

def groupMarginal (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) : ℝ

The marginal group average potential outcome ȳ(ψ) = n⁻¹ ∑_i ȳ_i(ψ), a genuine average only for a nonempty group.

CausalInference.Interference.popAvgdefinition

def popAvg (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (t : Bool) : ℝ

The population average potential outcome: the average over the N groups of the group averages, N⁻¹ ∑_g ȳ_g(t; ψ_g), where group g follows the strategy ψ g. It is a genuine average only when there is at least one group and every group is nonempty; every causal statement about it below assumes [Nonempty G] and [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)].

CausalInference.Interference.popMarginaldefinition

def popMarginal (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) : ℝ

The marginal population average potential outcome N⁻¹ ∑_g ȳ_g(ψ_g), a genuine average only for a nonempty family of nonempty groups.

CausalInference.Interference.directEffectdefinition

def directEffect (ybar : Bool → S → ℝ) (ψ : S) : ℝ

The direct effect DE(ψ) = ȳ(0; ψ) - ȳ(1; ψ) for a family of average potential outcomes ybar t ψ (sign convention of Hudgens and Halloran).

CausalInference.Interference.indirectEffectdefinition

def indirectEffect (ybar : Bool → S → ℝ) (φ ψ : S) : ℝ

The indirect effect IE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(0; φ) - ȳ(0; ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.totalEffectdefinition

def totalEffect (ybar : Bool → S → ℝ) (φ ψ : S) : ℝ

The total effect TE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(0; φ) - ȳ(1; ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.overallEffectdefinition

def overallEffect (ymarg : S → ℝ) (φ ψ : S) : ℝ

The overall effect OE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(φ) - ȳ(ψ) for a family of marginal averages.

CausalInference.Interference.totalEffect_eq_directEffect_add_indirectEffecttheorem

theorem totalEffect_eq_directEffect_add_indirectEffect (ybar : Bool → S → ℝ) (φ ψ : S) :
  totalEffect ybar φ ψ = directEffect ybar ψ + indirectEffect ybar φ ψ

The total effect is the sum of the direct effect under ψ and the indirect effect: TE(φ, ψ) = DE(ψ) + IE(φ, ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.overallEffect_eq_of_mixturetheorem

theorem overallEffect_eq_of_mixture (ybar : Bool → S → ℝ) (ymarg : S → ℝ) (p : S → ℝ)
  (hmix : ∀ ψ, ymarg ψ = (1 - p ψ) * ybar false ψ + p ψ * ybar true ψ) (φ ψ : S) :
  overallEffect ymarg φ ψ =
    indirectEffect ybar φ ψ - p φ * directEffect ybar φ + p ψ * directEffect ybar ψ

If the marginal average is the mixture ȳ(ψ) = (1 - p_ψ) ȳ(0; ψ) + p_ψ ȳ(1; ψ) for every strategy, then OE(φ, ψ) = IE(φ, ψ) - p_φ DE(φ) + p_ψ DE(ψ).

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.indirectEffect_eq_zerotheorem

theorem NoInterference.indirectEffect_eq_zero {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (i : ι) (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (hφ : 0 < φ.treatProb i false)
  (hψ : 0 < ψ.treatProb i false) :
  indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ = 0

Under no interference the individual indirect effect vanishes, provided i is a control with positive probability under both strategies.

CausalInference.Interference.indivTotalEffect_eqtheorem

theorem indivTotalEffect_eq (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (i : ι) (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι)
  (_hφ : φ.Positive) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  totalEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ =
    directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) ψ +
      indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ

Individual level: TE_i(φ, ψ) = DE_i(ψ) + IE_i(φ, ψ). The identity is algebraic; positivity of both strategies is assumed so that every average in it is a genuine conditional mean, and is not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.groupTotalEffect_eqtheorem

theorem groupTotalEffect_eq [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι)
  (_hφ : φ.Positive) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  totalEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) ψ +
      indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ

Group level: TE(φ, ψ) = DE(ψ) + IE(φ, ψ) for the group averages of a nonempty group. The identity is algebraic; positivity is assumed so that every average in it is meaningful, and is not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.groupDirectEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem groupDirectEffect_eq_average [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) ψ =
    (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) ψ

The group direct effect is the average of the individual direct effects (nonempty group, positive strategy; positivity is not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.groupIndirectEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem groupIndirectEffect_eq_average [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (_hφ : φ.Positive) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ

The group indirect effect is the average of the individual indirect effects (nonempty group, positive strategies; positivity is not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.groupTotalEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem groupTotalEffect_eq_average [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (_hφ : φ.Positive) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  totalEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, totalEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ

The group total effect is the average of the individual total effects (nonempty group, positive strategies; positivity is not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.groupOverallEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem groupOverallEffect_eq_average [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) :
  overallEffect (groupMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, overallEffect (fun s ↦ indivMarginal Y s i) φ ψ

The group overall effect is the average of the individual overall effects (nonempty group; no conditional average is involved, so no positivity is needed).

CausalInference.Interference.indivOverallEffect_eqtheorem

theorem indivOverallEffect_eq (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (i : ι) (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι)
  (_hφ : φ.Positive) (_hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  overallEffect (fun s ↦ indivMarginal Y s i) φ ψ =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ ψ -
      φ.treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ +
      ψ.treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) ψ

Individual level decomposition of the overall effect: OE_i(φ, ψ) = IE_i(φ, ψ) - p_i(φ) DE_i(φ) + p_i(ψ) DE_i(ψ), where p_i(ψ) is the probability that i is treated under ψ. The underlying mixture identity indivMarginal_eq holds for any strategies; positivity is assumed so that the direct and indirect effects are genuine contrasts of conditional means, and is not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.groupMarginal_eq_of_treatProbtheorem

theorem groupMarginal_eq_of_treatProb (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (s : AllocationStrategy ι)
  (p : ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, s.treatProb i true = p) :
  groupMarginal Y s = (1 - p) * groupAvg Y s false + p * groupAvg Y s true

If every individual of the group is treated with the same probability p s under each strategy s (as under complete randomization of a fixed number), the marginal group average is the mixture ȳ(s) = (1 - p s) ȳ(0; s) + p s ȳ(1; s). This is a probability weighted identity: it holds for any value of an undefined conditional average and for an empty group.

CausalInference.Interference.groupOverallEffect_eq_sumtheorem

theorem groupOverallEffect_eq_sum [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (hφ : φ.Positive) (hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  overallEffect (groupMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ -
      (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i, φ.treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) φ +
      (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i, ψ.treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) ψ

Group level decomposition of the overall effect in full generality, with unit specific treatment probabilities p_i(φ), p_i(ψ): OE(φ, ψ) = IE(φ, ψ) - n⁻¹ ∑_i p_i(φ) DE_i(φ) + n⁻¹ ∑_i p_i(ψ) DE_i(ψ), for a nonempty group and positive strategies.

CausalInference.Interference.groupOverallEffect_eqtheorem

theorem groupOverallEffect_eq [Nonempty ι] (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ)
  (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (_hφpos : φ.Positive) (_hψpos : ψ.Positive)
  (pφ pψ : ℝ) (hφ : ∀ i, φ.treatProb i true = pφ) (hψ : ∀ i, ψ.treatProb i true = pψ) :
  overallEffect (groupMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ -
      pφ * directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ +
      pψ * directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) ψ

Group level decomposition of the overall effect, OE(φ, ψ) = IE(φ, ψ) - p_φ DE(φ) + p_ψ DE(ψ), under the assumption that each strategy treats every individual with the same probability: the special case of groupOverallEffect_eq_sum in which all p_i agree, proved from the mixture identity. Nonemptiness and positivity are assumed so that the averages and effects are meaningful; they are not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.directEffect_eqtheorem

theorem NoInterference.directEffect_eq {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ} (h : NoInterference Y)
  (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (i : ι) (h0 : 0 < ψ.treatProb i false)
  (h1 : 0 < ψ.treatProb i true) :
  directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg Y s i t) ψ = y0 Y i - y1 Y i

Reduction to the classical case: under no interference, if i receives both treatments with positive probability, the individual direct effect is y0 i - y1 i (control minus treatment).

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.groupDirectEffect_eqtheorem

theorem NoInterference.groupDirectEffect_eq [Nonempty ι] {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ}
  (h : NoInterference Y) (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) ψ =
    (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (y0 Y i - y1 Y i)

Reduction to the classical case: under no interference and positivity, the group direct effect is n⁻¹ ∑_i (y0 i - y1 i), minus the finite population average treatment effect.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.groupIndirectEffect_eq_zerotheorem

theorem NoInterference.groupIndirectEffect_eq_zero [Nonempty ι] {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ}
  (h : NoInterference Y) (φ ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (hφ : φ.Positive) (hψ : ψ.Positive) :
  indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg Y s t) φ ψ = 0

Reduction to the classical case: under no interference and positivity of both strategies, the group indirect effect vanishes.

CausalInference.Interference.popTotalEffect_eqtheorem

theorem popTotalEffect_eq [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (_hφ : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (_hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  totalEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) ψ +
      indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ

Population level: TE(φ, ψ) = DE(ψ) + IE(φ, ψ) for the population averages. The identity is algebraic; nonemptiness and positivity are assumed so that every average is meaningful, and are not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.popDirectEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem popDirectEffect_eq_average [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (_hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ *
      ∑ g, directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (ψ g)

The population direct effect is the average of the group direct effects (nonempty groups, positive strategies; these hypotheses are not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.popIndirectEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem popIndirectEffect_eq_average [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (_hφ : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (_hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ *
      ∑ g, indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (φ g) (ψ g)

The population indirect effect is the average of the group indirect effects (nonempty groups, positive strategies; these hypotheses are not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.popTotalEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem popTotalEffect_eq_average [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (_hφ : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (_hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  totalEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ *
      ∑ g, totalEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (φ g) (ψ g)

The population total effect is the average of the group total effects (nonempty groups, positive strategies; these hypotheses are not used in the proof).

CausalInference.Interference.popOverallEffect_eq_averagetheorem

theorem popOverallEffect_eq_average [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) :
  overallEffect (popMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g, overallEffect (groupMarginal (Y g)) (φ g) (ψ g)

The population overall effect is the average of the group overall effects (nonempty groups).

CausalInference.Interference.popOverallEffect_eq_sumtheorem

theorem popOverallEffect_eq_sum [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (hφ : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  overallEffect (popMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ -
      (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g, (Fintype.card (κ g) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i, (φ g).treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg (Y g) s i t) (φ g) +
      (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g, (Fintype.card (κ g) : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i, (ψ g).treatProb i true * directEffect (fun t s ↦ indivAvg (Y g) s i t) (ψ g)

Population level decomposition of the overall effect in full generality, with unit specific treatment probabilities: OE(φ, ψ) equals IE(φ, ψ) - N⁻¹ ∑_g n_g⁻¹ ∑_i p_gi(φ_g) DE_gi(φ_g) + N⁻¹ ∑_g n_g⁻¹ ∑_i p_gi(ψ_g) DE_gi(ψ_g), the equal weight average over groups of groupOverallEffect_eq_sum.

CausalInference.Interference.popOverallEffect_eq_of_groupTreatProbtheorem

theorem popOverallEffect_eq_of_groupTreatProb [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (hφpos : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (hψpos : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) (pφ pψ : G → ℝ)
  (hφ : ∀ g i, (φ g).treatProb i true = pφ g) (hψ : ∀ g i, (ψ g).treatProb i true = pψ g) :
  overallEffect (popMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g,
      (indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (φ g) (ψ g) -
        pφ g * directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (φ g) +
        pψ g * directEffect (fun t s ↦ groupAvg (Y g) s t) (ψ g))

Population level decomposition of the overall effect with group specific treatment probabilities: if strategy φ g treats every member of group g with probability pφ g and likewise ψ g with pψ g, then OE(φ, ψ) is the average over groups of IE_g(φ_g, ψ_g) - pφ g DE_g(φ_g) + pψ g DE_g(ψ_g).

CausalInference.Interference.popOverallEffect_eqtheorem

theorem popOverallEffect_eq [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (_hφpos : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive) (_hψpos : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) (pφ pψ : ℝ)
  (hφ : ∀ g i, (φ g).treatProb i true = pφ) (hψ : ∀ g i, (ψ g).treatProb i true = pψ) :
  overallEffect (popMarginal Y) φ ψ =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ -
      pφ * directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ +
      pψ * directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) ψ

Population level decomposition of the overall effect, OE(φ, ψ) = IE(φ, ψ) - p_φ DE(φ) + p_ψ DE(ψ), under the assumption that each of the two strategy families treats every individual of every group with the same probability: the special case of popOverallEffect_eq_of_groupTreatProb with probabilities common to all groups. Nonemptiness and positivity are assumed so that every average is meaningful; they are not used in the proof.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.popIndirectEffect_eq_zerotheorem

theorem NoInterference.popIndirectEffect_eq_zero [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  {Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ} (h : ∀ g, NoInterference (Y g))
  (φ ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hφ : ∀ g, (φ g).Positive)
  (hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) φ ψ = 0

Reduction to the classical case at the population level: if every group satisfies no interference and every strategy is positive, the population indirect effect vanishes.

CausalInference.Interference.NoInterference.popDirectEffect_eqtheorem

theorem NoInterference.popDirectEffect_eq [Nonempty G] [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  {Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ} (h : ∀ g, NoInterference (Y g))
  (ψ : (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hψ : ∀ g, (ψ g).Positive) :
  directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) ψ =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ *
      ∑ g, (Fintype.card (κ g) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, (y0 (Y g) i - y1 (Y g) i)

Reduction to the classical case at the population level: if every group satisfies no interference and every strategy is positive, the population direct effect is the average over groups of minus the finite population average treatment effect of each group, N⁻¹ ∑_g n_g⁻¹ ∑_i (y0 i - y1 i).

CausalInference.Interference.TwoStage

CausalInference/Interference/TwoStage.lean · 1010 lines · 56 public theorems · 17 definitions · imports Interference.PartialInterference

Two-stage randomization and unbiased estimation under partial interference. The design based setting of Hudgens and Halloran: potential outcomes are fixed and the only randomness is in the assignment. Expectations are finite weighted sums.

Sources: Hudgens and Halloran (2008)

Public declarations (73)

CausalInference.Interference.FixedCountstructure

structure FixedCount (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (t : Bool) (m : ℕ) : Prop

A strategy with a fixed number of units receiving t: with probability one exactly m > 0 units receive t, and each unit receives t with probability m / n. Complete randomization has this property for t = true (when 0 < k) and for t = false (when k < n).

Under a fixed count strategy every unit receives t with positive probability, so every conditional average ȳ_j(t; ψ) entering the group estimand is a genuine conditional mean.

CausalInference.Interference.groupEstimatordefinition

def groupEstimator (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) (t : Bool) (a : ι → Bool) : ℝ

The estimator Ŷ(t; ψ) of Hudgens and Halloran for the group average potential outcome: the mean observed outcome Y a j among the units j with a j = t, where a is the realized assignment vector.

CausalInference.Interference.expect_groupEstimator_of_fixedtheorem

theorem expect_groupEstimator_of_fixed (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) {ψ : AllocationStrategy ι}
  {t : Bool} {m : ℕ} (h : FixedCount ψ t m) :
  expect ψ (groupEstimator Y t) = groupAvg Y ψ t

Unbiasedness of the group estimator: if the strategy ψ assigns t to exactly m > 0 units with probability one and assigns t to every unit with probability m / n, then E_ψ[Ŷ(t; ψ)] = ȳ(t; ψ). The fixed count hypothesis already makes the group nonempty (FixedCount.nonempty) and every conditional average in ȳ(t; ψ) genuine (FixedCount.treatProb_pos).

CausalInference.Interference.expect_groupEstimator_completeRandomization_truetheorem

theorem expect_groupEstimator_completeRandomization_true (Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ) {k : ℕ}
  (hk0 : 0 < k) (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card ι) :
  expect (completeRandomization ι k hk) (groupEstimator Y true) =
    groupAvg Y (completeRandomization ι k hk) true

Under complete randomization of k treated units with 0 < k ≤ n, the mean outcome of the treated is unbiased for the group average potential outcome under treatment.

  (hk : k < Fintype.card ι) :
  expect (completeRandomization ι k hk.le) (groupEstimator Y false) =
    groupAvg Y (completeRandomization ι k hk.le) false

Under complete randomization of k treated units with k < n, the mean outcome of the controls is unbiased for the group average potential outcome under control.

theorem pairProb_of_perm_invariant (ψ : AllocationStrategy ι) (t : Bool) (m : ℕ)
  (hperm : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) a, ψ.prob (a ∘ σ) = ψ.prob a)
  (hsupp : ∀ a, ψ.prob a ≠ 0 → numWith a t = m) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) :

    m * (m - 1) / (Fintype.card ι * (Fintype.card ι - 1))

Second order inclusion probabilities: if a strategy is invariant under permutations of the units and assigns t to exactly m units with probability one, then two distinct units both receive t with probability m (m - 1) / (n (n - 1)).

CausalInference.Interference.finitePopVardefinition

def finitePopVar (y : ι → ℝ) : ℝ

The finite population variance S² = (n - 1)⁻¹ ∑_j (y j - ȳ)² of the values y j, where ȳ = n⁻¹ ∑_j y j. It is meaningful for n ≥ 2.

  (hperm : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm ι) a, ψ.prob (a ∘ σ) = ψ.prob a)
  (hsupp : ∀ a, ψ.prob a ≠ 0 → numWith a t = m) (hm0 : 0 < m) (hmn : m < Fintype.card ι)
  (y : ι → ℝ) :
  variance ψ (fun a ↦ (∑ j ∈ univ.filter (fun j ↦ a j = t), y j) / m) =
    (1 / m - 1 / Fintype.card ι) * finitePopVar y

The variance of a sample mean under a permutation invariant fixed count design. If ψ is invariant under permutations of the units and assigns t to exactly m units with probability one, 0 < m < n, then the mean of fixed values y j over the units receiving t has variance (1/m - 1/n) S², with S² the finite population variance of y.

theorem StratifiedInterference.eq_indivAvg_completeRandomization {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ}
  (hY : StratifiedInterference (fun _ : ι ↦ ()) Y) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card ι)

CausalInference.Interference.variance_groupEstimator_completeRandomizationtheorem

theorem variance_groupEstimator_completeRandomization {Y : (ι → Bool) → ι → ℝ}
  (hY : StratifiedInterference (fun _ : ι ↦ ()) Y) {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card ι)

    (1 / m - 1 / Fintype.card ι) *
      finitePopVar (fun j ↦ indivAvg Y (completeRandomization ι k hk) j t)

Variance of the group estimator under stratified interference (Hudgens and Halloran). The group ι is completely randomized with k treated, stratified interference holds within the group, and exactly m units receive t, with 0 < m < n. Then Var(Ŷ(t; ψ)) = (1/m - 1/n) S², where S² is the finite population variance of the values ȳ_j(t; ψ); under stratified interference these are the outcomes of the units when receiving t with k treated in the group.

theorem sum_prod_mul_apply {α : G → Type*} [∀ g, Fintype (α g)] (q : ∀ g, α g → ℝ)
  (hq : ∀ g, ∑ x, q g x = 1) (h : G) (X : α h → ℝ) :
  ∑ A : (∀ g, α g), (∏ g, q g (A g)) * X (A h) = ∑ x, q h x * X x
