CausalInference.Interference.JointDesignstructure

structure JointDesign (G : Type*) [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] (κ : G → Type*)
  [∀ g, Fintype (κ g)] [∀ g, DecidableEq (κ g)]

A general two-stage design: an arbitrary joint probability law of the arm vector S : G → Bool (the first stage) and the population assignment A (the second stage). The assignments of different groups may be dependent, even given S.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expectdefinition

def expect (Q : JointDesign G κ) (F : (G → Bool) → ((g : G) → κ g → Bool) → ℝ) : ℝ

The expectation ∑_{S, A} Q(S, A) F(S, A) under a joint two-stage design.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.firstStagedefinition

def firstStage (Q : JointDesign G κ) : AllocationStrategy G

The first stage of a joint design: the marginal law of the arm vector S.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.Compatibledefinition

def Compatible (Q : JointDesign G κ) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) :
  Prop

The second stage condition of Hudgens and Halloran for a joint design: for every group g, arm b and group assignment z, P(S g = b, A g = z) = P(S g = b) * (strat b g)(z); that is, the law of the assignment of group g given that g is in arm b is the strategy strat b g. Nothing is assumed about the dependence between groups.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.prob_eq_zero_of_firstStagetheorem

theorem prob_eq_zero_of_firstStage (Q : JointDesign G κ) {S : G → Bool}
  (h : Q.firstStage.prob S = 0) (A : (g : G) → κ g → Bool) : Q.prob S A = 0

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_armAveragetheorem

theorem expect_armAverage (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat) {b : Bool}
  {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount Q.firstStage b c) (X : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → ℝ) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ (∑ g ∈ univ.filter (fun g ↦ S g = b), X g (A g)) / numWith S b) =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g, Interference.expect (strat b g) (X g)

The key computation for a general two-stage design. Suppose the first stage assigns exactly c > 0 groups to arm b with probability one, each group with probability c / N, and the second stage is compatible with strat. Then the average over the groups in arm b of group level statistics X g (A g) has expectation N⁻¹ ∑_g E_{strat b g}[X g].

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpectdefinition

def twoStageExpect (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (F : (G → Bool) → ((g : G) → κ g → Bool) → ℝ) : ℝ

The expectation of F S A under two-stage randomization. In the first stage the vector S : G → Bool assigning each group to one of two arms is drawn from P1; in the second stage, given S, the groups are randomized independently, group g drawing its assignment vector A g from the strategy strat (S g) g of its arm. In Hudgens and Halloran the arm true uses the strategy ψ and the arm false the strategy φ.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_subtheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_sub (P1 : AllocationStrategy G)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (F F' : (G → Bool) → ((g : G) → κ g → Bool) → ℝ) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (fun S A ↦ F S A - F' S A) =
    twoStageExpect P1 strat F - twoStageExpect P1 strat F'

The two-stage expectation of a difference is the difference of the expectations.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_addtheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_add (P1 : AllocationStrategy G)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (F F' : (G → Bool) → ((g : G) → κ g → Bool) → ℝ) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (fun S A ↦ F S A + F' S A) =
    twoStageExpect P1 strat F + twoStageExpect P1 strat F'

The two-stage expectation is additive in the estimator.

The two-stage expectation commutes with multiplication by a constant.

For each arm vector the second stage weights sum to one.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_consttheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_const (P1 : AllocationStrategy G)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (r : ℝ) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (fun _ _ ↦ r) = r

The two-stage design with independent groups given the arm vector, as a joint design: Q(S, A) = P1(S) ∏_g (strat (S g) g)(A g).

twoStageExpect is the expectation under the product design.

  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) {b : Bool} {c : ℕ}
  (h1 : FixedCount P1 b c) : FixedCount (productDesign P1 strat).firstStage b c

A fixed count first stage P1 gives a fixed count first stage of the product design.

CausalInference.Interference.productDesign_compatibletheorem

theorem productDesign_compatible (P1 : AllocationStrategy G)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) :
  (productDesign P1 strat).Compatible strat

The product design satisfies the second stage condition JointDesign.Compatible.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_armAveragetheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_armAverage (P1 : AllocationStrategy G)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) {b : Bool} {c : ℕ}
  (h1 : FixedCount P1 b c) (X : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → ℝ) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat
      (fun S A ↦ (∑ g ∈ univ.filter (fun g ↦ S g = b), X g (A g)) / numWith S b) =
    (Fintype.card G : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ g, expect (strat b g) (X g)

The key computation for two-stage randomization. Suppose the first stage assigns exactly c > 0 groups to arm b with probability one and assigns each group to arm b with probability c / N. Then the average over the groups in arm b of group level statistics X g (A g) has expectation N⁻¹ ∑_g E_{strat b g}[X g]. This is the instance of JointDesign.expect_armAverage for the product design.

CausalInference.Interference.popEstimatordefinition

def popEstimator (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (b t : Bool)
  (S : G → Bool) (A : (g : G) → κ g → Bool) : ℝ

The population estimator Ŷ(t; ·) for arm b of Hudgens and Halloran: the average, over the groups assigned to arm b by the first stage, of the group estimators Ŷ_g(t).

CausalInference.Interference.popMarginalEstimatordefinition

def popMarginalEstimator (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (b : Bool)
  (S : G → Bool) (A : (g : G) → κ g → Bool) : ℝ

The population marginal estimator for arm b: the average, over the groups assigned to arm b, of the mean observed outcome of the group.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_subtheorem

theorem expect_sub (Q : JointDesign G κ) (F F' : (G → Bool) → ((g : G) → κ g → Bool) → ℝ) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ F S A - F' S A) = Q.expect F - Q.expect F'

The expectation under a joint design is additive.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_popEstimatortheorem

theorem expect_popEstimator (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat)
  {b t : Bool} {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount Q.firstStage b c) {m : G → ℕ}
  (h2 : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) t (m g)) :
  Q.expect (popEstimator Y b t) = popAvg Y (strat b) t

Unbiasedness of the population estimator under a general two-stage design Q, the assignments of different groups being allowed to be dependent. First stage: exactly c > 0 groups are in arm b, each with probability c / N. Second stage: Q is compatible with strat (JointDesign.Compatible), and in each group g the strategy of arm b assigns t to exactly m g > 0 units, each with probability m g / n_g. Then E[Ŷ(t; ψ_b)] = ȳ(t; ψ_b). The fixed count hypotheses make every group and the set of groups nonempty and every conditional average genuine (FixedCount.nonempty, FixedCount.treatProb_pos).

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_popMarginalEstimatortheorem

theorem expect_popMarginalEstimator [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat)
  {b : Bool} {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount Q.firstStage b c) :
  Q.expect (popMarginalEstimator Y b) = popMarginal Y (strat b)

Unbiasedness of the population marginal estimator under a general two-stage design compatible with strat, for nonempty groups, with the fixed count first stage condition and no condition on the second stage strategies.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_directEffecttheorem

theorem expect_directEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat) {b : Bool}
  {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount Q.firstStage b c) {m₀ m₁ : G → ℕ}
  (h₀ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) false (m₀ g)) (h₁ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) true (m₁ g)) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y b false S A - popEstimator Y b true S A) =
    directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat b)

Unbiased estimation of the population direct effect of the strategies of arm b under a general compatible two-stage design.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_indirectEffecttheorem

theorem expect_indirectEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat)
  {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount Q.firstStage false c₀) (h1₁ : FixedCount Q.firstStage true c₁)
  {mφ mψ : G → ℕ} (hφ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat false g) false (mφ g))
  (hψ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat true g) false (mψ g)) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y false false S A - popEstimator Y true false S A) =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population indirect effect IE(φ, ψ), with φ the strategies of arm false and ψ those of arm true, under a general compatible two-stage design.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_totalEffecttheorem

theorem expect_totalEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) (Q : JointDesign G κ)
  (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) (hQ : Q.Compatible strat)
  {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount Q.firstStage false c₀) (h1₁ : FixedCount Q.firstStage true c₁)
  {mφ mψ : G → ℕ} (hφ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat false g) false (mφ g))
  (hψ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat true g) true (mψ g)) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y false false S A - popEstimator Y true true S A) =
    totalEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population total effect TE(φ, ψ) under a general compatible two-stage design.

CausalInference.Interference.JointDesign.expect_overallEffecttheorem

theorem expect_overallEffect [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)] (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (Q : JointDesign G κ) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  (hQ : Q.Compatible strat) {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount Q.firstStage false c₀)
  (h1₁ : FixedCount Q.firstStage true c₁) :
  Q.expect (fun S A ↦ popMarginalEstimator Y false S A - popMarginalEstimator Y true S A) =
    overallEffect (popMarginal Y) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population overall effect OE(φ, ψ) under a general compatible two-stage design, for nonempty groups.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_popEstimatortheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_popEstimator (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  {b t : Bool} {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount P1 b c) {m : G → ℕ}
  (h2 : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) t (m g)) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (popEstimator Y b t) = popAvg Y (strat b) t

Unbiasedness of the population estimator under two-stage randomization with independent groups given the arm vector (the instance productDesign of JointDesign.expect_popEstimator). First stage: exactly c > 0 groups are assigned to arm b, each with probability c / N. Second stage: in each group g the strategy of arm b assigns t to exactly m g > 0 units, each with probability m g / n_g. Then E[Ŷ(t; ψ_b)] = ȳ(t; ψ_b), the population average potential outcome under the strategies of arm b.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_popMarginalEstimatortheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_popMarginalEstimator [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)]
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  {b : Bool} {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount P1 b c) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (popMarginalEstimator Y b) = popMarginal Y (strat b)

Unbiasedness of the population marginal estimator under two-stage randomization, for nonempty groups, with the same first stage condition and no condition on the second stage strategies.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_popEstimator_completeRandomizationtheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_popEstimator_completeRandomization
  (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ) {c : ℕ} (hc : c ≤ Fintype.card G)
  (k : Bool → G → ℕ) (hk : ∀ b g, k b g ≤ Fintype.card (κ g)) (b t : Bool)
  (hcb : if b then 0 < c else c < Fintype.card G)
  (hkb : ∀ g, if t then 0 < k b g else k b g < Fintype.card (κ g)) :
  twoStageExpect (completeRandomization G c hc)
      (fun b g ↦ completeRandomization (κ g) (k b g) (hk b g)) (popEstimator Y b t) =
    popAvg Y (fun g ↦ completeRandomization (κ g) (k b g) (hk b g)) t

The fully specified design of Hudgens and Halloran. First stage: complete randomization of c of the N groups to arm true, the others going to arm false. Second stage: in arm b group g is completely randomized with k b g of its n_g members treated, independently across groups. The population estimator for arm b and treatment t is unbiased, E[Ŷ(t; ψ_b)] = ȳ(t; ψ_b), provided arm b is not empty (0 < c for b = true, c < N for b = false) and, in every group, treatment t is given to at least one unit in arm b (0 < k b g for t = true, k b g < n_g for t = false).

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_directEffecttheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_directEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g)) {b : Bool}
  {c : ℕ} (h1 : FixedCount P1 b c) {m₀ m₁ : G → ℕ}
  (h₀ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) false (m₀ g)) (h₁ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat b g) true (m₁ g)) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y b false S A - popEstimator Y b true S A) =
    directEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat b)

Unbiased estimation of the population direct effect DE(ψ_b) = ȳ(0; ψ_b) - ȳ(1; ψ_b) of the strategies of arm b by Ŷ(0; ψ_b) - Ŷ(1; ψ_b), under the fixed count conditions of twoStageExpect_popEstimator for arm b and both treatments.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_indirectEffecttheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_indirectEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount P1 false c₀) (h1₁ : FixedCount P1 true c₁) {mφ mψ : G → ℕ}
  (hφ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat false g) false (mφ g))
  (hψ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat true g) false (mψ g)) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat
      (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y false false S A - popEstimator Y true false S A) =
    indirectEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population indirect effect IE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(0; φ) - ȳ(0; ψ), with φ the strategies of arm false and ψ those of arm true, by Ŷ(0; φ) - Ŷ(0; ψ), under the fixed count conditions for both arms and treatment false.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_totalEffecttheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_totalEffect (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount P1 false c₀) (h1₁ : FixedCount P1 true c₁) {mφ mψ : G → ℕ}
  (hφ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat false g) false (mφ g))
  (hψ : ∀ g, FixedCount (strat true g) true (mψ g)) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat
      (fun S A ↦ popEstimator Y false false S A - popEstimator Y true true S A) =
    totalEffect (fun t s ↦ popAvg Y s t) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population total effect TE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(0; φ) - ȳ(1; ψ) by Ŷ(0; φ) - Ŷ(1; ψ), under the fixed count conditions for control in arm false and treatment in arm true.

CausalInference.Interference.twoStageExpect_overallEffecttheorem

theorem twoStageExpect_overallEffect [∀ g, Nonempty (κ g)] (Y : (g : G) → (κ g → Bool) → κ g → ℝ)
  (P1 : AllocationStrategy G) (strat : Bool → (g : G) → AllocationStrategy (κ g))
  {c₀ c₁ : ℕ} (h1₀ : FixedCount P1 false c₀) (h1₁ : FixedCount P1 true c₁) :
  twoStageExpect P1 strat
      (fun S A ↦ popMarginalEstimator Y false S A - popMarginalEstimator Y true S A) =
    overallEffect (popMarginal Y) (strat false) (strat true)

Unbiased estimation of the population overall effect OE(φ, ψ) = ȳ(φ) - ȳ(ψ) by the difference of the marginal estimators, for nonempty groups, under the first stage conditions for both arms.

CausalInference.Interference.DesignBridge

CausalInference/Interference/DesignBridge.lean · 130 lines · 8 public theorems · 3 definitions · imports Designs.Randomized.Complete, Interference.TwoStage

Randomized designs and allocation strategies. The design-based framework of CausalInference.Randomized describes an assignment law by a Design (a finite summation set with weights), while the interference files describe it by an AllocationStrategy (a weight on every assignment vector). This file converts between the two and shows that the conversions preserve expectations and treatment probabilities, that complete randomization is the same law on both sides, and that without interference the assignment-indexed outcomes are the observed outcomes of classical potential outcomes. Source: M. G. Hudgens and M. E. Halloran (2008), Toward causal inference with interference, Journal of the American Statistical Association 103; Imbens and Rubin (2015), Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences.

Sources: Imbens and Rubin (2015); Hudgens and Halloran (2008)

Mediation

Controlled and natural effects, the decompositions of the total effect, the mediation formula, and a cross-world counterexample.

CausalInference.Mediation.Basic

CausalInference/Mediation/Basic.lean · 200 lines · 9 public theorems · 9 definitions

Mediation: potential outcomes and effect definitions. We fix a binary treatment A : Ω → Bool (false is control, true is treatment), mediator potential outcomes M a : Ω → 𝓜 and joint potential outcomes Y a m : Ω → ℝ. The nested (cross world) potential outcome is Y a (M a') ω = Y a (M a' ω) ω.

Sources: Robins and Greenland (1992); Pearl (2001); VanderWeele (2015)

Public declarations (18)

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModelstructure

structure MediationModel (Ω 𝓜 : Type*)

A mediation model on a sample space Ω with mediator space 𝓜: a binary treatment A, mediator potential outcomes M a and joint potential outcomes Y a m. No assumption is attached to the structure; every assumption is a hypothesis of the theorem that needs it.

CausalInference.Mediation.condMeandefinition

def condMean {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) (s : Set Ω)
  (f : Ω → ℝ) : ℝ

The mean of f under μ conditioned on the event s, that is ∫ f ∂μ[|s]. The value is a conditional mean only when s is measurable with 0 < μ s < ∞ and f is integrable on s. When μ s = 0 (or μ s = ∞) the conditioned measure is zero and this value is 0. Every theorem of the library that interprets condMean μ s f assumes a finite measure (in fact a probability measure), a measurable event s, and positivity of s whenever the conditional mean enters with a nonzero weight, so this convention never carries a result.

CausalInference.Mediation.condMean_eqtheorem

theorem condMean_eq {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) (s : Set Ω) (f : Ω → ℝ) :
  condMean μ s f = (μ.real s)⁻¹ * ∫ ω in s, f ω ∂μ

The conditional mean is the restricted integral divided by the probability of the event.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nesteddefinition

def nested (a a' : Bool) (ω : Ω) : ℝ

The nested potential outcome Y a (M a'): the outcome under treatment a with the mediator set to the value it would take under treatment a'. It is cross world when a ≠ a'.

theorem Yobs_of_A_eq {a : Bool} {ω : Ω} (h : P.A ω = a) : P.Yobs ω = P.nested a a ω

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.Yobs_of_A_eq_of_Mobs_eqtheorem

theorem Yobs_of_A_eq_of_Mobs_eq {a : Bool} {m : 𝓜} {ω : Ω} (h : P.A ω = a)

On the event A = a, Mobs = m the observed outcome equals Y a m.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.A_inter_Mobs_eqtheorem

theorem A_inter_Mobs_eq (a : Bool) (m : 𝓜) :
  P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m} = P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.M a ⁻¹' {m}

The events A = a, Mobs = m and A = a, M a = m coincide.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nested_eq_sumtheorem

theorem nested_eq_sum [Fintype 𝓜] (a a' : Bool) (ω : Ω) :
  P.nested a a' ω = ∑ m, (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}).indicator (P.Y a m) ω

For a finite mediator, the nested outcome Y a (M a') is the sum over mediator values m of Y a m restricted to the event M a' = m.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.cdedefinition

def cde (μ : Measure Ω) (m : 𝓜) : ℝ

The controlled direct effect CDE(m) = E[Y 1 m - Y 0 m]. It is a causal mean only when μ is a probability measure; every theorem that interprets it assumes so.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.tedefinition

def te (μ : Measure Ω) : ℝ

The total effect TE = E[Y 1 (M 1) - Y 0 (M 0)]. It is a causal mean only when μ is a probability measure; every theorem that interprets it assumes so.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.ndedefinition

def nde (μ : Measure Ω) (a' : Bool) : ℝ

The natural direct effect NDE(a') = E[Y 1 (M a') - Y 0 (M a')], with the mediator held at its value under a'. nde μ false is the pure natural direct effect and nde μ true the total natural direct effect. It is a causal mean only when μ is a probability measure; every theorem that interprets it assumes so.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.niedefinition

def nie (μ : Measure Ω) (a : Bool) : ℝ

The natural indirect effect NIE(a) = E[Y a (M 1) - Y a (M 0)], with the treatment held at a. nie μ true is the total natural indirect effect and nie μ false the pure one. It is a causal mean only when μ is a probability measure; every theorem that interprets it assumes so.

  {μ : Measure Ω} {a a' : Bool} (hM : Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : ∀ m, Integrable (P.Y a m) μ) : Integrable (P.nested a a') μ

For a finite mediator with measurable M a', the nested outcome Y a (M a') is integrable when every Y a m is.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integrable_indicator_of_ne_zerotheorem

theorem integrable_indicator_of_ne_zero [MeasurableSpace 𝓜] [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓜]
  {μ : Measure Ω} {a a' : Bool} {m : 𝓜} (hM : Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ) :
  Integrable ((P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}).indicator (P.Y a m)) μ

The restriction of Y a m to the fiber M a' = m is integrable when Y a m is integrable or the fiber is null.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integrable_nested_of_ne_zerotheorem

theorem integrable_nested_of_ne_zero [Finite 𝓜] [MeasurableSpace 𝓜]
  [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓜] {μ : Measure Ω} {a a' : Bool} (hM : Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ) :
  Integrable (P.nested a a') μ

For a finite mediator with measurable M a', the nested outcome Y a (M a') is integrable when Y a m is integrable for every mediator value m with P(M a' = m) > 0: on a null fiber of M a' the nested outcome vanishes almost everywhere.

CausalInference.Mediation.Counterexamples

CausalInference/Mediation/Counterexamples.lean · 428 lines · 43 public theorems · 7 definitions · imports Mediation.Identification

Mediation: non-identification of the natural direct effect in a randomized model class. Two concrete mediation models on the eight point space Bool × Bool × Bool with the uniform (product) measure. Write a point as (A, U, V). In both models the treatment is the fair coin A, the mediators are M 0 = U and M 1 = V, and Y 0 m = 0. They differ only in Y 1 m: it is 1 when m = U in the first model and 1 when m ≠ U in the second.

CausalInference.Mediation.Decomposition

CausalInference/Mediation/Decomposition.lean · 172 lines · 9 public theorems · 5 definitions · imports Mediation.Basic

Mediation: decompositions of the total effect. Pure algebra on expectations of potential outcomes, with integrability as the only analytic assumption. No identification assumption appears here. Every theorem assumes a probability measure, under which the effects are means of potential outcomes.

Sources: Pearl (2001); VanderWeele (2015); VanderWeele, Vansteelandt and Robins (2014)

Public declarations (14)

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_nde_false_add_nie_truetheorem

theorem te_eq_nde_false_add_nie_true [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hd : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true false ω - P.nested false false ω) μ)
  (hi : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true true ω - P.nested true false ω) μ) :
  P.te μ = P.nde μ false + P.nie μ true

The total effect is the pure natural direct effect plus the total natural indirect effect: TE = NDE(0) + NIE(1), assuming the two component contrasts Y 1 (M 0) - Y 0 (M 0) and Y 1 (M 1) - Y 1 (M 0) are integrable. The total effect contrast is their pointwise sum.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_nde_true_add_nie_falsetheorem

theorem te_eq_nde_true_add_nie_false [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hd : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true true ω - P.nested false true ω) μ)
  (hi : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested false true ω - P.nested false false ω) μ) :
  P.te μ = P.nde μ true + P.nie μ false

The total effect is the total natural direct effect plus the pure natural indirect effect: TE = NDE(1) + NIE(0), assuming the two component contrasts Y 1 (M 1) - Y 0 (M 1) and Y 0 (M 1) - Y 0 (M 0) are integrable. The total effect contrast is their pointwise sum.

  (h11 : Integrable (P.nested true true) μ) (h10 : Integrable (P.nested true false) μ)
  (h00 : Integrable (P.nested false false) μ) :
  P.te μ = P.nde μ false + P.nie μ true

TE = NDE(0) + NIE(1) when Y 1 (M 1), Y 1 (M 0) and Y 0 (M 0) are integrable. A corollary of te_eq_nde_false_add_nie_true.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_nde_true_add_nie_false_of_integrable_nestedtheorem

theorem te_eq_nde_true_add_nie_false_of_integrable_nested [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (h11 : Integrable (P.nested true true) μ) (h01 : Integrable (P.nested false true) μ)
  (h00 : Integrable (P.nested false false) μ) :
  P.te μ = P.nde μ true + P.nie μ false

TE = NDE(1) + NIE(0) when Y 1 (M 1), Y 0 (M 1) and Y 0 (M 0) are integrable. A corollary of te_eq_nde_true_add_nie_false.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.NoInteractiondefinition

def NoInteraction (μ : Measure Ω) : Prop

No treatment and mediator interaction: for almost every unit the individual controlled direct effect Y 1 m - Y 0 m does not depend on the mediator value m.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integrable_nde_contrast_of_no_interactiontheorem

theorem integrable_nde_contrast_of_no_interaction (h : P.NoInteraction μ) (a' : Bool) (m : 𝓜)
  (hint : Integrable (fun ω => P.Y true m ω - P.Y false m ω) μ) :
  Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true a' ω - P.nested false a' ω) μ

Without treatment and mediator interaction, the natural direct effect contrast Y 1 (M a') - Y 0 (M a') is integrable as soon as one controlled contrast Y 1 m - Y 0 m is: the two agree almost everywhere.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nde_eq_cde_of_no_interactiontheorem

theorem nde_eq_cde_of_no_interaction [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : P.NoInteraction μ) (a' : Bool)
  (m : 𝓜) (_hint : Integrable (fun ω => P.Y true m ω - P.Y false m ω) μ) :
  P.nde μ a' = P.cde μ m

Without treatment and mediator interaction, the natural direct effect NDE(a') equals the controlled direct effect CDE(m) for every a' and every m. The two integrands agree almost everywhere, so the equality itself needs no analytic hypothesis; the integrability _hint of the controlled contrast Y 1 m - Y 0 m is required so that both sides are finite means rather than the value 0 that the Bochner integral assigns to a non-integrable function (the natural direct effect contrast is then integrable too, by integrable_nde_contrast_of_no_interaction).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integrable_nde_true_contrast_of_no_interactiontheorem

theorem integrable_nde_true_contrast_of_no_interaction (h : P.NoInteraction μ)
  (hint : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true false ω - P.nested false false ω) μ) :
  Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true true ω - P.nested false true ω) μ

Without treatment and mediator interaction, the total natural direct effect contrast is integrable when the pure one is: the two agree almost everywhere.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nde_true_eq_nde_false_of_no_interactiontheorem

theorem nde_true_eq_nde_false_of_no_interaction [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (h : P.NoInteraction μ)
  (_hint : Integrable (fun ω => P.nested true false ω - P.nested false false ω) μ) :
  P.nde μ true = P.nde μ false

Without treatment and mediator interaction, the pure and total natural direct effects coincide. As in nde_eq_cde_of_no_interaction the integrands agree almost everywhere; the integrability _hint of the pure natural direct effect contrast is required so that both sides are finite means (the other contrast is then integrable, by integrable_nde_true_contrast_of_no_interaction).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalMeandefinition

def interventionalMean [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) (a a' : Bool) : ℝ

The interventional mean Σ m, E[Y a m] P(M a' = m) for a finite mediator: the mean outcome under treatment a when the mediator is drawn at random, independently of everything else, from the law of M a'. It equals E[Y a (M a')] under cross world independence (see MediationModel.integral_nested_eq_interventionalMean). It is the mean of that random draw only when μ is a probability measure and M a' is measurable (so that the weights are probabilities summing to one); every theorem that interprets it assumes both.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalDirectdefinition

def interventionalDirect [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) : ℝ

The interventional direct effect: change of treatment from 0 to 1 with the mediator drawn from the law of M 0.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalIndirectdefinition

def interventionalIndirect [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) : ℝ

The interventional indirect effect: change of the mediator law from that of M 0 to that of M 1, with treatment held at 1.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalTotaldefinition

def interventionalTotal [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) : ℝ

The interventional overall effect: treatment 1 with the mediator drawn from the law of M 1, against treatment 0 with the mediator drawn from the law of M 0.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalTotal_eq_addtheorem

theorem interventionalTotal_eq_add [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] :
  P.interventionalTotal μ = P.interventionalDirect μ + P.interventionalIndirect μ

The interventional overall effect is the interventional direct effect plus the interventional indirect effect.

CausalInference.Mediation.Identification

CausalInference/Mediation/Identification.lean · 742 lines · 32 public theorems · 2 definitions · imports Mediation.Decomposition

Mediation: identification with a finite mediator. Identification of controlled direct effects, the total effect, interventional effects and natural effects from the observed law of (A, Mobs, Yobs), for a finite mediator, first without covariates and then with a finite covariate. The observed variables are defined from the potential outcomes, so consistency and composition hold by construction. Every theorem that interprets an effect or a conditional mean assumes a probability measure.

Sources: Robins and Greenland (1992); Pearl (2001); VanderWeele (2015); VanderWeele, Vansteelandt and Robins (2014)

CausalInference.Mediation.integrable_cond_of_integrabletheorem

theorem integrable_cond_of_integrable {s : Set Ω} (hf : Integrable f ν) (hs : ν s ≠ 0) :
  Integrable f ν[|s]

A function integrable under ν is integrable under ν conditioned on an event of positive measure.

CausalInference.Mediation.setIntegral_preimage_singleton_of_indepFuntheorem

theorem setIntegral_preimage_singleton_of_indepFun (hfX : IndepFun f X ν) (hX : Measurable X)
  (hf : Integrable f ν) (x : 𝓧) :
  ∫ ω in X ⁻¹' {x}, f ω ∂ν = ν.real (X ⁻¹' {x}) * ∫ ω, f ω ∂ν

If an integrable f is independent of X, the integral of f over the event X = x is the probability of that event times the mean of f.

CausalInference.Mediation.condMean_preimage_singleton_of_indepFuntheorem

theorem condMean_preimage_singleton_of_indepFun [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (hfX : IndepFun f X ν)
  (hX : Measurable X) (hf : Integrable f ν) {x : 𝓧} (hpos : ν (X ⁻¹' {x}) ≠ 0) :
  condMean ν (X ⁻¹' {x}) f = ∫ ω, f ω ∂ν

If an integrable f is independent of X and the event X = x has positive probability, conditioning on that event does not change the mean of f.

CausalInference.Mediation.integral_eq_sum_condMeantheorem

theorem integral_eq_sum_condMean [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {𝓒 : Type*} [Fintype 𝓒] [MeasurableSpace 𝓒]
  [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓒] {C : Ω → 𝓒} (hC : Measurable C) (hf : Integrable f ν) :
  ∫ ω, f ω ∂ν = ∑ c, ν.real (C ⁻¹' {c}) * condMean ν (C ⁻¹' {c}) f

Law of total expectation over a finite partition: if C takes finitely many values and f is integrable, then E[f] = Σ c, P(C = c) E[f | C = c]. Cells of probability zero contribute 0 on both sides.

CausalInference.Mediation.condMean_cond_eq_condMean_intertheorem

theorem condMean_cond_eq_condMean_inter [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {s t : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
  (ht : MeasurableSet t) (f : Ω → ℝ) : condMean ν[|s] t f = condMean ν (s ∩ t) f

Conditioning twice is conditioning on the intersection: for measurable events s and t, E[f | s][| t] = E[f | s ∩ t], that is condMean ν[|s] t f = condMean ν (s ∩ t) f.

CausalInference.Mediation.observedMediationFormuladefinition

def observedMediationFormula {𝓜 : Type*} [MeasurableSpace 𝓜] [Fintype 𝓜]
  (ρ : Measure (Bool × 𝓜 × ℝ)) (a a' : Bool) : ℝ

The mediation formula computed from a law ρ of a triple (treatment, mediator, outcome) on Bool × 𝓜 × ℝ: Σ m, E_ρ[y | a, m] ρ(m | a').

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_Y_eq_condMeantheorem

theorem integral_Y_eq_condMean [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : Bool} {m : 𝓜} (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (hM : Measurable (P.M a)) (hY : Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ)
  (hmed : IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hpos : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  ∫ ω, P.Y a m ω ∂μ = condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) P.Yobs

Single world identification of E[Y a m]: if treatment is ignorable for Y a m (Y a m ⫫ A), the mediator is ignorable for Y a m given A = a (Y a m ⫫ M a under μ[|A = a]) and the cell A = a, Mobs = m has positive probability, then E[Y a m] = E[Yobs | A = a, Mobs = m].

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.cde_eq_condMean_subtheorem

theorem cde_eq_condMean_sub [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m : 𝓜} (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a))
  (hY : ∀ a, Integrable (P.Y a m) μ) (hrandY : ∀ a, IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ)
  (hmed : ∀ a, IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hpos : ∀ a, μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.cde μ m = condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {true} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) P.Yobs -
    condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {false} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) P.Yobs

Identification of the controlled direct effect under single world assumptions only: for each treatment level a, treatment ignorability Y a m ⫫ A, mediator ignorability Y a m ⫫ M a under μ[|A = a] and positivity of the cell A = a, Mobs = m give CDE(m) = E[Yobs | A = 1, Mobs = m] - E[Yobs | A = 0, Mobs = m]. No cross world assumption is used.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.measureReal_M_eq_condtheorem

theorem measureReal_M_eq_cond [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a' : Bool} (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (_hMa' : Measurable (P.M a')) (hrandM : IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0) (m : 𝓜) :
  μ.real (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) = (μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a'}]).real (P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})

Single world identification of the mediator law: if treatment is ignorable for the mediator (M a' ⫫ A) and P(A = a') > 0, then P(M a' = m) = P(Mobs = m | A = a'). The identity itself holds for any M a', because Mathlib's IndepFun factorizes the (outer) measure of preimages; the measurability _hMa' of M a' is required so that P(M a' = m) is the probability of an event and these weights sum to one (sum_measureReal_M_eq_one). Without it the mediation formula can assign total weight larger than one.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.sum_measureReal_M_eq_onetheorem

theorem sum_measureReal_M_eq_one [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a' : Bool}
  (hM : Measurable (P.M a')) : ∑ m, μ.real (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) = 1

For a probability measure and a measurable mediator M a' with finitely many values, the probabilities P(M a' = m) sum to one.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.mediationFormuladefinition

def mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) (a a' : Bool) : ℝ

The mediation formula Σ m, E[Yobs | A = a, Mobs = m] P(Mobs = m | A = a'). It is defined for every measure; it is a functional of the observed law of (A, Mobs, Yobs) when this triple is almost everywhere measurable (mediationFormula_eq_observedMediationFormula).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.mediationFormula_eq_sum_filtertheorem

theorem mediationFormula_eq_sum_filter [Fintype 𝓜] (μ : Measure Ω) (a a' : Bool) :
  P.mediationFormula μ a a' =
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun m => μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a'}] (P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0),
      condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) P.Yobs *
        (μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a'}]).real (P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})

Only mediator values with P(Mobs = m | A = a') > 0 contribute to the mediation formula. Under treatment ignorability for M a' these are the values with P(M a' = m) > 0 (measureReal_M_eq_cond).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.interventionalMean_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem interventionalMean_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {a a' : Bool} (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a)) (hMa' : Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ)
  (hrandM : IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ)
  (hmed : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.interventionalMean μ a a' = P.mediationFormula μ a a'

Identification of the interventional mean by the mediation formula under single world assumptions only. Assume treatment ignorability for M a' with M a' measurable, P(A = a') > 0, and, for every mediator value m with P(M a' = m) > 0: integrability of Y a m, treatment ignorability Y a m ⫫ A, mediator ignorability Y a m ⫫ M a under μ[|A = a], and positivity of the cell A = a, Mobs = m.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_nested_eq_interventionalMeantheorem

theorem integral_nested_eq_interventionalMean [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a a' : Bool}
  (hM : Measurable (P.M a')) (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hcross : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a') μ) :
  ∫ ω, P.nested a a' ω ∂μ = P.interventionalMean μ a a'

Under cross world independence Y a m ⫫ M a' for every mediator value m with P(M a' = m) > 0, the nested mean E[Y a (M a')] equals the interventional mean Σ m, E[Y a m] P(M a' = m). This is the only place where a cross world assumption enters.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_nested_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem integral_nested_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a a' : Bool}
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a)) (hMa' : Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ)
  (hrandM : IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ)
  (hmed : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hcross : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a') μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  ∫ ω, P.nested a a' ω ∂μ = P.mediationFormula μ a a'

The mediation formula (Pearl 2001), finite mediator, no covariates. Assume treatment ignorability for M a' with M a' measurable, P(A = a') > 0, and, for every mediator value m with P(M a' = m) > 0: integrability of Y a m, treatment ignorability Y a m ⫫ A, mediator ignorability Y a m ⫫ M a under μ[|A = a], the cross world independence Y a m ⫫ M a' under μ, and positivity of the cell A = a, Mobs = m. Then E[Y a (M a')] = Σ m, E[Yobs | A = a, Mobs = m] P(Mobs = m | A = a'). For a = a' the weaker hypotheses of integral_nested_self_eq_mediationFormula suffice.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_nested_self_eq_condMeantheorem

theorem integral_nested_self_eq_condMean [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : Bool} (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (hrand : IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ) (hint : Integrable (P.nested a a) μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0) :
  ∫ ω, P.nested a a ω ∂μ = condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) P.Yobs

Identification of the same world nested mean E[Y a (M a)] by the observed arm mean E[Yobs | A = a], under treatment ignorability for the nested outcome (Y a (M a) ⫫ A), its integrability, and P(A = a) > 0. No mediator assumption is used.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.condMean_A_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem condMean_A_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : Bool}
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a)) (hint : Integrable (P.nested a a) μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0) :
  condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) P.Yobs = P.mediationFormula μ a a

The observed arm mean is the mediation formula on the diagonal: E[Yobs | A = a] = Σ m, E[Yobs | A = a, Mobs = m] P(Mobs = m | A = a), for measurable A and M a, P(A = a) > 0 and integrable Y a (M a). This is the law of total expectation within the arm; no ignorability assumption is used.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_nested_self_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem integral_nested_self_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : Bool}
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a)) (hrand : IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ)
  (hint : Integrable (P.nested a a) μ) (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0) :
  ∫ ω, P.nested a a ω ∂μ = P.mediationFormula μ a a

Identification of the same world nested mean by the mediation formula on the diagonal: E[Y a (M a)] = E[Yobs | A = a] = mediationFormula μ a a, under treatment ignorability for the nested outcome, its integrability, P(A = a) > 0 and measurability of M a. Neither mediator ignorability nor any cross world assumption is needed.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_condMean_subtheorem

theorem te_eq_condMean_sub [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (hrand : ∀ a, IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ) (hint : ∀ a, Integrable (P.nested a a) μ)
  (hposA : ∀ a, μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0) :
  P.te μ = condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {true}) P.Yobs - condMean μ (P.A ⁻¹' {false}) P.Yobs

Identification of the total effect from the two treatment arms: TE = E[Yobs | A = 1] - E[Yobs | A = 0], under treatment ignorability Y a (M a) ⫫ A, integrability of Y a (M a) and P(A = a) > 0 for both a.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_mediationFormula_subtheorem

theorem te_eq_mediationFormula_sub [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hA : Measurable P.A)
  (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a)) (hrand : ∀ a, IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ)
  (hint : ∀ a, Integrable (P.nested a a) μ) (hposA : ∀ a, μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0) :
  P.te μ = P.mediationFormula μ true true - P.mediationFormula μ false false

The total effect as a difference of diagonal mediation formulas: TE = mediationFormula μ 1 1 - mediationFormula μ 0 0, under the hypotheses of te_eq_condMean_sub and measurability of both mediators.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nde_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem nde_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a' : Bool}
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a))
  (hrandD : IndepFun (P.nested a' a') P.A μ) (hintD : Integrable (P.nested a' a') μ)
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y (!a') m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) P.A μ)
  (hrandM : IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ)
  (hmed : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) (P.M (!a')) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {!a'}])
  (hcross : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) (P.M a') μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → μ (P.A ⁻¹' {!a'} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.nde μ a' = P.mediationFormula μ true a' - P.mediationFormula μ false a'

Identification of the natural direct effect NDE(a') by the mediation formula: NDE(a') = Σ m, (E[Yobs | A = 1, Mobs = m] - E[Yobs | A = 0, Mobs = m]) P(Mobs = m | A = a'), written as a difference of two mediation formulas. Of the two nested means, E[Y a' (M a')] is same world and is identified by integral_nested_self_eq_mediationFormula (hypotheses hrandD, hintD); only the cross world mean E[Y (!a') (M a')] uses the hypotheses of integral_nested_eq_mediationFormula for the treatment !a', required for the mediator values m with P(M a' = m) > 0.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nie_eq_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem nie_eq_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a : Bool}
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hM : ∀ a', Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hrandD : IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ) (hintD : Integrable (P.nested a a) μ)
  (hposD : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0)
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ)
  (hrandM : IndepFun (P.M (!a)) P.A μ)
  (hmed : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hcross : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M (!a)) μ)
  (hposA : μ (P.A ⁻¹' {!a}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → μ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.nie μ a = P.mediationFormula μ a true - P.mediationFormula μ a false

Identification of the natural indirect effect NIE(a) by the mediation formula: NIE(a) = Σ m, E[Yobs | A = a, Mobs = m] (P(Mobs = m | A = 1) - P(Mobs = m | A = 0)), written as a difference of two mediation formulas. Of the two nested means, E[Y a (M a)] is same world and is identified by integral_nested_self_eq_mediationFormula (hypotheses hrandD, hintD, hposD); only the cross world mean E[Y a (M (!a))] uses the hypotheses of integral_nested_eq_mediationFormula for the mediator world !a, required for the mediator values m with P(M (!a) = m) > 0.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nde_false_eq_interventionalDirecttheorem

theorem nde_false_eq_interventionalDirect [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hM : Measurable (P.M false))
  (hY : ∀ a m, μ (P.M false ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hcross : ∀ a m, μ (P.M false ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M false) μ) :
  P.nde μ false = P.interventionalDirect μ

Under cross world independence Y a m ⫫ M 0 for both treatment levels a, the pure natural direct effect equals the interventional direct effect: NDE(0) = interventionalDirect.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nie_true_eq_interventionalIndirecttheorem

theorem nie_true_eq_interventionalIndirect [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hM : ∀ a', Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hY : ∀ a' m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y true m) μ)
  (hcross : ∀ a' m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y true m) (P.M a') μ) :
  P.nie μ true = P.interventionalIndirect μ

Under cross world independence Y 1 m ⫫ M a' for both mediator worlds a', the total natural indirect effect equals the interventional indirect effect: NIE(1) = interventionalIndirect.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.te_eq_interventionalTotaltheorem

theorem te_eq_interventionalTotal [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a))
  (hY : ∀ a m, μ (P.M a ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hcross : ∀ a m, μ (P.M a ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ) :
  P.te μ = P.interventionalTotal μ

Under the independence Y a m ⫫ M a for both treatment levels a, the total effect equals the interventional overall effect: TE = interventionalTotal.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.mediationFormula_eq_observedMediationFormulatheorem

theorem mediationFormula_eq_observedMediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] (a a' : Bool)
  (hobs : AEMeasurable (fun ω => (P.A ω, P.Mobs ω, P.Yobs ω)) μ) :
  P.mediationFormula μ a a' =
    observedMediationFormula (μ.map fun ω => (P.A ω, P.Mobs ω, P.Yobs ω)) a a'

The mediation formula depends on μ only through the observed law of (A, Mobs, Yobs), provided this triple is almost everywhere measurable: it equals observedMediationFormula of the pushforward of μ by the triple.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.mediationFormula_eq_of_map_eqtheorem

theorem mediationFormula_eq_of_map_eq [Fintype 𝓜] {Ω' : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω']
  (Q : MediationModel Ω' 𝓜) {μ' : Measure Ω'} (a a' : Bool)
  (hP : AEMeasurable (fun ω => (P.A ω, P.Mobs ω, P.Yobs ω)) μ)
  (hQ : AEMeasurable (fun ω => (Q.A ω, Q.Mobs ω, Q.Yobs ω)) μ')
  (h : μ.map (fun ω => (P.A ω, P.Mobs ω, P.Yobs ω)) =
    μ'.map (fun ω => (Q.A ω, Q.Mobs ω, Q.Yobs ω))) :
  P.mediationFormula μ a a' = Q.mediationFormula μ' a a'

Two mediation models with almost everywhere measurable observed triples and the same observed law of (A, Mobs, Yobs) have the same mediation formula.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.mediationFormula_cond_eqtheorem

theorem mediationFormula_cond_eq [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {s : Set Ω} {a a' : Bool}
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a)) :
  P.mediationFormula μ[|s] a a' =
    ∑ m, condMean μ (s ∩ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})) P.Yobs *
      (μ[|s ∩ P.A ⁻¹' {a'}]).real (P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})

Conditioning the mediation formula on a measurable event s gives the flat form Σ m, E[Yobs | s, A = a, Mobs = m] P(Mobs = m | s, A = a').

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.integral_nested_eq_sum_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem integral_nested_eq_sum_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {𝓒 : Type*} [Fintype 𝓒] [MeasurableSpace 𝓒] [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓒] {a a' : Bool}
  (C : Ω → 𝓒) (hC : Measurable C) (hA : Measurable P.A) (hMa : Measurable (P.M a))
  (hMa' : Measurable (P.M a')) (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hrandM : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hmed : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}][|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hcross : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a') μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hposA : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  ∫ ω, P.nested a a' ω ∂μ =
    ∑ c, μ.real (C ⁻¹' {c}) * P.mediationFormula μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] a a'

The mediation formula with a finite covariate C. Assume that every Y a m with P(M a' = m) > 0 is integrable under μ, and that for every covariate value c with P(C = c) > 0 the hypotheses of integral_nested_eq_mediationFormula hold under the conditioned measure μ[|C = c]: treatment ignorability for M a', P(A = a' | C = c) > 0 and, for every m with P(M a' = m | C = c) > 0, treatment ignorability for Y a m, mediator ignorability Y a m ⫫ M a given A = a, the cross world independence Y a m ⫫ M a' and positivity of the cell A = a, Mobs = m. Then E[Y a (M a')] = Σ c, P(C = c) Σ m, E[Yobs | C = c, A = a, Mobs = m] P(Mobs = m | C = c, A = a'), where the inner sum is mediationFormula under μ[|C = c] (written in this flat form by mediationFormula_cond_eq).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.cde_eq_sum_condMean_subtheorem

theorem cde_eq_sum_condMean_sub [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {𝓒 : Type*} [Fintype 𝓒]
  [MeasurableSpace 𝓒] [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓒] {m : 𝓜} (C : Ω → 𝓒) (hC : Measurable C)
  (hA : Measurable P.A) (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a)) (hY : ∀ a, Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandY : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ a, IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hmed : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ a,
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}][|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hpos : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ a,
    μ (C ⁻¹' {c} ∩ (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})) ≠ 0) :
  P.cde μ m = ∑ c, μ.real (C ⁻¹' {c}) *
    (condMean μ (C ⁻¹' {c} ∩ (P.A ⁻¹' {true} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})) P.Yobs -
      condMean μ (C ⁻¹' {c} ∩ (P.A ⁻¹' {false} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m})) P.Yobs)

Identification of the controlled direct effect with a finite covariate C, under single world assumptions holding within each covariate value c with P(C = c) > 0: treatment ignorability Y a m ⫫ A and mediator ignorability Y a m ⫫ M a given A = a under μ[|C = c], and positivity of the cells C = c, A = a, Mobs = m, for both a. Then CDE(m) = Σ c, P(C = c) (E[Yobs | C = c, A = 1, Mobs = m] - E[Yobs | C = c, A = 0, Mobs = m]).

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nde_eq_sum_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem nde_eq_sum_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {𝓒 : Type*}
  [Fintype 𝓒] [MeasurableSpace 𝓒] [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓒] {a' : Bool} (C : Ω → 𝓒)
  (hC : Measurable C) (hA : Measurable P.A) (hM : ∀ a, Measurable (P.M a))
  (hintD : Integrable (P.nested a' a') μ)
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y (!a') m) μ)
  (hrandD : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.nested a' a') P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hrandY : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hrandM : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.M a') P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hmed : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) (P.M (!a')) μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}][|P.A ⁻¹' {!a'}])
  (hcross : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y (!a') m) (P.M a') μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hposA : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {a'}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M a' ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {!a'} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.nde μ a' = ∑ c, μ.real (C ⁻¹' {c}) *
    (P.mediationFormula μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] true a' - P.mediationFormula μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] false a')

Identification of the natural direct effect NDE(a') with a finite covariate C: NDE(a') = Σ c, P(C = c) (mediationFormula μ[|C = c] 1 a' - mediationFormula μ[|C = c] 0 a'). The global hypotheses are integrability of Y a' (M a') and of every Y (!a') m with P(M a' = m) > 0; for every c with P(C = c) > 0 the hypotheses of nde_eq_mediationFormula hold under μ[|C = c], the mediator conditions being required for the values m with P(M a' = m | C = c) > 0.

CausalInference.Mediation.MediationModel.nie_eq_sum_mediationFormulatheorem

theorem nie_eq_sum_mediationFormula [Fintype 𝓜] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {𝓒 : Type*}
  [Fintype 𝓒] [MeasurableSpace 𝓒] [MeasurableSingletonClass 𝓒] {a : Bool} (C : Ω → 𝓒)
  (hC : Measurable C) (hA : Measurable P.A) (hM : ∀ a', Measurable (P.M a'))
  (hintD : Integrable (P.nested a a) μ)
  (hY : ∀ m, μ (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 → Integrable (P.Y a m) μ)
  (hrandD : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.nested a a) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hposD : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {a}) ≠ 0)
  (hrandY : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hrandM : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → IndepFun (P.M (!a)) P.A μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hmed : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M a) μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}][|P.A ⁻¹' {a}])
  (hcross : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    IndepFun (P.Y a m) (P.M (!a)) μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}])
  (hposA : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {!a}) ≠ 0)
  (hpos : ∀ c, μ (C ⁻¹' {c}) ≠ 0 → ∀ m, μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.M (!a) ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0 →
    μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] (P.A ⁻¹' {a} ∩ P.Mobs ⁻¹' {m}) ≠ 0) :
  P.nie μ a = ∑ c, μ.real (C ⁻¹' {c}) *
    (P.mediationFormula μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] a true - P.mediationFormula μ[|C ⁻¹' {c}] a false)

Identification of the natural indirect effect NIE(a) with a finite covariate C: NIE(a) = Σ c, P(C = c) (mediationFormula μ[|C = c] a 1 - mediationFormula μ[|C = c] a 0). The global hypotheses are integrability of Y a (M a) and of every Y a m with P(M (!a) = m) > 0; for every c with P(C = c) > 0 the hypotheses of nie_eq_mediationFormula hold under μ[|C = c], the mediator conditions being required for the values m with P(M (!a) = m | C = c) > 0.

Missing data mechanisms and weighting.

CausalInference.MissingData.Basic

CausalInference/MissingData/Basic.lean · 251 lines · 13 public theorems · 9 definitions · imports PartialIdentification.IdentifiedSet

Missing data: models, the observed-data projection, observed-data functionals. The basic setting of missing-data theory in the sense of Rubin (1976).

Sources: Rubin (1976); Little and Rubin

CausalInference.MissingData.respInddefinition

def respInd {Ω : Type*} (R : Ω → Bool) : Ω → ℝ

The real indicator of the response event {R = true}: it is 1 where the outcome is observed and 0 where it is missing.

  respInd R ω = if R ω = true then 1 else 0

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModelstructure

structure MissingDataModel (Ω 𝒳 : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω]

A missing-data model on the sample space Ω with covariate space 𝒳: a measure μ, an always observed covariate X, a full-data outcome Y, and a response indicator R (R ω = true means Y ω is observed).

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.observedYdefinition

def observedY (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) : Ω → ℝ

The observed outcome R · Y: the outcome where it is observed and 0 where it is missing.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.observedDatadefinition

def observedData (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) : Ω → 𝒳 × Bool × ℝ

The observed-data projection ω ↦ (X ω, R ω, R ω · Y ω).

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.observedLawdefinition

def observedLaw (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) : Measure (𝒳 × Bool × ℝ)

The observed-data law: the law of (X, R, R · Y) under μ. It is the law of the observed data only when the observed-data projection is almost everywhere measurable, as it is on an admissible model (IsAdmissible). Otherwise Mathlib's Measure.map returns 0 for the zero measure and an arbitrary Dirac mass for a nonzero measure, which carries no information about the model. For example, on a two point probability space with the trivial σ-algebra, constant X and Y and a response indicator that separates the two points, the projection is not almost everywhere measurable.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.fullMeandefinition

def fullMean (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) : ℝ

The full-data mean E[Y], the usual target of a missing-data analysis. It is the expectation of Y only when Y is integrable; otherwise the Bochner integral is 0 by convention. The identification theorems that interpret it assume Integrable M.Y M.μ (on a finite sample space with a finite measure this holds automatically).

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.observedY_of_truetheorem

theorem observedY_of_true (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) {ω : Ω} (h : M.R ω = true) :
  M.observedY ω = M.Y ω

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.IsAdmissiblestructure

structure IsAdmissible (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳) : Prop

A missing-data model is admissible when its measure is a probability measure and X, R and Y are measurable. Then the observed-data projection is measurable (IsAdmissible.measurable_observedData), so the observed-data law is the genuine law of the observed data.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.IsAdmissible.measurable_observedDatatheorem

  Measurable M.observedData

On an admissible model the observed-data projection is measurable.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.IsAdmissible.aemeasurable_observedDatatheorem

  (hM : M.IsAdmissible) : AEMeasurable M.observedData M.μ

On an admissible model the observed-data projection is almost everywhere measurable.

theorem IsAdmissible.isProbabilityMeasure_observedLaw {M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳}
  (hM : M.IsAdmissible) : IsProbabilityMeasure M.observedLaw

On an admissible model the observed-data law is a probability measure.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.observedLaw_eq_of_observedData_eqtheorem

theorem observedLaw_eq_of_observedData_eq {M M' : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳} (hμ : M.μ = M'.μ)
  (h : M.observedData = M'.observedData) : M.observedLaw = M'.observedLaw

Two models whose observed-data projections agree pointwise, on the same measure, have the same observed-data law.

CausalInference.MissingData.completeCaseMeandefinition

def completeCaseMean {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω)
  (R : Ω → Bool) (Y : Ω → ℝ) : ℝ

The complete-case mean E[Y | R = true]: the mean of Y under μ conditioned on the response event. It is the conditional mean only when μ is finite, μ {R = true} ≠ 0 and Y is integrable on the response event; otherwise the conditional measure is 0 or the integral is 0 by convention.

CausalInference.MissingData.IsObservedDataFunctionaldefinition

def IsObservedDataFunctional (S : Set (MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳))
  (θ : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳 → ℝ) : Prop

On the model class S, the real functional θ is a function of the observed-data law: some G on laws of (X, R, R · Y) satisfies θ M = G (law of the observed data of M) for every M ∈ S. The observed-data law is meaningful only on admissible models (MissingDataModel.IsAdmissible), so the classes S used with this predicate in this library consist of admissible models.

CausalInference.MissingData.isObservedDataFunctional_iff_pointIdentifiedtheorem

theorem isObservedDataFunctional_iff_pointIdentified {S : Set (MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳)}
  {θ : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳 → ℝ} :
  IsObservedDataFunctional S θ ↔ PointIdentified S MissingDataModel.observedLaw θ

A functional is a function of the observed-data law on S exactly when it is point identified on S from the observed-data law: models of S with the same observed-data law have the same value.

CausalInference.MissingData.MissingDataModel.completeCaseMean_eq_observedLawtheorem

theorem MissingDataModel.completeCaseMean_eq_observedLaw (M : MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳)
  (hM : M.IsAdmissible) (hpos : M.μ (M.R ⁻¹' {true}) ≠ 0)
  (hint : IntegrableOn M.Y (M.R ⁻¹' {true}) M.μ) :
  completeCaseMean M.μ M.R M.Y =
      ∫ p, p.2.2 ∂M.observedLaw[|{p : 𝒳 × Bool × ℝ | p.2.1 = true}] ∧
    IsProbabilityMeasure M.observedLaw[|{p : 𝒳 × Bool × ℝ | p.2.1 = true}] ∧
    Integrable (fun p : 𝒳 × Bool × ℝ => p.2.2)
      M.observedLaw[|{p : 𝒳 × Bool × ℝ | p.2.1 = true}]

The complete-case mean depends on the model only through the observed-data law: on an admissible model whose response event has positive probability and on which Y is integrable, it equals the mean of the third coordinate under the observed-data law conditioned on R = true. Under the same hypotheses that conditioned law is a probability measure under which the third coordinate is integrable, so both sides are genuine conditional means.

CausalInference.MissingData.isObservedDataFunctional_completeCaseMeantheorem

theorem isObservedDataFunctional_completeCaseMean {S : Set (MissingDataModel Ω 𝒳)}
  (hS : ∀ M ∈ S, M.IsAdmissible ∧ M.μ (M.R ⁻¹' {true}) ≠ 0 ∧
    IntegrableOn M.Y (M.R ⁻¹' {true}) M.μ) :
  IsObservedDataFunctional S (fun M => completeCaseMean M.μ M.R M.Y)

The complete-case mean is a function of the observed-data law on every class of admissible models whose response event has positive probability and on which Y is integrable over the response event.
